# Export Campaign User Reports

Understand how users interact with your campaigns.

Campaign user reports contain details about users who interacted with a campaign in a certain date range. Reports can be exported in two ways:

  * Export from the campaign list
  * Export via [Report API](ref:getting-started-with-the-report-api): Programmatically export reports using the provided API.

![](https://files.readme.io/3f3f50a-Screen_Shot_2022-05-31_at_12.50.51_AM.png)

* * *

## 

Notes and limitations

  * For in-app inbox campaigns, the report only includes data if your app logs the `qg_inapp_displayed` and `qg_inapp_clicked` events using the Appier SDK. Note that these events aren't logged by default.
  * The **Export user report** button is only available for campaigns that meet the following criteria.
    * Campaigns created after May 31, 2022.
    * Campaigns that have run in the past 60 days.
      * It can take up to 10 minutes for the option to become available after a campaign has run, or for message trigger campaigns which have just been toggled on or off.
      * For message trigger campaigns, in-web campaigns, and in-app campaigns, this includes campaigns that have been toggled on. The campaign's scheduled time is not considered.
  * Report data is limited to the past 60 days.



* * *

## 

Export from the campaign list

  1. From the campaign list, click the three vertical dots next to the campaign you'd like to export the user report for.
  2. Click **Export user report**. In the pop-up that appears, specify the date range for the campaign report, then click **Export**.

![](https://files.readme.io/c4dadac57a80857fe7fae9c10522710224daca4a56ef93cd626aead03a3573a0-user-report-export.png)

When the report is ready, an email containing the download link for the report in CSV format will be sent to your account's email address.

* * *

## 

Reading the user report

  * Each row in the sheet represents a user who has been sent this campaign or has interacted with this campaign during the export time range. An interaction can include campaign delivery, impressions, opens, clicks, conversions, and email unsubscription.
  * If the campaign is sent to the user multiple times during the export time range, each campaign sent is a separate row in the report for that user.

![](https://files.readme.io/3fae2c0-Screen_Shot_2022-05-27_at_7.53.26_PM.png)

  * If the user has interacted with the campaign during the export time range, but the sent time is outside of the export time range, the user will be listed in report, but the `Sent Time` field will be empty.

![](https://files.readme.io/9bf14e1-Screen_Shot_2022-05-27_at_5.53.18_PM.png) ![](https://files.readme.io/0a7c092-Screen_Shot_2022-05-27_at_5.53.52_PM.png)

  * A user might complete the same type of interaction multiple times during the export time range, such as multiple clicks or multiple email opens. The report shows the time of the first interaction within the export time range in the following columns: `First Delivered Time`, `First Impression Time`, `First Open Time`, `First Click Time`, `First Conversion Time`.
  * In some scenarios, the first interaction time can be earlier than the campaign sent time.  
In the example below, the user's `First Open Time` is from an email campaign that was sent before the export time range. As a result, the `First Open Time` is earlier than the `Sent Time` in the report.

![](https://files.readme.io/d7333d9-Screen_Shot_2022-05-27_at_6.17.52_PM.png) ![](https://files.readme.io/4f68ac3-Screen_Shot_2022-05-27_at_6.19.08_PM.png)

  * The date and time in the report are based on the timezone set in the acount settings.
  * Conversion-related data is based on the attribution model set in the account settings.



#### 

Limitations

If a LINE user clicks on a link in the LINE campaign that directs to a website integrated with Appier Web SDK, the click will be listed under a separate LINE user in the report.

If the user also completes a conversion after clicking, both the click and the conversion will be listed under the second LINE user as shown in the illustration below. In the example below, you can see two LINE users with the same LINE UID but with different user IDs. The click and the conversion are listed under the second user with an empty `Sent Time` field.

![](https://files.readme.io/1ef2eea-Screen_Shot_2022-05-30_at_3.09.12_PM.png)

* * *

## 

Report columns

The columns included in the report are different based on the campaign type and channel.

The following columns in the report are related to information about the user.

Column name| Campaign type| Channel| Description  
---|---|---|---  
Variants| • Message (regular)  
• In-web  
• In-app| • Email  
• Push  
• In-web  
• In-app| This column is only available if you have enabled the Experiment feature for this campaign.This is the name of the variant that the user was assigned to.  
User ID| • Message • In-web  
• In-app| All| This is the unique ID AIQUA assigns to users. AIQUA stores this ID using the `userId` parameter.  
Customer ID| • Message  
• In-web  
• In-app| All| This is the custom user ID used by your company (e.g. member ID from your CRM system). The data needs to be stored using the parameter name `user_id`.  
Email| Message| Email| This is the user's email address. The data needs to be stored using the parameter name `email`.  
Phone No| Message| • SMS  
  
• LINE  
• Kakao| This is the user's phone number. The data needs to be stored using the parameter name `phoneNo`.  
LINE UID| Message| LINE| This is the user's LINE UID.  
IDFA| • Message  
• In-web  
• In-app| • Push (iOS)  
  
• In-app (iOS)| This is the Identifier for Advertisers of the user's iOS device.  
AAID| • Message  
• In-web  
• In-app| • Push (Android)  
  
• In-app (Android)| This is the Android Advertising ID of the user's Android device.  
  
The following columns in the report are related to campaign delivery and performance.

# Export Email Click Report

Understand link engagement in your email campaigns.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Contact your customer success manager to enable this feature.

Track link engagement in your email campaigns to understand which links were clicked and how often. Reports are exported as CSV files and delivered via email.

* * *

## 

Notes and limitations

  * Click data is available only for campaigns sent on or after December 25, 2025.
  * The **Export click report** button is only available for campaigns that meet the following criteria.
    * Campaigns sent on or after December 25, 2025.
    * Campaigns sent within the past 60 days.
  * Report data is limited to the past 60 days.
  * Download links expire after one week.
  * A maximum of 50 links per email are tracked. Links beyond this limit aren't tracked.
  * For emails created in the [HTML Editor](doc:creatives-email-html-editor), only links that meet these criteria are tracked:
    * Links within `<a href>` tags.
    * Links that start with `http://` or `https://`.
    * Links or references outside these specific tags are not tracked.
  * Dynamic links aren't supported. If your email uses dynamic links, each unique URL generated by that dynamic link appears as a separate row in the report.



* * *

## 

Export from the campaign list

You can export click reports for [email](doc:campaigns-regular-create-email) message campaigns.

From the campaign list, click the three vertical dots next to the campaign you'd like to export the click report for, then click **Export click report**.

![](https://files.readme.io/69c8a9c664454ea3178632c5daba1ff730fc5a5ec3c38ffe0b7049b1c3dc3649-email-export-click-report.png)

When the report is ready, an email containing the download link for the report in CSV format will be sent to your account's email address.

* * *

## 

Report columns

The exported CSV file contains the following columns:

Column| Description  
---|---  
Link URL| The specific URL clicked.  
Total clicks| The total number of times the link was clicked during the reporting period.  
Campaign ID| The unique identifier for the campaign.  
Variant| The [experiment](doc:campaigns-experiments-message) creative variant where the click occurred. This field is blank if no variant exists.  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/69f4aef9b6c26199e43c24d1b4d3d798e194d54cb6ceb545ca3bd8bd10e5d835-click-report-file.png)

# Campaign Performance Page

View detailed performance for a campaign.

To open an individual campaign's performance page, go to the campaign list and click the campaign's name.

> 👍
> 
> You can edit the metric settings and date range to customize the performance data range and calculations.

From the **Performance** tab, you can view overall campaign performance metrics. For campaigns with experiments enabled, go to the **Experiment analysis** tab to view performance for each variant.

![](https://files.readme.io/a3f990dc50ea638afd7db3637cd52bf92ccd0f3696dd0e1e48e46e03ed750a59-campaign-performance-page-performance-tabs.png)

* * *

## 

Metric settings and date range

Set the date range for data displayed in the performance page and metric settings to determine how performance data is calculated.

![](https://files.readme.io/00afc1db639e27f0076b987275810e475b6282ec7e4d5e9d0a313401893a18e2-campaign-performance-page-settings.png)

Metric setting| Description  
---|---  
**Event count**|  • **Total event** : Each event is counted once.  
• **Unique event** : If a user completes the same event multiple times, the event is only counted once. The number of unique events is an approximation with a < 1% margin of error. Unique event count is not supported for offline events.  
**Online attribution model**|  Select the attribution model for online events, that is, events logged via Appier SDK. The online conversions and attributed event data on this page will be based on this attribution rule.  
**Offline attribution model**|  Select the attribution model for offline events uploaded via API. The offline conversions on this page will be based on this attribution rule.  
  
  


> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * The attribution model and event count settings in the campaign performance page don't affect campaign reports or the metrics in the campaign list. See [Attribution Settings](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution-setting-attribution#setting-attribution-model) for details.
>   * For campaigns created before February 2021, the online event count calculated using unique events is only available if the last-view & last-click attribution model is selected.
> 


* * *

## 

Performance

View the campaign's performance metrics and performance trend. The following charts are available:

  * Performance overview
  * Performance trend



### 

Performance overview

#### 

Message campaigns

The following table provides metric definitions used to calculate data in the performance overview.

Metric| Channels| Description  
---|---|---  
Delivered| • Email  
•SMS/MMS  
• Kakao| The number of times the campaign is successfully delivered by the message delivery provides, for example, the SMS or email service provider (`notification_delivered` events).  
Sent| All channels| The total number of campaign messages sent by AIQUA (`notification_sent` events).Only available for campaigns created after April 18, 2023 (00:00 UTC).  
Opens| Email| The number of times the email was opened (`qg_email_opened` events).  
Impressions| Push| The number of users who received the push notification on their devices (`notification_received` events).  
Clicks| All channels| The number of times users clicked on an URL in the campaign.• Push (Android): The number of clicks on the notification or customized buttons (`notification_clicked` and `actionClicked` events).• Push (Web and iOS): The number of clicks on the notification (`notification_clicked` events).• Email: The number clicks on a URL in the email (`notification_clicked` events).• SMS/MMS: The number of clicks on [AIQUA short URLs](doc:creatives-sms-mms#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url) (`notification_clicked` events).• LINE: The number of times users clicked on any valid links in carousel or rich message creative that directs the user to a web page or app embedded with Appier SDK (iOS SDK 7.20.0 or later, Android SDK 7.12.0 or later). Click data is not available for [non-AIQUA shortened URLs](doc:how-do-i-track-clicks-with-shortened-url).• Kakao: The number of clicks on [AIQUA short URLs](doc:campaigns-message-create-kakao#add-an-aiqua-short-url) (`notification_clicked` events).  
Conversions| All channels| The number of online conversion events or goal events logged via Appier SDK that happen after the users interact with the campaign based on the configured attribution model, attribution window, and the conversion events.Click and click attribution data is not available for [non-AIQUA shortened URLs](doc:how-do-i-track-clicks-with-shortened-url).  
Offline conversions| All channels| The number of offline conversion events uploaded via [API](ref:getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2) that happen after the users interact with the campaign based on the attribution model, attribution window, and the conversion events you have set.• Must be enabled by Appier Support.• AIQUA calculates the offline conversion count once a day using offline events with a timestamp within 90 days.• For a list of channels that support offline conversion attribution, see [Attribution models by channels](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution#attribution-models-by-channel).  
Unsubscribed| Email| The number of clicks on [email unsubscription links](doc:creatives-email-drag-and-drop-editor#add-unsubscription-links).  
  
#### 

In-web campaigns

Metrics| Description| Events  
---|---|---  
Impressions| The number of times the campaign is shown on the website.The impression count for the control group in experiment campaigns is not included.| `qg_inweb_displayed`  
Clicks| 

  * **Subscription boost** : The number of times users click to allow push notifications.
  * **Fixed banner** : The number clicks on the action button.
  * **Multiple images** : The number of clicks on an image or action button.
  * **Multiple actions** : The number of clicks on an action button where the button's **Click action** is set to**Open URL**.
  * **Lead generation** : The number of lead generation form submissions.
  * **Creative Studio** : The number of clicks on a creative element with the **Action** set to **URL** or **Submit form**.

| `qg_inweb_clicked`  
`qg_inweb_lead_gen`  
Submissions| 

  * **Lead Generation** : The number of lead generation form submissions.
  * **Creative Studio** : The number times users submit a form by clicking on a creative element where the element's "Action" is set to**Submit form**.

| `qg_inweb_lead_gen`  
Conversions| The number of online conversion events or goal events logged via Appier SDK that happen after the users interact with the campaign based on the configured attribution model, attribution window, and the conversion events.|   
Offline conversions| The number of offline conversion events uploaded via [API](ref:getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2) that happen after the users interact with the campaign based on the attribution model, attribution window, and the conversion events you have set.• Must be enabled by Appier Support.• AIQUA calculates the offline conversion count once a day using offline events with a timestamp within 90 days.• For a list of channels that support offline conversion attribution, see [Attribution models by channels](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution#attribution-models-by-channel).|   
  
#### 

In-app campaigns

  * **In-app pop-up campaigns** : Performance data is automatically tracked by the SDK.
  * **In-app inbox campaigns** : Performance data is only available if you manually log inbox notification events using the Appier SDK methods ([iOS](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-ios#logging-events-for-a-particular-inbox-message), [Android](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-android#logging-events-for-inbox-campaign-notifications)).



Metrics| Description| Events  
---|---|---  
Impressions| The number of times the campaign is shown on the app.For campaigns with experiments, the impression for the control group aren't included.| `qg_inapp_displayed`  
Clicks| When the users click on any valid links in the creative.When the users submit a form by clicking on a creative element in Creative Studio where the element's **Action** is set to **Submit form**.| `qg_inapp_clicked`  
`qg_inapp_lead_gen`  
Submissions| Available for Creative Studio only. When the users submit a form by clicking on a creative element where the element's **Action** is set to **Submit form**.| `qg_inapp_lead_gen`  
Conversions| The number of online conversion events or goal events logged via Appier SDK that happen after the users interact with the campaign based on the configured attribution model, attribution window, and the conversion events.|   
Offline conversions| The number of offline conversion events uploaded via [API](ref:getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2) that happen after the users interact with the campaign based on the attribution model, attribution window, and the conversion events you have set.• Must be enabled by Appier Support.• AIQUA calculates the offline conversion count once a day using offline events with a timestamp within 90 days.• For a list of channels that support offline conversion attribution, see [Attribution models by channels](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution#attribution-models-by-channel).|

## 

Attribution

![](https://files.readme.io/7bea63be420a4a44c97bbd25931e959188b2dcf148bf9ea5c952a0a8e0750bc5-performance-attribution.png)

Metrics| Definition  
---|---  
Attributed events| This is the number of events attributed to the campaign, based on the attribution model and attribution window you have set.Attributed events highlighted in bold are the conversion events you have selected.Some system events such as `notification_received` are excluded and do not count toward Attributed Events.Click **View details** to see the event count for each attributed event.  
Attributed value| If attributed events contain `valueToSum` to track the monetary value associated with the event, the total value attributed to the campaign will be displayed here.Click **View details** to see the attributed value for each attributed event.  
  
* * *

## 

Experiment analysis

Go to the **Experiment analysis** tab to view performance data for [experiment](doc:campaigns-experiments) campaigns. The following charts are available:

  * Performance analysis
  * Performance trend



### 

Performance analysis

View metrics for each variant in an experiment campaign. Note that for campaign experiments using **Winner distribution** , the report only includes data collected during the test duration.

![](https://files.readme.io/2072ff0fa8480881939c079a7407e1ba0bb4f2a5d9e031ae54ed3a71d57b04df-experiment-performance-analysis.png)

In addition to the metrics listed above, **CVR lift** is available experiments with a control group.

Metric| Definition| Campaign types  
---|---|---  
CVR lift| The increase in conversion rate. Calculated using: Target conversion rate from (all variants) / Target conversion rate from control group - 1.| In-web and in-app (pop-up): Experiments with control group  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * For the control group, an impression is counted when the user meets the trigger rule of the campaign.
>   * When **Event count** is set to **Unique events** , the number of unique events is an approximation with a < 1% margin of error.
> 


* * *

## 

Performance trend

  * Select the metric to analyze from the dropdown menu on the left.
  * To view exact details for a specific date, hover over that date in the chart.
  * You choose to display counts by **Daily** and **Weekly** totals.

![](https://files.readme.io/117e4b1fbb75a61260a44287e389ec4ee5212e73f1859a1d6b74e8b75407ed41-performance-trend.png)

# Understanding Event Attribution

Attribution determines how to give credit to campaigns when users complete events. Use attribution to evaluate how effective your campaigns are. For example, you can determine how effective a campaign is by seeing how many product purchases or sign-ups occur after users view the campaign.

![](https://files.readme.io/374e4bee13c44527c8d8ccdc5978ca9f7244298f400cd88af21be259986f4e18-attributed-events.png)

You can also define conversion events, such as `product_purchased` or `registration_completed`, to track conversion-related performance metrics.

![](https://files.readme.io/bc53a7798933c20741aa01936aa820353609ce6b7e92b003f65ab6d037d13d50-campaign-performance-page-conversion-metrics.png)

* * *

## 

How does AIQUA attribute events to campaigns?

Two conditions must be satisfied for an event to be attributed to a campaign:

  1. **The user must click or view the campaign before completing the event.** AIQUA provides different attribution models to let you control when events are attributed to a campaign. See [Setting attribution models](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution-setting-attribution#setting-the-attribution-model) for configuration details.
  2. **After the user clicks or views the campaign, the event must occur within theattribution window.** The default attribution window is 24 hours for click-through attribution and 1 hour for view-through attribution for online events collected via Appier SDK. See [Setting the attribution window](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution-setting-attribution#setting-the-attribution-window) for configuration details.



For a conversion to be attributed to a campaign, you need to [set conversion events](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution-setting-attribution#setting-conversion-events). If the user completes the conversion event and satisfies both attribution conditions, that conversion will be attributed to the campaign.

* * *

## 

Supported event types and channels

### 

Supported event types

AIQUA supports the following types of events for event attribution.

Event type| Description  
---|---  
Online events (logged via [Appier SDK](doc:sdk-getting-started))| All events, except campaign-related default events such as `notification_clicked`, `qg_inapp_received`, and `qg_inweb_closed`, count as attributed events.  
Offline events  
(Uploaded via [Offline Event API v2](ref:reference/getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2))| Only offline conversion events you selected in [account settings](doc:user-settings#offline-conversion-and-attribution) can be attributed to campaigns.  
  
### 

Supported attribution models by channel

Refer to the table below for the attribution models supported by different channels. Note that attribution window settings are shared for web push, in-web, email, and LINE.

Channel| Online event attribution| Offline event attribution  
---|---|---  
Push (web and app)| • Last-view model  
• Last-click model  
• Last-view & last-click model| • Last-view model  
• Last-click model  
• Last-view & last-click model  
• Click model  
• View model  
Email| Last-click model| • Last-view model  
• Last-click model  
• Last-view & last-click model  
• Click model  
• View model  
LINE| Last-click model| • Last-click model  
• Click model  
SMS, Kakao| Last-click modelNote: Click-based attribution is only supported for campaigns containing an AIQUA short URL ([SMS](doc:creatives-sms-mms#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url), [Kakao (ChinguTalk)](doc:creatives-kakao-chingutalk#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url)).| • Last-click model  
• Click model  
MMS| N/A| N/A  
In-web| • Last-view model   
• Last-click model  
• Last-view & last-click model  
• Click model (Beta)  
• View model (Beta)| N/A  
In-app| • Last-view model   
• Last-click model  
• Last-view & last-click model| N/A  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Shortened URLs
> 
>   * To track clicks for SMS and Kakao campaigns, you can add an AIQUA short URL to your [SMS](doc:creatives-sms-mms#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url) or [Kakao](doc:tracking-clicks-for-kakao-campaigns) campaign creative.
>   * If you're creating your own shortened URLs instead of using an AIQUA short URL, clicks and click-based attributions will not be tracked. To work around this limitation, see [how to track clicks and attribution with shortened URLs](doc:how-do-i-track-clicks-with-shortened-url).
> 


* * *

## 

Understanding attribution models

AIQUA supports the following attribution models.

Attribution model| Description  
---|---  
**Last-Click**|  An event is attributed to the campaign last clicked by the user within the attribution window.  
**Last-View**|  An event is attributed to the campaign last viewed by the user within the attribution window.  
**Last-View + Last-Click**|  An event is attributed to the campaign last viewed and the campaign last clicked by the user within the attribution window.  
**Click** (Beta)| An event is attributed to all campaigns the user clicked within the attribution window.Note that this model is a beta feature and is only supported for in-web campaigns. To enable this model, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#214452527e525451514e5355614051514844530f424e4c)).  
**View** (Beta)| An event is attributed to all campaigns the user viewed within the attribution window.Note that this model is a beta feature and is only supported for in-web campaigns. To enable this model, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#2e4b5d5d715d5b5e5e415c5a6e4f5e5e474b5c004d4143)).  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Performance data for in-web campaigns is available starting from the following dates:
> 
>   * **Click** , **View** model: Data related to attribution and conversion is available from February 15, 2022.
>   * **Last-Click** , **Last-View** , **Last-View + Last-Click** model: Performance data is available from January 1, 2021 if the **Click** and **View** model are enabled.
> 


### 

Last-Click model

Under the **Last-Click** model, if the user clicks on multiple AIQUA campaigns before completing the events, the events will be attributed to the campaign the user last clicked on, as long as the events happen within the attribution window.

In the example below, if you have selected the **Last-Click** model, the `added_to_cart` and `checkout_completed` events will be attributed to Campaign B.

![](https://files.readme.io/bbea880-Screen_Shot_2022-02-14_at_12.51.47_PM.png)

### 

Last-View model

Under the **Last-View** model, if the user views multiple AIQUA campaigns before completing the events, the events will be attributed to the campaign the user last viewed, as long as the events happen within the attribution window.

In the example below, if you have selected the **Last-View** model, the `added_to_cart` and `checkout_completed` events will be attributed to Campaign C.

![](https://files.readme.io/dd075e3-Screen_Shot_2022-02-14_at_12.59.34_PM.png)

### 

Last-View + Last-Click model

Under the **Last-View + Last-Click** model, both clicks and views can count toward Attributed Events, but if the last-click campaign and the last-view campaign are the same campaign, the same event will only be counted as an attributed event once (not double-counted).

In the example below, Campaign A is the last-view and last-click campaign before the user added a product to the cart. The `added_to_cart` event will only be attributed to Campaign A once.

![](https://files.readme.io/fc34b3f-Screen_Shot_2022-02-14_at_12.55.09_PM.png)

If the last-click campaign and last-view campaign are different campaigns, the same event will be separately attributed once to each campaign.

For example, if the last-click campaign is Campaign A and the last-view campaign is Campaign B, the `added_to_cart` event will be attributed to campaign A once and then to campaign B once.

![](https://files.readme.io/6ed9623-Screen_Shot_2022-02-14_at_12.55.24_PM.png)

### 

Click model

With the **Click** model, if the user clicks on AIQUA campaigns before completing the events, the events will be attributed to all campaigns the user clicked on within the attribution window.

In the example below, if you have selected the **Click** model, the `added_to_cart` and `checkout_completed` events will be attributed to both Campaign A and Campaign B.

![](https://files.readme.io/b46d5cf-Screen_Shot_2022-02-14_at_12.52.15_PM.png)

### 

View model

With the **View** model, if the user views AIQUA campaigns before completing the events, the events will be attributed to all campaigns the user viewed within the attribution window.

In the example below, if you have selected the **View** model, the `added_to_cart` and `checkout_completed` events will be attributed to both Campaign B and Campaign C.

![](https://files.readme.io/1f2619c-Screen_Shot_2022-02-14_at_4.11.23_PM.png)

* * *

## 

Understanding attribution windows

For an event to be attributed to a campaign, the user needs to complete the event within a certain time period after viewing or clicking the campaign. In the following example:

  * The click-through attribution window is 24 hours.
  * The view-through attribution window is 1 hour.



The `checkout_completed` event is only attributed to Campaign A because the user completed the event within the 24-hour click-through attribution window. Since the event happened more than one hour after the user views Campaign B, it is not attributed to Campaign B.

![](https://files.readme.io/10308a6-Screen_Shot_2022-02-16_at_6.59.09_PM.png)

# Attribution Settings

  * Setting the attribution model
  * Setting the attribution window
  * Setting conversion events



* * *

## 

Setting the attribution model

You can adjust the attribution model for online events and offline events in two places:

  1. Account settings page
  2. Campaign performance page



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported models and limitations
> 
> For details about the attribution models supported for each channel, see [Understanding Event Attribution](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution#understanding-attribution-models).

### 

Account settings page

In the [account settings](doc:user-settings#conversion-and-attribution) page, you can set the attribution model and conversion events for online events (collected via Appier SDK) and offline events (uploaded via API).

  * Online events: Go to the **Conversion and attribution** section.
  * Offline events: Go to the **Offline conversion and attribution** section.



The attribution models selected in your account settings impact metrics found in:

  * The campaign list.
  * Campaign reports downloaded from the campaign list.
  * Campaign reports downloaded using the [Campaign Report API](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/getting-started-with-the-report-api#campaign-performance-report).

![Campaign List](https://files.readme.io/8e2550414153ad194e53dd8285a42c91ec4565edb6f4555dd9395012b512025d-attribution-settings-campaign-list.png)   


> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Changing the attribution model
> 
> If another team member changes the app's attribution model settings while you're using AIQUA, the new settings are only reflected in the campaign list after you:
> 
>   * Reload the AIQUA dashboard.
>   * Visit the account settings page.
> 


### 

Campaign performance page

On the campaign performance page for an individual campaign, you can click **Metric settings** to change how events count and attribution model settings. Note that the selected metric settings only affect performance metrics shown on this page.

![](https://files.readme.io/2f4c22c3818c88f145b35d18136548e99ca5412d8fe98bbac584a06a099afa62-campaign-performance-page-metric-settings.png)

* * *

## 

Setting the attribution window

  * Setting the attribution window for online events
  * Setting the attribution window for offline events



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Shared attribution window settings
> 
> The following channels share the same attribution window settings:
> 
>   * Web push
>   * In-web
>   * Email
>   * LINE
> 


### 

Setting the attribution window for online events

  * The maximum attribution window size is 30 days.
  * Changes to attribution window settings will only be applied to campaigns sent after the change was saved.



Channel type| Default window| Modifying the window  
---|---|---  
Web push, in-web| Click-through: 24 hours  
View-through: 1 hour| Contact Appier Support  
LINE, email| Click-through: 24 hours| Contact Appier Support  
SMS| Click-through: 24 hours  
View-through: Not supported  
Click-through attribution is only supported for SMS campaigns containing an [AIQUA short URL](doc:creatives-sms-mms#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url).| Contact Appier Support  
Kakao| Click-through: 24 hours  
View-through: Not supported  
Click-through attribution is supported for Kakao campaigns containing an [AIQUA short URL](doc:creatives-kakao-chingutalk#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url).| Contact Appier Support  
Android push, Android in-app| Click-through: 24 hours  
View-through: 1 hour| [Use the Android SDK](doc:event-attribution-android-sdk#attribution-windows)  
iOS push, iOS in-app| Click-through: 24 hours  
View-through: 1 hours| [Use the iOS SDK](doc:event-attribution-ios-sdk)  
  
### 

Setting the attribution window for offline events

  * The attribution window can be between 1 and 30 days.
  * The same attribution window is applied for both view-through and click-through attribution.
  * If you change the attribution window, the new window is only applied to offline events uploaded after the change.



To set the attribution window for offline event attribution, go to **Account settings** , then go to **Offline conversion and attribution > Attribution window**.

* * *

## 

Setting conversion events

  * Setting online conversion events
  * Setting offline conversion events



### 

Setting online conversion events

Conversion event type| Scope| Instructions| Notes  
---|---|---|---  
Conversion events| Account-level| 

  1. Go to the **Account settings** page.
  2. Under **Conversion and Attribution > Conversion events**, select the desired events from the dropdown.

| 

  * Conversion-related metrics are calculated based on the selected conversion events.
  * In the attributed event list, the conversion events are shown in bold.

  
Goal events| Campaign-level| When creating a message campaign, go to the **Settings** step and enable **Set campaign goals**.| 

  * Conversion-related metrics are calculated based on goal events set in the campaign settings rather than conversion events set in the account settings.
  * In the attributed event list, goal events are shown in bold instead of the conversion events.

  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Modifying conversion events
> 
> After modifying conversion events, the new settings are applied to conversion-related metrics immediately.

### 

Setting offline conversion events

To set conversion events for offline data uploaded using the [Offline Event API v2](ref:getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2):

  1. Go to **Account settings**.
  2. Under **Offline conversion and attribution > Conversion events**, select up to five events from the dropdown.

# Performance and Reports

For campaigns created with Creative Studio, you can view the interaction report and download the submitted form data.

## 

View interaction reports

To view the interaction report, navigate to the campaign list, click on the campaign's name to open its performance page, and then click **Interaction report**.

![](https://files.readme.io/ac50a5075920bc782a16ea4840575b227f921e4c832012900da929c1ec46057d-CS-interaction-report.png)

In the interaction report, you will see the metrics of each creative view.

![](https://files.readme.io/4620a18-Screen_Shot_2021-09-15_at_4.19.41_PM.png)

The metrics are calculated based on **unique sessions**. This is different from how metrics are calculated in the rest of the campaign performance page and in downloaded reports.

For in-web campaigns created with Creative Studio, a unique session is defined as below.

  * A session starts when a user triggers an in-web campaign.
  * A session ends when the user does not perform any actions on your website for over 30 minutes.
  * Actions taken by the same user in the same browser tab are counted once per session.



For in-app campaigns created with Creative Studio, a unique session is defined as below.

  * A session starts when a user triggers an in-app campaign.
  * The session expires when:
    * The user does not perform any actions inside the in-app campaign for over 30 minutes.
    * The in-app campaign is closed or a new in-app campaign is triggered.
  * Repeated actions taken by the same user inside the in-app campaign are only counted once during the same session.



In addition:

  * **Overall usage** shows interaction data for the specified time period.
  * **Actions taken** shows interaction data for the selected version during the specified time period.



* * *

## 

Download form data

For campaigns that include **Submit form** actions, such as a lead generation form or a survey, you can download the form data submitted by the users.

![](https://files.readme.io/9adc5ef918216c14906815513dac8723cb067b356c76dc37ad076508da751469-CS-export-form-data.png)

To download form data, navigate to the campaign list, click the menu icon of the campaign, and select **Export form data**. You will need to select a date range and click the **Export** button. The download link will be sent to the email address associated with your login account.

![](https://files.readme.io/8c3c728d2670aa54a2a2ed7fb9f0d22fd3f762786e001b08bce23ec3276ec15f-CS-export-.png)

Here's an example of the downloaded form data.

![](https://files.readme.io/bedac52-Screen_Shot_2021-09-22_at_5.23.38_PM.png)

# Default Templates

Creative Studio offers a variety of prebuilt templates to simplify your campaign creation process. Each template is tailored to different use cases, allowing you to quickly design personalized and engaging creatives for your users without starting from scratch.

Below is an introduction to each template category with an example of how to customize the template:

  * Recommendation
  * Slider surveys
  * Lucky wheel
  * Limited-time sales
  * Story
  * Promotions



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tips
> 
> Before applying creatives to your promotional campaign, ensure all relevant configurations are valid, and use the **[Preview](doc:designing-creatives#4-preview-creatives-across-devices)** button to review your creatives for a seamless user experience.

> 
> To learn how AIQUA's Recommendation 2.0 can boost user engagement, see [Recommendation 2.0](doc:recommendations-v2).

The recommendation template is ideal for personalized product suggestions in your campaigns. In this guide, we'll use the **Multi-tab recommendation (Desktop)** as an example to demonstrate how to customize the settings in Creative Studio to meet your campaign requirements.

  1. To get started with a recommendation template, first obtain a **Scenario ID** from your Recommendation scenario. For more details, see [how to display recommendations in campaign creatives](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#display-recommendations-in-campaign-creatives).

  2. Choose **Multi-tab Recommendation (Desktop)** from the Creative Studio template list.

  3. In the top left, click the template's name and select **Variables and formulas** :

     * Configure the key fields, such as
       * `scenario_id`
       * `currency`
       * `title_length_limit`
       * `product_number`: The number of products to display. Set to a fixed system value of `15.` The number of displayed products won't change even if you edit the field's value. To change the value of `product_number`, contact your customer success manager.
     * Fallback values: Set the following values to ensure the recommendation campaign continues to work normally if any primary data is missing.
       * `category` for the category name shown at the top.
       * `title` for the product title.
       * `price`
       * `rec_url_item` for the image URL.
       * `click_url_1` to `click_url_15` for the product page URL.

![](https://files.readme.io/d7b693a9105bba5141881ec44cbee46b805162ff659cb5fa5c31bbf84bc2b7ad-Variables_and_formulas_-_recommendation.png)

  4. Update the text and URL for the "Check website" button. For more information on modifying elements and optimizing designs, see [Designing Creatives](doc:designing-creatives).
  5. Once your modifications are complete, save and apply the template to your campaign to display personalized product recommendations based on your configurations.



* * *

## 

Slider surveys

![](https://files.readme.io/7d57902f2af93c589460190daeee855773a29c78828ca86d5d602f9314a60f68-slider_survey.png)

Use the slider surveys template to engage users through interactive surveys, and leverage their responses for targeted segmentation.

We'll use the **Emoji Slider - 4 products** as an example to demonstrate how to customize the settings in Creative Studio to align with your product information and segment users based on their responses.

  1. Choose **Emoji Slider - 4 products** from the template list.

  2. In the top left, click the template's name and select **Variables and formulas**. Update product names in the **Value** column.


![](https://files.readme.io/58320982f519c3c0c977562359d951dd9315657b8800c7e54c4bb64c55d73cfd-Variables_and_formulas_-_slider_survey.png)

  3. Customize the text and image elements to fit your campaign's needs. See [Creative Elements](doc:creative-elements) to learn more about how elements can be customized.
  4. Save and apply the survey to your campaign. You'll be able to gather feedback and create segments based on user preferences.



#### 

Survey results

The system automatically adds survey results to the user segment. To create a segment based on survey responses, navigate to the **Audience > Create segment** and click **[Segment by Condition](doc:segments-create-conditions)**.

  * For the template **Emoji Slider - 1 product** , set the attribute as `preference_for_[productName]` and the value can be one of the 4 satisfaction levels based on your creative.

![](https://files.readme.io/21acd125e25425e0d74e939c7a198b78938f3ddfe0c7a62e7c950cb4ebf10512-Emoji-slider-1.png)

  * For template **Emoji Slider - 4 products** , set the attribute as `PreferenceProduct` and the value can be one of the 4 products based on your creative.

![](https://files.readme.io/2b985f9104959abe4cd96fcc2e56b0c9233a9d71a7f47bb89f18056021c7d6c5-Emoji-slider-4.png)

Survey results may take several minutes to appear in the segment after users completed the surveys.

* * *

## 

Lucky wheel

![](https://files.readme.io/e5dd12e85ab96f62d586d25c9761fe56ae1c28c79ef6f1f54a8ffe96288be567-Frame_2.png)

Drives engagement with fun, reward-based interactions with the Lucky wheel template. We'll use the **Lucky Wheel (Desktop)** as an example to demonstrate how to customize the template, so users can spin the wheel for a chance to win prizes or offers.

  1. Choose **Lucky Wheel (Desktop)** from the template list.

  2. Customize the following settings:

     * **Styles** tab: Adjust your wheel appearance styles to match your brand and campaign.
     * **[Settings](doc:creative-elements#wheel-of-fortune)** tab: Set the spin duration and the number of wheel sections to complete your design.
     * **Actions** tab: Set the **Check** and **Action** conditions to configure outcomes based on the spinner result.
     * Example for setting **Actions** for a "You win!":
       * Select **\+ Check** , choose **Spinner result** from the first dropdown menu, then select the section that corresponds with the desired outcome, such as "You win," from the second dropdown menu to trigger actions for that specific result.
       * In the **Actions** tab, select **Change view** to display a message like "Congratulations! You won the prize!".
![](https://files.readme.io/9138d57215e7d474259c6abbaa921652987e1e704a692fa193bd6c5fd24728a0-Lucky_wheel_Actions.png)
  3. After customizing the template, save and apply the template to your campaign. Users can then spin the wheel, and actions will execute based on the spinner result.




* * *

## 

Limited-time sales

![](https://files.readme.io/7e8497bc45fc52acf6ff09cdbb84040ba746bb58750687fac6f861480d287d1a-image.png)

Use the limited-time sales template with a countdown timer to create time-sensitive promotions that encourage quick purchase decisions.

We'll use the **Countdown Timer Blue (Mobile)** as an example to demonstrate how to customize the settings in Creative Studio to encourage a quicker purchase.

  1. Choose **Countdown Timer Blue (Mobile)** from the template list.

  2. In the top left, click the template's name and select **Variables and formulas**.

     * Set the `end_date_time` to specify countdown end date and time.
     * Set `timezone_UTC` to define the time zone in UTC.
![](https://files.readme.io/945b9cfc35a4009c60d809e296aac287974d1dd1db89fb81affd67b973b22c89-Variables_and_formulas-Countdown.png)
  3. Update the text and URL for the "Shop now" button. For more information about modifying elements and optimizing designs, see [Designing Creatives](doc:designing-creatives).

  4. Save and apply the template to your campaign.




* * *

## 

Story

![](https://files.readme.io/c9cc7602acb409261ad1ca17ed985c600def6ae1c9d0005271f22fc8ffb1c610-image.png)

Use the story template to showcase multiple products or highlights in an engaging sequence. Similar to social media stories, you can effectively combine images with calls-to-action.

We'll use the **Story - Promote Products** as an example to demonstrate how to customize the settings in Creative Studio, highlighting product features and driving engagement through linked views.

  1. Choose **Story - Promote Products** from the template list.
  2. Configure the main view (View 0).
     * Upload preview images. Click on the circle to access the **Settings** tab.
     * Under the **Actions** tab, set the destination URL and link to the story view.
     * Repeat these steps to set up the remaining story images and **Actions**.

![](https://files.readme.io/eceae3a28d0a70cb0cf375f01bbb6a8d9666dfbd8a885101a6977233b71294c0-Story-View-0.png)

  3. Configure Views 1 through 5 to customize each individual product you want to feature.
     * Select the view you’re customizing and click the image and upload the product image on the **Settings** tab.
     * Update the text and URL for the "Check product details" button. For more information on modifying elements and optimizing designs, see [Designing Creatives](doc:designing-creatives).
     * Repeat steps above for all views to feature each product in sequence.

![](https://files.readme.io/cd2c4fd04622c5644e67f15eb056ff71acbc8a8c5060447f66e914e300cf9773-Story-View1-View5.png)

  4. Save and apply the template to your campaign.



* * *

## 

Promotions

![](https://files.readme.io/4a9c85f560d26002bf6b789974dc90dfa07a53df1042160985fcbccb86d89009-image.png)

Use the promotions template to create coupon-based campaigns with promo codes, discounts, or special deals to drive conversions.

We'll use the **Coupon Code (Brown)** as an example to demonstrate how to customize the settings in Creative Studio and simplify promotional campaigns using unique coupon codes.

  1. Choose **Coupon Code (Brown)** from the template list.
  2. In the top left, click the template's name and select **Variables and formulas**. Set the `coupon` variable with your coupon code to make it easily accessible for users.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Check the coupon code's validity and redemption settings before launching the campaign.

![](https://files.readme.io/dfbd520d2cde1556581489006c57d23307e13d297cc16682587400addaec7c33-Variables_and_formulas-Promotions.png)

  3. Update the text and URL for the "Copy & shop" button. For more information on modifying elements and optimizing designs, see [Designing Creatives](doc:designing-creatives).
  4. Customize the text and image elements to fit your campaign's needs. For more information, see [Creative Elements](doc:creative-elements) to learn more about how elements can be customized.
  5. Save and apply the template to your campaign.

# Product Data Feed Onboarding

A product data feed is a spreadsheet file that lists all your products along with various product information such as product title, description, link, price, inventory availability, and more. You will need to prepare a data feed file and then host the file on your server.

Integrating product data feed allows you to utilize the following functions of AIQUA:

  * [Recommendation 2.0](doc:recommendations-v2)
  * [Use product data feed information in dynamic content](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives#using-product-information-from-datafeed-as-parameter)
  * [Trigger campaign based on changes in product data feed](doc:campaigns-trigger-create#based-on-feed-changes)

![](https://files.readme.io/808e014-Screen_Shot_2020-06-30_at_3.21.04_PM.png)

* * *

## 

1\. Preparing the data feed file

### 

File format and encoding

  * File format: AIQUA supports CSV, JSON, and XML formats.
  * File encoding: The supported encoding is UTF-8 without BOM. Do not use UTF-8 BOM or other encodings.
  * Multiple files: In case you have multiple product feed files, for example, one for production environment and the other for testing environment, you will need to provide separate data feed files.



### 

Data specifications

Refer to the table below for the fields to include in the data feed file and follow the guidelines below.

  * **Field names**
    * It is highly recommended to use the field names listed below in your data feed file. However, if the field names of your data feed file do not match the field names in the table, you can have Appier Support map your fields to the field names used in Appier's system.
    * Make sure you do not change the field names in the data feed after you provide the data feed to Appier.
    * The field names in the data feed are case-sensitive.
    * Do not use non-alphabetical characters in field names.
  * **Escaping commas and double-quotes**
    * Fields with embedded commas or double-quote characters must be enclosed in double-quotes. Example: `Extra Virgin Olive Oil,ID002173,"Organic and natural, cold-pressed, 500ml"`
    * If double-quotes are used to enclose fields, then a double-quote appearing inside a field must be escaped by preceding it with another double quote. Example: `Extra Virgin Olive Oil,ID002173,"Organic and natural, ""cold-pressed"", 500ml"`

![](https://files.readme.io/598f54c-Screen_Shot_2022-06-22_at_6.10.41_PM.png)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Sample file
> 
> Here's a sample data feed file: [Sample Data Feed](https://drive.google.com/file/d/13iUvsSQSloR4dgcrs8X01uWH3G2zRzDY/view?usp=share_link).

Field name| Description| Syntax and specifications| Required?  
---|---|---|---  
`productId`| The unique ID that represents the product.Example: b14s001-8100| • String• Max 32 bytes (equivalent to 32 characters in ASCII encoding)• Only characters within the ASCII range 0x21 ~ 0x7e are allowed| Required  
`title`| The name of the product.Example: Lemon Herbal Tea 抗UV太陽眼鏡 お香２０種セット| • String• Max 100 bytes (equivalent to 100 characters in ASCII encoding)| Required  
`url`| The URL that directs to the product details page.| • String| Required  
`image`| The URL that links to the product image.| • String• Must start with http:// or https://• Image format should be PNG, GIF, JPG/JPEG or WebP.• Use the same image size across all products.• Use images that let users easily identify the product.• Remove noise from the images (e.g. watermarks, discount tags)| Required if using **Similar Images** recommendation model  
`description`| The product’s description.| • String• Use informative description to build high-quality product recommendation models.• Avoid using repetitive descriptions. Keep it unique to help users easily identify and remember your products.• Max 5000 bytes (equivalent to 5000 characters in ASCII encoding)| Required if using **Similar Product Attributes** recommendation model  
`category`| The category IDs or names based on your product taxonomy.Example: L0 > L1 > L2 > L3 > L4Category_A > Category_B, Category_C| • String• Use > to separate multiple levels in a category and include a space before and after the >.• If there are multiple product hierarchy, use `,` (comma) to separate the categories.• To have better Recommendation results, avoid categories that are too generic (e.g. a toy store using "toy" as the category).• To have better Recommendation results, avoid categories that are irrelevant to the product attributes (e.g. "on-sale").| Required if using **Similar Product Attributes** or **Similar Images** recommendation model  
`currency`| The price currency.Example: JPY KRW TWD| • String• Currency should follow the standard 3-letter code from ISO-4217. Do not use currency symbols.| RequiredIf your data feed does not include a field for currency, you can ask CSM to apply a constant value such as "USD".  
`originalPrice`| The retail price (excluding discount).Example: 1000 199.9| • Float| Required  
`price`| The current price (including discount).Example: 800 149.9| • Float| Required  
`availability`| The product’s availability.Example: available / unavailable 1 / 0 in stock / out of stock| • String• Binary scheme to indicate whether the product is available or not.| Required  
`condition`| The product's condition.Example: New Like New Used| • String| Required if using trigger campaign based on changes in product condition  
`android_url`| If you have an Android app where you'd like to use deep links, provide the deep link that redirects to the in-app page for Android.| • String| Required if you have an Android app  
`ios_url`| If you have an iOS app where you'd like to use deep links, provide the deep link that redirects to the in-app page for iOS.| • String| Required if you have an iOS app  
`customLabel00` `customLabel01` `customLabel02` `customLabel03` `customLabel04`| If your data feed includes other fields that are not listed in this table, they will be mapped as custom labels.| • String or float or boolean• Max 5000 bytes (equivalent to 5000 characters in ASCII encoding)| Optional  
  
* * *

## 

2\. Hosting the data feed file

You need to host the data feed file on your server, and AIQUA will regularly synchronize the feed file from the specified URL.

### 

Requirements: File hosting

  * You should provide a direct HTTP/HTTPS URL of the data feed file hosted on your own server.
  * You can provide an authentication such as Username-Password to control the access. Examples: `https://username:password@your-web-server/dir/products.json`
  * If you're using an access control list to manage permissions for your data feed file, please allow the following IP addresses so Appier's services can access it:
    * `61.216.8.104`
    * `61.216.8.103`
    * `13.229.23.41`
    * `3.0.119.155`

    * `34.84.107.180/32`
    * `34.84.45.228/32`

    * `34.84.94.6/32`
    * `111.235.224.78/32`
    * `111.235.224.79/32`
    * `111.235.224.80/32`

## 

3\. Onboarding process

### 

Work with your customer success manager to complete the integration procedures

If you have experience with creating feeds for Google Shopping or Facebook Catalog, then it would be a similar procedure to create the product data feed for AIQUA. In general, we recommend working with your Customer Success Manager to walk through the following steps.

  1. Work with your Customer Success Manager to design the scenarios and decide which data fields to include in the product data feed, and the semantics of the fields.
  2. Prepare a hosting server for the data feed file.
  3. Provide the URL of the data feed to your Customer Success Manager. Your Customer Success Manager will proceed with the following steps:
     * Validate the data feed requirements (File format, encoding, CSV delimiter, XML product tag names)
     * Inspect products of the data feed file
     * Map your fields to AIQUA product schema (for Recommendation only)
     * Test parsing data feed
     * Enable the data feed to your AIQUA AppId
  4. Once enabled, you will be notified by your Customer Success Manager and get a data feed id, such as `your-app.com`.
  5. Test your scenario to see if the campaign contents or the product recommendation are functioning properly.



* * *

## 

4\. FAQs

### 

What product data should I include in the data feed?

To decide what product data to include in the data feed, think about whether and how you will be utilizing the following features. Below are some scenarios of how the features can be used and the product data required.

Features| Scenario  
---|---  
Product recommendations| To generate product recommendations, it is best to integrate all fields labeled as "Required" in the table above. For the `description` column, having informative info about the product is important for AIQUA to build high-quality AI models for recommendations.  
Using product feed in dynamic content| Let's say you want to include the brand of the products viewed by users in dynamic content, but this information is not collected by the SDK. If you provide a `brand` field in the product feed, you can now include `brand` information in a message like this: "Check out the latest collection from {{product_viewed.0.feed.brand}}!"  
Trigger campaign based on feed changes| You can set up a trigger campaign based on changes in the product price. Whenever the product price drops by 10%, a "Don’t miss it. Your favorite item is now on sale!" notification can be sent to users who have added the product to their carts before. To achieve this, you need to have `price` in your data feed.  
  
* * *

### 

How often should I update my product data?

The update frequency depends on the nature of your business. In general, it is usually sufficient to have an automatic update from your system to your hosting server on a **daily basis**. Some people choose to update **hourly** or **twice a day** as the products in their CMS/PLM systems update more frequently and they need to have more timely data for their marketing campaigns.

* * *

### 

How often does AIQUA fetch data feed from my hosting server?

By default, AIQUA fetches the data feed from your hosting server every 3 hours. This update frequency can impact the related features in the following ways.

Feature| Impact  
---|---  
Product recommendations| AIQUA excludes out-of-stock products from recommendation results. However, if a product becomes out-of-stock recently, it is possible for the recommendation results to still include the out-of-stock product until the next time AIQUA fetches the updated data feed.  
Using product feed in dynamic content| Changes in product attributes that happened after AIQUA last fetches the data feed may not be reflected yet.  
Trigger campaign based on feed changes| Trigger campaigns based on feed changes will be sent when AIQUA fetches the updated data feed.  
  
* * *

### 

Can I change how often AIQUA fetches the data feed?

For product recommendations, this frequency can be adjusted based on your needs.

Usually, AIQUA does a **full update** by replacing the entire data feed file. If you want AIQUA to fetch data feed at a higher frequency and your data feed has a large file size that takes a long time to synchronize, it is recommended to do **partial updates** instead. With partial updates, you need to also provide a smaller feed file with the updated products only in addition to the entire data feed file.

#### 

Full Update

You need to provide a feed file to AIQUA that includes the entire product data feed.

  * AIQUA replaces the existing product data feed with the new source file.
  * If an existing product is not in the new source file, AIQUA excludes this product from the latest product data feed.



#### 

Partial Update

For partial updates, you also need to provide a feed file that only includes the updates you want to make to the product data feed. In this partial feed file:

  * Product data with a new product `id` would be added as a new product.
  * To delete a product, change the `availability` to out of stock.
  * To update an existing product, the product `id` needs to match with the product `id` in an existing row. AIQUA overwrites the entire row, so make sure you include the value for the unchanged columns as well.



Below is an example of a data feed file that includes three products.

![](https://files.readme.io/f0be0c2-Screen_Shot_2021-12-15_at_8.42.07_PM.png)

Let's say you want to make the following changes.

  * Update the price of product "P001"
  * Delete product "P002"
  * Add a new product "P004"



Using partial update, you will need to prepare a feed file that looks like this.

![](https://files.readme.io/b353d1f-Screen_Shot_2021-12-15_at_8.53.34_PM.png)

# (Optional) Sending Provisional Push Notifications

## 

What is provisional authorization

iOS 12 introduced a new feature called **Provisional Authorization** to give you the ability to send notifications silently, without user permission. The notification is only delivered in the notification center, and the user gets the option to keep receiving notifications from the app silently, prominently, or to turn them off.

![](https://files.readme.io/9d322ac-c5eb6f4-ios_provisional_sample_1.png)

* * *

## 

Sending a provisional push notification

Here's how you can use the [UNAuthorizationOptionProvisional](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unauthorizationoptions/2993019-provisional) API:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplicationLaunchOptionsKey: Any]?) -> Bool {
      // Override point for customization after application launch
      let QG = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
      #if DEBUG
        QG.onStart("AIQUA_APPID", withAppGroup:"APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID", setDevProfile: true)
      #else
        QG.onStart("AIQUA_APPID", withAppGroup:"APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID", setDevProfile: false)
      #endif
    
      if #available(iOS 10.0, *) {
        let center = UNUserNotificationCenter.current()
        center.delegate = self
        var options = UNAuthorizationOptions([.alert, .sound, .badge, .carPlay])
        
        // sample code to enable Provisional Authorization
        if #available(iOS 12.0, *) {
          options.update(with: .provisional)
        }
        
        
        center.requestAuthorization(options: options) { (granted, error)in
          print("Granted: \(granted), Error: \(String(describing: error))")
        }
      } else {
        let settings = UIUserNotificationSettings(types: [.alert, .badge, .sound], categories:nil)
        UIApplication.shared.registerUserNotificationSettings(settings)
      }
    
      return true
    }
    
    
    - (BOOL)application:(UIApplication *)application didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:(NSDictionary *)launchOptions
    {
    
      //Initializing the SDK 
      QGSdk *qgsdk = [QGSdk getSharedInstance];
      #ifdef DEBUG
        [qgsdk onStart:@"your aiqua appid" withAppGroup:@"group.com.company.product.notification" setDevProfile:YES];
      #else
        [qgsdk onStart:@"your aiqua appid" withAppGroup:@"group.com.company.product.notification" setDevProfile:NO];
      #endif
    
        //Registering Push Notification
        if (@available(iOS 10.0, *)) {
            UNAuthorizationOptions options = (UNAuthorizationOptions) (UNAuthorizationOptionAlert | UNAuthorizationOptionBadge | UNAuthorizationOptionSound | UNAuthorizationOptionCarPlay);
        
            //add provisional for silent push in notification center
            if (@available(iOS 12.0, *)) {
              options = options | UNAuthorizationOptionProvisional;
            }
    
            UNUserNotificationCenter *center = [UNUserNotificationCenter currentNotificationCenter];
            center.delegate = self;
            [center requestAuthorizationWithOptions:options completionHandler:^(BOOL granted, NSError *error){
                NSLog(@"GRANTED: %i, Error: %@", granted, error);
            }];
        } else {
            // Fallback on earlier versions - iOS 8 & 9
            UIUserNotificationType types = UIUserNotificationTypeAlert | UIUserNotificationTypeSound |
            UIUserNotificationTypeBadge;
            UIUserNotificationSettings *settings = [UIUserNotificationSettings settingsForTypes:types categories:nil];
            [[UIApplication sharedApplication] registerUserNotificationSettings:settings];
        }
    
      
        return YES;
    }

# Android Push Campaigns

## 

Overview

Push notifications can be used to deliver important or useful information to your users, even when your app is running in the background or inactive.

  * **For apps targeting API level 33 or higher** : Your app's `AndroidManifest.xml` must [include the `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission](doc:installing-in-android-studio#request-the-notification-permission-for-apps-targeting-api-level-33) for devices running Android 13 or later to receive push notifications.
  * **For apps targeting API level 32 or lower** : The Appier Android SDK automatically handles push notifications from Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM).



You can also customize your `FirebaseMessagingService` implementation depending on your app's specific needs (e.g. if your app requires the use of multiple FCM services, custom FCM services, or needs to disable push AIQUA push notifications).

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notifications from non-FCM services
> 
> Impressions and clicks for notifications sent by notification services other than FCM are not tracked.

* * *

## 

Custom `FirebaseMessagingService` implementation

You can use a custom implementation of `FirebaseMessagingService` if you want to:

  * Support behaviors that aren't supported by the default implementation provided by the Android SDK (e.g. using multiple FCM services).
  * Disable AIQUA push notifications.



### 

1\. Define a class

First, define a class that extends `FirebaseMessagingService`.

In the following examples, we'll use a class named `MyFcmListener` to demonstrate a custom implementation:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService;
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage;
    
    public class MyFcmListener extends FirebaseMessagingService {
        // Implement any required class methods
    }
    
    
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage
    
    class MyFcmListener : FirebaseMessagingService() {
        // Implement any required class methods
    }

### 

2\. Implement class methods

Depending on what functionalities you need, implement the following methods in the class you defined:

  * `onMessageReceived()`: Required for receiving or blocking AIQUA push notifications.
  * `onNewToken()`: Required for receiving AIQUA push notifications.



#### 

Receiving AIQUA push notifications

JavaKotlin
    
    
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService;
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage;
    import com.quantumgraph.sdk.QG;
    
    public class MyFcmListener extends FirebaseMessagingService {
        @Override
        public void onMessageReceived(RemoteMessage message) {
            // If the message is from AIQUA, handleRemoteMessage() returns true
            // and processes it. Otherwise, the method returns false.
            if (!QG.getInstance(this).handleRemoteMessage(message)) {
                // handle FCM message from other services
            }
        }
    
        @Override
        public void onNewToken(String token) {
            super.onNewToken(token);
            QG.logFcmId(getApplicationContext());
            // handle FCM token for other services
        }
    }
    
    
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage
    import com.quantumgraph.sdk.QG
    
    class MyFcmListener : FirebaseMessagingService() {
        override fun onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage) {
            // If the message is from AIQUA, handleRemoteMessage() returns true
            // and processes it. Otherwise, the method returns false.
            if (!QG.getInstance(this).handleRemoteMessage(message)) {
                // handle FCM message from other services
            }
        }
    
        override fun onNewToken(token: String) {
            super.onNewToken(token)
            QG.logFcmId(applicationContext)
            // handle FCM token for other services
        }
    }

#### 

Blocking AIQUA push notifications

JavaKotlin
    
    
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService;
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage;
    import com.quantumgraph.sdk.QG;
    
    public class MyFcmListener extends FirebaseMessagingService {
        @Override
        public void onMessageReceived(RemoteMessage message) {
            if (QG.getInstance(getApplicationContext()).isAppierPush(message.getData())) {
                // Do nothing to block AIQUA message
            }
        }
    }
    
    
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.FirebaseMessagingService
    import com.google.firebase.messaging.RemoteMessage
    import com.quantumgraph.sdk.QG
    
    class MyFcmListener : FirebaseMessagingService() {
        override fun onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage) {
            if (QG.getInstance(applicationContext).isAppierPush(message.data)) {
                // Do nothing to block AIQUA message
            }
        }
    }

### 

3\. Add the class to `AndroidManifest.xml`

After you've defined the class and implemented the required methods, declare the class as a service in `AndroidManifest.xml`.

AndroidManifest.xml
    
    
    <service android:name=".MyFcmListener">
      <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT" />   
      </intent-filter>
    </service>

# Flutter Push Campaigns

There are two ways to implement push notifications in your Flutter app.

  * **Option 1** : [Native setup](doc:flutter-push-native-setup)
  * **Option 2** : [Using the Firebase Messaging plugin for Flutter](doc:flutter-using-the-firebase-messaging-plugin)
    * The Appier SDK supports the `firebase_messaging` plugin for push notifications; this push notification setup method works for both Android and iOS platforms.

# Push Notifications

AIQUA React Native Library supports sending push notifications in Android as well as iOS builds. To be able to send push notifications, complete the following integrations.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> Make sure you have already configured the initial setups required for Android and iOS. See [here](doc:initial-setup-for-native-android-and-ios).

## 

For Android

Required Integration| Instructions  
---|---  
Push Notifications| Follow the steps in [[Android] Push Notifications](doc:registering-push-notifications-react-native-android).  
Implementing Deep Links| Follow the steps in [[Android] Implementing Deep Links](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-android).  
  
* * *

## 

For iOS

Required Integration| Instructions  
---|---  
Registering Push Notifications| Follow the steps in [[iOS] Registering Push Notifications](doc:registering-push-notifications-react-native).  
Handling Push Notifications| Follow the steps in [[iOS] Handling Push Notifications](doc:handling-push-notifications-for-ios).  
Rich Push Notifications| Follow the steps in [[iOS] Rich Push Notifications](doc:rich-push-notifications-react-native).  
Implementing Deep Links| Follow the steps for [implementing iOS deep links](doc:react-native-implementing-deep-links#ios-deep-links).

# Implementing Deep Links

## 

Overview

The Appier React Native SDK supports passing deep links to your app. Note that the React Native SDK doesn't resolve or handle deep links—the links are passed directly to the app for handling.

Refer to the instructions below to start using deep links with your app:

  * Android deep links
  * iOS deep links



* * *

## 

Android deep links

Follow the [deep link implementation instructions for Android](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-android).

* * *

## 

iOS deep links

iOS deep links can be implemented using one of the following methods:

  * Option 1: Using a custom URL scheme
  * Option 2: Using universal links



### 

Option 1: Using a custom URL scheme

Follow the [deep link implementation instructions for iOS](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-ios#option-1-using-a-custom-url-scheme).

### 

Option 2: Using universal links

Call `setUniversalLinkDomains()` after `RNAiqua.configure()`:

JavaScript
    
    
    RNAiqua.setUniversalLinkDomains(["YOUR_DOMAIN_1", "YOUR_DOMAIN_2"])

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> To prevent unexpected issues, don't call `setUniversalLinkDomains()` in the native iOS code.

# React Native SDK Overview

The Appier Enterprise Service SDK ("Appier SDK") is the main SDK for Appier's Enterprise Products: AIXON, AIQUA, and AiDeal.

Refer to the following versions when setting up React Native integrations in AIQUA.

Current Appier SDK Version| SDK Download  
---|---  
**2.1.4**| [Appier React Native SDK](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@appier/react-native-sdk)  
  
> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> IMPORTANT NOTICES
> 
>   * If you're upgrading from version 1.8.0 or earlier, you'll need to change the React Native SDK package name from `react-native-aiqua-sdk` to `@appier/react-native-sdk` in all the import lines in your app and your app's dependencies in `package.json`
> 
>   * If you're setting your Android app's `targetSdkVersion` to `31` (Android 12), you'll need to upgrade to React Native SDK 1.8.0.
> 
>   * Starting in November 2021, Android app updates will be required to target API level 30 or above and adjust for behavioral changes in Android 11. See the official Android Developer guides [here](https://developer.android.com/distribute/best-practices/develop/target-sdk#pre11).  
>  **[SDK Upgrade Required]** To avoid a crash issue in Android apps targeting API level 30 or above, upgrade your app to Appier React Native SDK 1.6.1. See [Release Notes](doc:react-native-sdk-release-notes#v161---september-7-2021).
> 
>   * Starting from version 1.4.0, Appier SDK uses CocoaPods dependency. We recommend you to upgrade to React Native version > 0.60.
> 
>   * **If you are upgrading to Appier SDK 1.4.0 or above for the first time** , some migration steps are needed for iOS Rich Push integration. Refer to this [**Migration Doc**](doc:ios-sdk-migration-for-react-native).
> 
>   * Appier SDK **does NOT support Expo Managed Workflow**. If you want to use Appier SDK in Expo, eject to Bare Workflow.
> 
> 


* * *

## 

Dependencies Version Support

Supported Versions| Dependency  
---|---  
• **React** \- 16.0.0 and above   
• **React Native** \- 0.46.0 and above| [React Native WebView](https://github.com/react-native-community/react-native-webview) \- 5.0.1 and above  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> **For React Native versions 0.60.0 and above** ,
> 
>   * Use Appier SDK versions 1.3.1 and above only.
>   * Appier SDK versions 1.3.1 and above support CocoaPods installation and automatic linking.
> 

> 
> **For React Native versions 0.59.x and below** , Appier SDK version 1.3.1 is also supported.

* * *

## 

Release Notes

Release notes of Appier React Native SDK can be found [here](doc:react-native-sdk-release-notes).

* * *

## 

Release Candidates (Testing Only)

Any Appier SDK version with `rc` in the version number is a release candidate. When installing SDK, use release versions such as `1.3.0` or `1.3.1` instead of release candidates such as `1.3.1-rc-1` or `1.3.1-rc-2`. Release candidates may be unstable and are intended for testing purposes.
