# Other Important Methods

## 

Common methods

Some additional useful and important methods are listed here. Use these to call functions in the React Native SDK.

Method| Description  
---|---  
`RNAiqua.setInAppCampaignVisible(true)`| • Passing `true` Allows in-app campaigns to be displayed.• Passing `false` Closes the in-app campaign that's currently being displayed and prevents future in-app campaigns from displaying.  
`RNAiqua.removeInAppCampaign()`| Closes the in-app campaign that's currently being displayed.  
`RNAiqua.disableInAppCampaigns(true)`| Disable in-app pop-up campaigns.  
`RNAiqua.hideInAppCampaigns()`| Clear all the foreground in-app pop-ups.  
`RNAiqua.flush()`| By default, queued data is flushed to the AIQUA servers every 15 seconds--the default for `flushInterval`. Call this method manually if you want to force a flush at a particular moment.  
`RNAiqua.setAttributionWindow(7200)`| Sets the view-through attribution window. The default is one hour, i.e. 3600 seconds. Value should be passed in seconds.Starting from React Native SDK 1.5, if set to `0`, the attribution window will fall back to its default value.  
`RNAiqua.setClickAttributionWindow(43200)`| Sets the click-through attribution window. The default is 24 hours, i.e. 86,400 seconds. Value should be passed in seconds.Starting from React Native SDK 1.5, if set to 0, the attribution window will fall back to its default value.  
`RNAiqua.renewUserId()`| Deprecated starting from React Native SDK 1.10.0.Creates a new AIQUA userId and clean all local data related to the previous userId. When the process is completed, return a promise with no return values.  
`RNAiqua.enableStoredNotification()`| Enables the local storage of push notifications.  
`RNAiqua.setMaxNumStoredNotifications(60)`| Sets the maximum number of push notifications that can be stored locally.  
`RNAiqua.getStoredNotifications( ret => { //ret is the stored notifications } )`| Retrieves locally-stored push notification data. Return a promise with an array of the stored notifications.  
`RNAiqua.deleteStoredNotification(5)`| Removes a specific locally stored push notification with its index.  
`RNAiqua.deleteStoredNotifications()`| Removes all locally stored push notification data.  
`RNAiqua.getAppierId()`| Returns the Appier ID.  
`RNAiqua.renewAppierId()`| Regenerate the ID.  
`RNAiqua.isAppierPush("string")`| Checks if the entered message is an AIQUA message.  
  
* * *

## 

iOS methods

The following methods are only available for iOS.

Method| Description  
---|---  
      
    
    RNAiqua.setUniversalLinkDomains(
    ["first.domain.com", "second.domain.com”])

| Use this method to set the Associated Domains for Universal Links.  
`RNAiqua.setIDFAConsent(true)`| To use this method, you need to integrate the App Tracking Transparency framework first.Refer to the [App Tracking Transparency document](doc:app-tracking-transparency-react-native) for details.  
`RNAiqua.disableInAppCampaigns(false)`| Re-enable in-app pop-up campaigns.  
  
  


* * *

## 

Android methods

The following methods are only available for Android.

Method| Description  
---|---  
`RNAiqua.setUtmSource('UTMSOURCE')``RNAiqua.setUtmMedium('UTMMEDIUM')``RNAiqua.setUtmTerm('UTMTERM')``RNAiqua.setUtmContent('UTMCONTENT')``RNAiqua.setUtmCampaign('UTMCAMPAIGN')`| Apart from default user profile parameters, you can also log the UTM source through which the user installed the app via these methods.  
`RNAiqua.isQGMessage( 'SOME_MESSAGE', ret => { //ret is the result--true or false } )`| Deprecated starting from React Native SDK 1.10.0.Checks if the entered message is an AIQUA message.  
`RNAiqua.enablePushBooster()`| Enables push booster.  
`RNAiqua.disableLocationTracking()`| Disables location tracking.

# Development React Native SDK Versions

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note: Known issues
> 
> This page only announces critical known issues and their fixes. Issues are classified as critical if they cause campaign failures or app crashes that are highly likely to be encountered by app users.
> 
> For a comprehensive list of known issues and bug fixes, please refer to the native SDK release notes ([Android](doc:release-notes-android), [iOS](doc:release-notes-ios)).

# 

v2.1.4 - July 4, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `8.2.5` to `8.3.1`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `8.2.3` to `8.3.2`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where event failed to be logged for iOS apps running in developer mode after force killing the app, then relaunching it.



* * *

# 

v2.1.3 - April 30, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `8.2.4` to `8.2.5`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `8.2.1` to `8.2.3`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Fixed

  * The following error is no longer displayed when building apps using React Native 0.74 or later: `AppierWebView has no setter or ivar for its methodQueue, which is not permitted. You must either @synthesize the methodQueue property, or provide your own setter method.`



* * *

# 

v2.1.2 - March 14, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `8.2.1` to `8.2.4`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Added logic to map incorrectly regenerated Appier IDs to their original correct IDs, enabling data recovery efforts initiated due to the known issue present in versions 2.1.0 and 2.1.1.



### 

Fixed

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is no longer incorrectly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background). This issue is present in versions 2.1.0 and 2.1.1



* * *

#  v2.1.1 - February 7, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `8.2.0` to `8.2.1`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `8.2.0` to `8.2.1`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Known issues

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is mistakenly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background) after upgrading to this SDK version. These regenerated Appier IDs were mistakenly counted as new users, impacting related metrics and segments.



* * *

#  v2.1.0 - January 23, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `8.0.1` to `8.2.0`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `8.0.1` to `8.2.0`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Fixed

  * Calling `setCustomKey` with a large non-integer number on Android produced incorrect output.



### 

Known issues

  * The Appier ID (`userId`) is mistakenly regenerated on the first app launch (either in the foreground or background) after upgrading to this SDK version. These regenerated Appier IDs were mistakenly counted as new users, impacting related metrics and segments.



* * *

# 

v2.0.1 - December 9, 2024

### 

Changed

  * `react-native-webview` is now an optional dependency.



* * *

# 

v2.0.0 - November 22, 2024

## 

New

  * Support for Retail Media Network features (beta). To learn more, contact your customer success manager.



## 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `7.25.0` to `8.0.1`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `7.33.0` to `8.0.1`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * `configure()` now returns a promise that resolves to a boolean, enabling you to verify that the SDK has initialized successfully before calling other methods. To learn more, see [Initializing the SDK via React Native](doc:initializing-the-sdk-via-react-native#importing-react-native-aiqua).
  * Starting from this version, the Appier React Native SDK requires additional initialization code for Android. For details, see [Initializing the React Native SDK](doc:initializing-the-sdk-via-react-native).
  * For Android notifications to work, you need to apply the Google Services Gradle plugin in `android/app/build.gradle` file. For details, see [[Android] Push Notifications](doc:registering-push-notifications-react-native-android).

> Note: Known issues
> 
> This page only announces critical known issues and their fixes. Issues are classified as critical if they cause campaign failures or app crashes that are highly likely to be encountered by app users.

> For a comprehensive list of known issues and bug fixes, please refer to the native SDK release notes ([Android](doc:release-notes-android), [iOS](doc:release-notes-ios)).

# 

v1.5.0 - May 07, 2021

  * [Updated] Native iOS SDK from 7.3.0 to 7.9.0.
    * See [iOS SDK Release Notes](doc:release-notes-for-ios#v790---march-31-2021).
    * See [here](doc:app-tracking-transparency-react-native) for integrating **App Tracking Transparency (ATT)** framework.
  * [Updated] Native Android SDK from 6.4.0 to 6.10.0.
    * See [Android SDK Release Notes](doc:release-notes-for-android#v6100---march-12-2021).
  * [Fixed] Initialization of Appier Web SDK fails from time to time in `RNAiquaWebView` if web SDK is initialized before app SDK. (Android)



* * *

# 

v1.4.0 - November 11, 2020

  * [New] iOS Rich Push Integration with CocoaPods `AppierFramework`.
  * [Updated] Native iOS SDK to version 7.3.0.
  * [Updated] Native Android SDK to version 6.4.0.
  * [Fixed] Crash issue on iOS 14 when the app runs in background.



* * *

# 

v1.3.3 - July 28, 2020

  * [New] Support for Firebase Integration in iOS.
  * [Fixed] Fixed issue with notification sound in Android Push.



* * *

# 

v1.3.2 - June 19, 2020

  * [Fixed] Fixed issue with handling profile parameters in Android that occurs when using `setCustomKey` method and using numbers as value.



* * *

# 

v1.3.1 - April 6, 2020

  * [New] Support for CocoaPods installation and automatic linking in React Native versions 0.60.0 and above.

# Stable React Native SDK Versions

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note: Known issues
> 
> This page only announces critical known issues and their fixes. Issues are classified as critical if they cause campaign failures or app crashes that are highly likely to be encountered by app users.
> 
> For a comprehensive list of known issues and bug fixes, please refer to the native SDK release notes ([Android](doc:release-notes-android), [iOS](doc:release-notes-ios)).

# 

v1.13.1 - February 6, 2026

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.27.0 to 7.27.1. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes-stable) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Fixed

  * (Android) Fixed a backwards compatibility issue causing in-app campaigns fail to display on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions weren't tracked for failed campaigns. Affected version: 1.13.0.



* * *

# 

v1.13.0 - November 10, 2025

### 

New

  * Support for logging data to different app IDs from within a web view. To enable this feature, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#543127270b272124243b2620143524243d31267a373b39)).



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.26.0 to 7.27.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes-stable) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.34.1 to 7.35.6. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Known issues

  * (Android) In-app campaigns fail to display due to a backwards compatibility issue on devices running Android 10 or earlier. Impressions aren’t tracked for failed campaigns.



* * *

# 

v1.12.0 - December 6, 2024

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.25.0 to 7.26.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.33.0 to 7.34.1. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v1.11.1 - August 12, 2024

No changes were introduced in this version.

* * *

# 

v1.11.0 - August 9, 2024

## 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.24.3 to 7.25.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.32.3 to 7.33.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v1.10.2 - May 2, 2024

## 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.24.2 to 7.24.3. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.32.2 to 7.32.3. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v1.10.0 - March 27, 2024

## 

New

  * Support for TypeScript.
  * Added the following SDK methods:
    * `getAppierId()`
    * `renewAppierId()`
    * `isAppierPush()`



## 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.11.0 to 7.24.2. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.19.1 to 7.32.2. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Added the following SDK methods:
    * `renewUserId()`
    * `isQgMessage()`



## 

Fixed

  * [Requesting recommendations](doc:recommendation-web) in a web view caused a JSON syntax error.



* * *

# 

v1.9.1 - March 3, 2023

## 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.19.1 to 7.19.2. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



## 

Fixed

  * In mobile apps using React Native SDK 1.9.0, calling the Recommendation API resulted in an error message displaying in the app and no results being returned.



* * *

# 

v1.9.0 - October 28, 2022

## 

Changed

  * The React Native SDK's package name has been changed from `react-native-aiqua-sdk` to `@appier/react-native-sdk`
  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.8.0 to 7.11.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.16.0 to 7.19.1. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



## 

Fixed

  * The fractional portion of float values in event parameters was truncated when logging events using `logEvent()`



* * *

# 

v1.8.0 - March 29, 2022

## 

New

  * A method to clear all foreground in-app pop-up notifications. See `hideInAppCampaigns()` in the [list of React Native SDK methods](doc:react-native-sdk-methods).



## 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.6.1 to 7.8.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.15.0 to 7.16.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



## 

Fixed

  * An issue that caused Android push campaign notifications to be unclickable. This issue would occur after setting `targetSdkVersion` to `31`.
  * An issue causing Activity leaks.
  * An issue that caused some OPPO, Xiaomi, and Realme devices to crash unexpectedly.
  * Aligned the Android SDK's in-app campaign floating icon size with the iOS SDK's floating icon size.



* * *

# 

v1.7.0 - February 22, 2022

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.3.1 to 7.6.1. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.13.0 to 7.15.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
    * If you've configured rich push notifications, please [update your Podfile to use the latest version of `ApperExtensionFramework`](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/rich-push-notifications-react-native#installing-with-cocoapods).



### 

Fixed

  * Suppressed erroneous Android error messages when calling `setFCMToken()`.



* * *

# 

v1.6.1 - September 7, 2021

  * [Updated] Native Android SDK from 7.3.0 to 7.3.1.
    * See [Android SDK Release Notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes#v731---august-30-2021).



* * *

# 

v1.6.0 - August 24, 2021

  * [Updated] Native iOS SDK from 7.9.0 to 7.13.0.
    * See [iOS SDK Release Notes](doc:release-notes-for-ios#v7130---august-12-2021).
  * [Updated] Native Android SDK from 6.10.0 to 7.3.0.
    * See [Android SDK Release Notes](doc:release-notes-for-android#v730---august-12-2021).
  * [New] Support for collecting the React Native SDK version and SDK type used in the app.
  * [New] Support for [filtering out purchased products](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#optional-step-eliminate-purchased-products-from-results) from recommendation results based on `user_id` in WebView.
  * [New] Introduced new API for easier [FCM customization](doc:registering-push-notifications-react-native-android) in Android.
  * [Fixed] Improved compatibility with Expo Bare Workflow

# Manage Scenarios

Manage your existing recommendation scenarios.

  * View your scenarios
  * Edit scenario settings
  * Perform scenario operations
  * Export performance reports



* * *

## 

View your scenarios

In the scenario list, you can view, search, and filter scenarios as well as set scenario conversion settings.

  * Set a date range for scenario metrics
  * Search and filter scenarios
  * Choose the conversion definition
  * Monitor scenario status



### 

Set a date range for scenario metrics

You can set a custom date range for the scenario metrics displayed in the scenario list by selecting a preset or setting a custom range, then clicking **Apply**.

![](https://files.readme.io/67f6b1cb63e2cbc52664090cf007c4753d1c35136a610ae8d9a8e1fc2df26d3b-scenario-list-date-range.png)

### 

Search and filter scenarios

To search scenarios by name or scenario ID, enter a keyword in the search box.

![](https://files.readme.io/2295a14aecf6dd974b2492ec580a49efb3d7b21c836a02c0f759a8beda100304-scenario-list-search.png)

You can also filter by specific scenario settings such as status, placement, or model.

![](https://files.readme.io/623642787a6903aa7079b454927b57c178be06eb7c761a0e75656e266e75109e-scenario-list-filters.png)

### 

Choose the conversion definition

Set the [conversion definition](doc:recommendations-20-analytics#conversion-definitions) used to calculated conversion-based metrics.

![](https://files.readme.io/223512736710e94c1c02e0d4f74a1cd9205c8f5fe210a5db792122e110b9cf2c-scenario-list-set-conversion-setting.png)

### 

Monitor scenario status

Check the **Status** column to determine whether a scenario is currently serving recommendation results.

![](https://files.readme.io/a610b73e6d0dc1b822aa3703247f14bd16afa01cc24e133ad1ee87eff4697f0c-scenario-list-status.png)

Status| Description  
---|---  
**Preparing**|  This scenario is still training and isn't ready for use.It can take several days for the model to finish training depending on how large your product data feed is and which model the scenario is using.  
**Ready**|  This scenario has finished training and is ready for use. The model will continue to collect data and optimize results.  
**Updating**|  This scenario is in the process of retraining based on changes to scenario settings. During this time, results continue to be served based on the previous settings.  
**Archived**|  This scenario can't be used and no longer serves recommendation results.  
  
* * *

## 

Edit scenario settings

Click the edit button next to a scenario's name to open its settings. After editing the scenario settings, the model re-trains based on the new settings. The previously configured settings will be used until the training is complete.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Limitations
> 
>   * The **Page type** setting can't be edited.
>   * Settings can't be edited for scenarios using the following models:
>     * **Autopilot**
>     * **Professional Service - Custom Model (Premium)**
> 


![](https://files.readme.io/cac77715cc1a65c16690cb140199b32435ad172c33c49bc3a11099edf92c1fc9-scenario-list-edit.png)

* * *

## 

Perform scenario operations

Click ![](https://files.readme.io/4a6c9c036e217b391e63315b326c75ac96198c1f68407954faf6fb90594d5abe-details.png) to see the available scenario actions. 

![](https://files.readme.io/5fe9ebb7dcc1c470a240abbdd0c463c69de88b69d4b1e703d9144fef86178d14-scenario-list-operations.png)

Action| Description  
---|---  
**Copy scenario ID**|  Copy the scenario ID to use for recommendation requests. This option is available after a scenario completes its first training.  
**Preview results**| [Preview the scenario's results](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#previewing-recommendation-results). This option is only available after the scenario completes its first training.  
**Activity log**|  View timestamped records of all operations on this scenario.  
**Archive**|  Archive the campaign. Once archived, the scenario will stop serving recommendation results.  
  
* * *

## 

Export performance reports

To export performance reports (total and daily) by email, click **Export report**. For details about the metrics contained in performance reports, see [Recommendation Analytics](doc:recommendations-20-analytics#performance-report).

# Recommendation Analytics

Understand the performance of your recommendation scenarios.

After completing the required setup, you'll be able to access recommendation scenario performance data from the scenario list (**Recommendation > Scenario List**).

![](https://files.readme.io/4399d3879359548f52a4ff7b851035d92c45118ff7a00f2b7f3a9f9a3495e0df-scenario-list.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Performance analytics aren't available for recommendation scenarios placed in campaign creatives as dynamic content.

* * *

## 

Required setup

  1. Track clicks on recommendations
  2. Set attribution settings
  3. Set conversion settings



### 

1\. Track clicks on recommendations

Your developers can use the Appier SDK methods to track clicks on scenario results. For implementation details, refer to the following guides.

[ ![Web SDK](https://files.readme.io/4ea9ef89042bd4c960295d3efd8de6a09b243612b2fa4aa08660c5acf8ce7685-Web_push.png) Web ](/docs/sdk-web-recommendation#tracking-clicks-and-impressions) [ ![Android SDK](https://files.readme.io/acaf48aec3ad0ab62ad5b68751390de05ae8fac1af4ea440e9d21ac607702ab1-android-head_flat.png) Android ](/docs/sdk-android-recommendation#tracking-clicks-and-impressions) [ ![iOS SDK](https://cdn.simpleicons.org/apple/000000) iOS ](/docs/sdk-ios-recommendation#tracking-clicks-and-impressions  ) [ ![Flutter SDK](https://files.readme.io/7d87ad47dc05a69ba7c2d419809d4ff4d803c477aea68f91a18ad6a0bc65b3df-icon_flutter.0dbfcc7a59cd1cf16282.png) Flutter ](/docs/sdk-flutter-recommendation#tracking-clicks-and-impressions) [ ![React Native SDK](https://cdn.simpleicons.org/react/61DAFB) React Native ](/docs/sdk-react-native-recommendation#tracking-clicks-and-impressions)

### 

2\. Set attribution settings

Go to **Recommendation > Settings** to set the scenario's attribution model and attribution window.

Setting| Description  
---|---  
**Attribution Model**| 

  * **Last-click model** : If the user clicks on multiple recommendation items before conversion, the conversion is attributed to the last clicked recommendation item (if within the attribution window).
  * **First-click model** : If the user clicks on multiple recommendation items before conversion, the conversion is attributed to the first clicked recommendation item (if within the attribution window)

  
**Attribution Window**|  The default attribution window is one day.For conversions to be attributed to a scenario, a conversion must be completed within the attribution window after the user clicks the recommendation.  
  
### 

3\. Set conversion settings

Next, go to **Conversion Settings** to set conversion events for item conversions and event conversions.

#### 

Conversion events

The following table list of available conversion events for each conversion definition.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Custom conversion events
> 
> If the event you want to use isn't included, you can use `custom_item_conversion_x`(**Item Conversion**) and `custom_goal_x` (**Event Conversion**) to define your own custom conversion events.

Item Conversion| Event Conversion  
---|---  
`product_added_to_wishlist`  
`product_added_to_cart`  
`product_purchased`  
`content_viewed`  
`content_downloaded`  
`content_scrolldepth_25`  
`content_scrolldepth_50`  
`content_scrolldepth_75`  
`content_scrolldepth_100`  
`content_playtime_25`  
`content_playtime_50`  
`content_playtime_75`  
`content_playtime_100`  
`content_faved`  
`content_shared`  
`content_commented`  
`custom_item_conversion_1`  
`custom_item_conversion_2`  
`custom_item_conversion_3`| `added_to_cart`  
`added_to_wishlist`  
`cart_viewed`  
`wishlist_viewed`  
`checkout_initiated`  
`checkout_step_viewed`  
`checkout_payment_added`  
`checkout_completed`

`login_completed`

`subscription_completed`

## 

Scenario list metrics

![](https://files.readme.io/4399d3879359548f52a4ff7b851035d92c45118ff7a00f2b7f3a9f9a3495e0df-scenario-list.png)

In the scenario list (**Recommendation > Scenario list**) you can set performance data display settings.

  * Conversion definition: Set the conversion definition to **Item Conversion** or **Event Conversion**.
  * Performance date range: Set the date range of the performance data you want to view. The start and end date need to be within 180 days of the current date, based on your account's timezone setting.



> 👍
> 
> Performance data shown in the scenario list is automatically updated every three hours.

![](https://files.readme.io/b827528dcf7fae839dccc55a1eaba5470c8c255fa8257036e8bc637a90857e8b-scenario-list-performance-settings.png)

From the scenario list, you can view the following metrics.

Metric| Description  
---|---  
**Requests**|  The total number of requests made to this scenario.  
**Impressions**|  The total count of `recommendation_impression` events representing the total number of views on recommended items.  
**Clicks**|  The total count of `recommendation_clicked` events representing the total number of clicks on recommended items.  
**CTR**|  The scenario's click-through rate. Calculated using (**Clicks** / **Impressions**) x 100%.  
**Conversions**|  The total number of conversions attributed to the recommendation scenario.  
**CVR**|  The scenario's conversion rate. Calculated using (**Conversions** / **Clicks**) x 100%.  
**Conversion value**|  The total value of the attributed events based on tracked event parameters (`valueToSum` and `vts`).  
  
### 

Conversion definitions

In the scenario list, you can switch between the two to view performance based on each definition.

Setting| Description  
---|---  
**Item Conversion**|  Conversions occurring within the attribution window will be converted to the scenario only if the conversion item is the same item the user clicked. Specifically, the conversion item's product ID parameter must match the clicked recommendation's product ID.  
**Event Conversion**|  Conversions occurring within the attribution window will be converted to the scenario if the user clicks any of the recommended items.  
  
For example, if you select `product_purchased` for **Item Conversion** , and selected `checkout_completed` for **Event Conversion** :

  * **Scenario 1** : A user clicks on products X and Y, which are products recommended by scenario A. The user purchases product Q within the attribution window.
    * **Item Conversion** : No conversion is attributed to scenario A, because the product purchased does not have the same `product_id` as the clicked recommended product.
    * **Event Conversion** : One conversion (`checkout_completed`) is attributed to scenario A.

![](https://files.readme.io/5fe47cb-Screen_Shot_2020-12-20_at_6.15.07_PM.png)

  * **Scenario 2** : A user clicks on products X and Y, which are products recommended by scenario A. The user purchases product X, Y, and Q in one order within the attribution window.
    * **Item Conversion** : Two conversions (`product_purchased` for products X and Y) are attributed to scenario A.
    * **Event Conversion** : One conversion (`checkout_completed`) is attributed to scenario A.

![](https://files.readme.io/9291033-Screen_Shot_2020-12-20_at_6.15.16_PM.png)

* * *

## 

Scenario performance page

From the scenario list, click a scenario's name to view its performance page. In the scenario's performance page, you can select the conversion definition and date range you'd like to view data for.

![](https://files.readme.io/89ce4064c0069d227abc72178f6966cd9a59e9890138cb3e46b98cc0dfb215a5-scenario-analytics.png)

The scenario performance page consists of the following sections:

  * Performance overview
  * Performance trend
  * Performance lift (Autopilot scenarios)
  * Model traffic distribution (Autopilot scenarios)
  * CTR trend by model (Autopilot scenarios)
  * Performance details (Autopilot scenarios)



### 

Performance overview

![](https://files.readme.io/52ad6fbd8c2209e1071a9e71be2d41ae57ce9a72f2633e717b309be59f6d68b2-scenario-analytics-performance-overview.png)

The performance overview chart summarizes the overall performance of the scenario, highlighting the following metrics.

Metric| Description  
---|---  
**CTR**|  The scenario's click-through rate. Calculated using (**Clicks** / **Impressions**) x 100%.  
**CVR**|  The scenario's conversion rate. Calculated using (**Conversions** / **Clicks**) x 100%.  
**Imp. CVR**|  The scenario's Impression to Conversion rate. Calculated using (**Conversions** / **Impressions**) x 100%.  
**Conversion value**|  The total value of the attributed events based on tracked event parameters (`valueToSum` and `vts`).  
  
The highlighted performance metrics are calculated using click, impression, and conversion event counts.

Event| Definition  
---|---  
**Clicks**|  The total count of `recommendation_clicked` events representing the total number of clicks on recommended items.  
**Conversions**|  The total number of conversions attributed to the recommendation scenario.  
**Impressions**|  The total count of `recommendation_impression` events representing the total number of views on recommended items.  
  
### 

Performance trend

Use the performance trend chart to visualize how performance changes over time. From the dropdown menus, you can select two different metrics to display.

![](https://files.readme.io/f967e845b0155fa998cf1d528780ffa3ba399131d174d17cadb3935be8a1e6e2-scenario-analytics-performance-trend.png)

### 

Performance lift (Autopilot scenarios)

> 📘
> 
> This data is only available for scenarios using **Autopilot** recommendation model setting.

**CTR lift** represents the uplift compared to the **Benchmark CTR** , which is the estimated CTR if traffic was evenly distributed across all models without Autopilot's dynamic redistribution.

![](https://files.readme.io/f0a6a2272f5149bd4829833be800f6d4b2edf719380fc2f3f8514e75136d7b60-scenario-analytics-performance-lift.png)

### 

Model traffic distribution (Autopilot scenarios)

> 📘
> 
> This data is only available for scenarios using **Autopilot** recommendation model setting.

The model distribution chart allows you to compare the traffic distribution between each recommendation model.

![](https://files.readme.io/cca8c8b98d4e2a9fc525e07ed172a1acd33e94293280eb675b4af33db0b143db-scenario-analytics-model-traffic-distribution.png)

### 

CTR trend by model (Autopilot scenarios)

> 📘
> 
> This data is only available for scenarios using **Autopilot** recommendation model setting.

The CTR trend by model chart allows you to visualize the CTR trend for each model.

![](https://files.readme.io/e4fb2bf75ad0623fcaf149b8e6f4b6c0ec013ad9dbaa4850a36e0b9886e65c02-scenario-analytics-ctr-trend-by-model.png)

### 

Performance details (Autopilot scenarios)

> 📘
> 
> This data is only available for scenarios using **Autopilot** recommendation model setting.

The performance table summarizes scenario performance metrics broken down by recommendation model.

![](https://files.readme.io/7c065c6edd4858e978856864c092dbbe99b3bf396ca5c81083a02d010b235a92-scenario-analytics-performance-details.png)

* * *

## 

Performance report

To receive performance reports via email, click **Export report** , specify a date range, and click **Export**. The date range is based on your account's timezone setting.

> 📘
> 
> Performance data in the report is calculated based on the conversion definition you selected.

![](https://files.readme.io/36568da714915f969862b2d668e218bbeefc291a8b2e2d5a77aa047e621bdacb-scenario-list-export-report.png)

After clicking **Export** , you'll receive an email that includes download links for two CSV files: a total performance report and a daily performance report.

  1. Total performance report: Contains the total performance accumulated during the specified date range for each scenario.

![](https://files.readme.io/4b57642-Screen_Shot_2022-02-15_at_10.36.05_AM.png)

  2. Daily performance report: Contains daily impressions, clicks, CTR, conversion count, CVR, and conversion value for each scenario.

![](https://files.readme.io/f461412-Screen_Shot_2022-02-15_at_10.57.08_AM.png)

Metrics are counted based on the date of occurrence. In the example illustrated below, two clicks and one conversion are counted on March 8, and one conversion is counted on March 9. Since **Clicks** is 0 on March 9, and **CVR** is calculated using `Conversions / Clicks`, the **CVR** will be listed as "-" in the report.

![](https://files.readme.io/f6ca756-Screen_Shot_2020-12-31_at_9.56.50_AM.png)

# Recommendation

Recommend personalized products to your audience.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Contact your customer success manager to enable this feature.

Use AIQUA's recommendations to show users relevant, personalized products to your audience in your mobile app, website, and campaign creatives.

## 

Getting started with recommendations

You can use AIQUA recommendations with one or both of the following methods:

  * Using the Appier SDK API: Only available for platforms supported by the Appier SDK.
  * Using the REST API: Available for any platform.



### 

Using the Appier SDK API

You can integrate with the Appier SDK to gather user event data and display product recommendations:

  * **On your website or app** : Show products recommended for each user on your website or app.

![](https://files.readme.io/c00e6fa-Screen_Shot_2021-01-12_at_8.05.33_PM.png)

  * **In campaign creatives** : Embed personalized recommendations in your creative's [dynamic content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives).

![](https://files.readme.io/7fa230b-Screen_Shot_2021-01-12_at_11.03.02_AM.png)

### 

Using the REST API

The [Recommendation REST API](ref:recommendation-getting-started) allows you to use recommendations without having to integrate the Appier SDK, giving you maximum flexibility to use recommendations in ways that best suit your needs. For example, the Recommendation REST API on platforms without a supported Appier SDK, such as apps for smart TVs or your physical store's point-of-sale system.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Using recommendations in campaign creatives (via dynamic content) is not supported for REST API-enabled recommendation scenarios. To use recommendations in creatives, use the Appier SDK API to upload event data and retrieve recommendations.

#### 

REST API limitations

By default, scenarios are only compatible with the Appier SDK API methods. Contact your customer success manager to enable the Recommendation REST API for your scenario. REST API-enabled scenarios have the following limitations:

  * **Appier SDK API methods for retrieving recommendations are not supported**. Use the [Get Recommendations](ref:get-recommendations-1) endpoint instead.
  * **Appier SDK API methods for logging user events are not supported for collecting recommendation model training data.** Use the [Upload Event Data endpoint](ref:upload-offline-event-data-v2) to upload an event file containing user event data.
  * **Analytics and performance data are not natively supported for REST API-enabled scenarios**. To [track performance data for REST API-enabled scenarios](ref:recommendation-getting-started#performance-and-analytics), use the Appier SDK's event logging methods.



* * *

## 

Get started with AIQUA recommendations

### 

Prerequisites

Before getting started with AIQUA recommendations, you need to [onboard your product data feed](doc:product-data-feed). A product data feed is a CSV file containing data about all of your products. For recommendation results to be correct, ensure that your data feed includes the fields as described in [model reference](doc:recommendation-models#model-reference).

### 

1\. Upload user event data

Upload user event data to train the recommendation model using either the SDK logging methods or the REST API.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes
> 
>   * Include the product ID parameter when uploading or logging required events. Events without the product ID parameter won't be used to train recommendation models.
>   * If you're using the Web SDK, we recommend [setting a default designated product](doc:recommendation-web#recommended-setting-a-default-selected-product) on every page that contains product data.
> 


Appier SDK | Recommendation REST API  
---|---  
Log user events using one of the following Appier SDK API methods:

  * [Web SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/logging-data-on-the-web-sdk)
  * [Android SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/logging-user-events-for-the-android-sdk)
  * [iOS SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/logging-events-with-parameters-for-ios-sdk)
  * [React Native SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/event-and-profile-logging-for-react-native)
  * [Flutter SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/event-and-profile-logging-for-flutter)

Some recommendation models require specific event types in order to train properly. See [model reference](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/recommendation-models#model-reference) for a full list of required events.  |  To begin uploading event data for a REST API-enabled scenario, please contact Appier Support ([[email protected]).   
2\. Create a recommendation scenario First, [create a recommendation scenario](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20) to obtain a scenario ID. The scenario ID is required to request recommendations via SDK or REST API. ![](https://files.readme.io/3efb552-recommendation-flow.png) 3\. Retrieve recommendations Once your scenario has been created and the recommendation model has completed training, retrieve recommendations using either the SDK API or the REST API. Appier SDK API | Recommendation REST API  
---|---  
Retrieve product recommendations using one of the following Appier SDK API methods:

  * [Web SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/sdk-web-recommendation)
  * [Android SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/sdk-android-recommendation)
  * [iOS SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/sdk-ios-recommendation)
  * [React Native SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/sdk-react-native-recommendation)
  * [Flutter SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/sdk-flutter-recommendation)

You can also use recommendations in your creative's [dynamic content](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives#based-on-recommendation-20).  |  Use the [Get Recommendations endpoint](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/get-recommendations-1) to retrieve product recommendations.   
4\. View performance data View performance and analytics data for all of your scenarios on the AIQUA Dashboard. Appier SDK API | Recommendation REST API  
---|---  
[Tracking recommendation performance](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/recommendations-20-analytics) is supported by the Appier SDK.  |  No native REST API support for performance and analytics data. Requires the use of the Appier SDK logging methods.  See the [Recommendation REST API docs](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/recommendation-getting-started#performance-and-analytics) for instructions on tracking performance data for REST API-enabled scenarios.

# Managing iOS Users

## 

Overview

AIQUA iOS users are identified using the Appier SDK-generated `userId`.

  * Retrieving `userId`
  * Deleting and regenerating iOS users



* * *

## 

Retrieving `userId`

> 📘
> 
> Retrieving the `userId` is only available in iOS SDK v7.25.0 and later.

To retrieve the value of `userId`, call `getAppierId()`:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let qgsdk = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
    let appierUserId = qgsdk?.getAppierId()
    
    
    QGSdk *qgsdk = [QGSdk getSharedInstance];
    NSString *appierUserId = [qgsdk getAppierId];

* * *

## 

Deleting and regenerating iOS users

To delete an iOS user's data and regenerate `userId`, for example, when a user modifies their data tracking consent settings, you'll need to complete two steps:

  1. **Delete the user 's data with the [Delete Users API](ref:delete-users)** using their unique identifier from your CRM (`user_id`).
  2. **Regenerate`userId` using the iOS SDK**. In addition to generating a new `userId`, calling this method will delete all locally cached data, including events, attributes, and campaigns.
     1. **iOS SDK 7.25.0 and later** : Use `renewAppierId()`
     2. **iOS SDK 7.5.0 to 7.24.0** : Use `renewUserId()`
     3. **iOS SDK 7.4.0 and earlier** : Regenerating `userId` is not supported



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> When regenerating `userId`:
> 
>   * The iOS SDK won't renew the app's push token. This prevents users from receiving campaigns before cached data (deleted using the [Delete Users API](ref:delete-users)) is purged from AIQUA's servers.
>   * [User data collection permissions](doc:ios-user-data-permissions) will remain unchanged. Reconfigure the relevant user data permissions after regenerating the user if needed.
> 


SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let qgsdk = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
    
    // iOS SDK 7.25.0 and later
    qgsdk?.renewAppierId({
      // Do anything you want after the Appier ID is renewed
    })
    
    // iOS SDK 7.5.0 to 7.24.0
    qgsdk?.renewUserId({
      // Do anything you want after the Appier ID is renewed
    })
    
    
    QGSdk *qgsdk = [QGSdk getSharedInstance];
    
    // iOS SDK 7.25.0 and later

# Registering for Push Notifications

To be able to send push notifications, you need to request permission from the user. After the user grants permissions to receive notifications, a push notification token will be generated by the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) or Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) servers, then the token must be passed to Appier's servers.

## 

1\. Add the UserNotifications framework

In the main app target, go to **Build Phases** and add the framework **UserNotifications**.

![1050](https://files.readme.io/4c3dcb8-Screen_Shot_2020-06-03_at_7.05.22_PM.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Include headers

In your class where you will handle the push notifications, preferably in the `AppDelegate` class,

  * For Swift, import `UserNotifications`.
  * For Objective-C, import `<UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>`.



You also need to add `UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate` to the class interface.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Import UserNotifications
    import UserNotifications
    
    // Add UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate to the class interface
    class AppDelegate: UIResponder, UIApplicationDelegate, UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate {
      ...
    }
    
    
    #import <UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>
    #import "QGSdk.h"
      
    // Add UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate to the class interface
    @interface AppDelegate ()<UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate>
    
    @end
      
    @implementation AppDelegate
    
    ...
    
    @end

* * *

## 

3\. Request permission

Request users to grant permission to your app to send push notification by displaying a permission prompt. Users will be able to receive your app's push notifications after viewing the permission prompt and authorizing your app to send push notifications.

Include the code sample below somewhere within your app. You need to register for `userNotificationSettings` (for iOS 8 and iOS 9) or `requestAuthorization` (for iOS 10 and above).

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Registering Push Notification 
        if #available(iOS 10.0, *) {
          let center = UNUserNotificationCenter.current()
          center.delegate = self
          center.requestAuthorization(options: [.badge, .carPlay, .alert, .sound]) { (granted, error) in
            print("Granted: \(granted), Error: \(String(describing: error))")
          }
        } else {
          // Fallback on earlier versions - iOS 8 & 9
          let settings = UIUserNotificationSettings(types: [.alert, .badge, .sound], categories: nil)
          UIApplication.shared.registerUserNotificationSettings(settings)
        }
    
    
    // Registering Push Notification
      if (@available(iOS 10.0, *)) {
        UNAuthorizationOptions options = (UNAuthorizationOptions) (UNAuthorizationOptionAlert | UNAuthorizationOptionBadge | UNAuthorizationOptionSound | UNAuthorizationOptionCarPlay);
        UNUserNotificationCenter *center = [UNUserNotificationCenter currentNotificationCenter];
        center.delegate = self;
        [center requestAuthorizationWithOptions:options completionHandler:^(BOOL granted, NSError *error){
          NSLog(@"GRANTED: %i, Error: %@", granted, error);
        }];
      } else {
        // Fallback on earlier versions - iOS 8 & 9
        UIUserNotificationType types = UIUserNotificationTypeAlert | UIUserNotificationTypeSound |
        UIUserNotificationTypeBadge;
        UIUserNotificationSettings *settings = [UIUserNotificationSettings settingsForTypes:types categories:nil];
        [[UIApplication sharedApplication] registerUserNotificationSettings:settings];
      }

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> The iOS SDK offers an optional feature, "Provisional Push Notification," that allows you to silently deliver a trial push notification to iOS 12 users before asking for push permission. [More details](doc:provisional-push-notifications-in-ios-12)

* * *

## 

4\. Pass the push token to Appier

If the user grants permission for push notifications, a push token is generated from the APNs or FCM servers. Follow the steps for APNs or FCM below to pass the token to the Appier server.

### 

Option 1: For iOS apps using APNs

If your app is using APNs, copy the following methods and paste inside your `AppDelegate` class so that the application will pass the push token to the Appier server.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // add these delegate methods to your AppDelegate class
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken deviceToken: Data) {
      let QG = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
      print("My token is: \(deviceToken.description)")
      QG.setToken(deviceToken as Data)
    }
    
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didFailToRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithError error: Error) {
      print("Failed to get token, error: \(error.localizedDescription)")
    }
    
    
    // add these delegate methods to your AppDelegate class
    
    - (void)application:(UIApplication*)application didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:(NSData*)deviceToken
    {
      NSLog(@"My token is: %@", deviceToken);
      [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] setToken:deviceToken];
    }
    
    - (void)application:(UIApplication*)application didFailToRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithError:(NSError*)error
    {
      NSLog(@"Failed to get token, error: %@", error.localizedDescription);
    }

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> If you requested for a push token using `registerForRemoteNotification` before the Appier SDK is initialized, save the token and send it when you initialize the SDK.

### 

Option 2: For iOS apps using FCM

If your app is using FCM, follow the steps below.

  1. Add the `Firebase/Messaging` pod to your Podfile and install the pod. For more details on adding Firebase SDKs to your app, refer to the [Firebase documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging/ios/client#add-sdks).



Swift
    
    
    target 'PROJECT_TARGET' do
      ...
      
      // Add the pod for Firebase Cloud Messaging
      pod 'Firebase/Messaging'
    
    end

  2. Initialize Firebase in your app by importing the Firebase module in your `UIApplicationDelegate`.



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import Firebase
    
    
    @import Firebase;

  3. Configure a `FirebaseApp` shared instance, typically in your app's `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:` method.



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Use Firebase library to configure APIs
    FirebaseApp.configure()
    
    
    // Use Firebase library to configure APIs
    [FIRApp configure];

  4. Set the messaging delegate. Add `<FIRMessagingDelegate>` in your AppDelegate interface.



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    Messaging.messaging().delegate = self
    
    
    [FIRMessaging messaging].delegate = self;

  5. Pass the token to the Appier server using `setFCMToken()`.



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Use FIRMessagingDelegate
    // Firebase FCM subscribe to any topic
    func messaging(_ messaging: Messaging, didReceiveRegistrationToken fcmToken: String) {
        // TODO: If necessary send token to application server.
        // Note: This callback is fired at each app startup and whenever a new token is generated.
        print("Firebase registration token: \(fcmToken)")
        // Important for Appier
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().setFCMToken(fcmToken)
    }
    
    
    // Use FIRMessagingDelegate
    // Firebase FCM subscribe to any topic
    - (void)messaging:(FIRMessaging *)messaging didReceiveRegistrationToken:(NSString *)fcmToken {
        // TODO: If necessary send token to application server.
        // Note: This callback is fired at each app startup and whenever a new token is generated.
        NSLog(@"My FCM token is: %@", fcmToken);
        // Important for Appier
        [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] setFCMToken:fcmToken];
    }

* * *

## 

Checkpoint

  1. At this checkpoint, make sure your app builds correctly and run the app on a physical iOS device.
  2. When the app is launched, you should be prompted to subscribe to notifications.

# [iOS] Registering Push Notifications

To be able to send push notifications in iOS, you need to request permission from the user. If the user grants permission to receive push, a push notification token will be generated from the APNs or FCM servers and the token must be passed to the Appier server.

There are 4 steps required for registering push notifications. [Step 4](doc:registering-push-notifications-react-native#step-4-passing-push-token-to-appier-server) is different depending on the push notification service provider you are using.

  * [Option A] Using APNs
  * [Option B] Using Firebase Cloud Messaging: Firebase Native iOS SDK
  * [Option C] Using Firebase Cloud Messaging: React Native Firebase



If you are using Firebase Cloud Messaging, it is recommended to use Firebase Native iOS SDK.

* * *

## 

1\. Add relative frameworks

In the main app target, go to **Build Phases** and add the framework **UserNotifications**.

![](https://files.readme.io/4c3dcb8-Screen_Shot_2020-06-03_at_7.05.22_PM.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Including headers

In your class where you will handle the push notifications, preferably in the `AppDelegate` class,

  * For Swift, import `UserNotifications`.
  * For Objective-C, import `<UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>`.



You also need to add `UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate` to the class interface.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Import UserNotifications
    import UserNotifications
    
    // Add UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate to the class interface
    class AppDelegate: UIResponder, UIApplicationDelegate, UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate {
      ...
    }
    
    
    #import <UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>
    #import <Appier/Appier.h>
      
    // Add UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate to the class interface
    @interface AppDelegate ()<UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate>
    
    @end
      
    @implementation AppDelegate
    
    ...
    
    @end

* * *

## 

3\. Request permissions

You need to prompt the users to grant permission for sending push notifications.

Include the code sample below within your app’s `application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions` delegate method. They register for **userNotificationSettings** (for iOS 8 and iOS 9) or **requestAuthorization** (for iOS 10 and above).

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Registering Push Notification 
        if #available(iOS 10.0, *) {
          let center = UNUserNotificationCenter.current()
          center.delegate = self
          center.requestAuthorization(options: [.badge, .carPlay, .alert, .sound]) { (granted, error) in
            print("Granted: \(granted), Error: \(String(describing: error))")
          }
        } else {
          // Fallback on earlier versions - iOS 8 & 9
          let settings = UIUserNotificationSettings(types: [.alert, .badge, .sound], categories: nil)
          UIApplication.shared.registerUserNotificationSettings(settings)
        }
    
    
    // Registering Push Notification
      if (@available(iOS 10.0, *)) {
        UNAuthorizationOptions options = (UNAuthorizationOptions) (UNAuthorizationOptionAlert | UNAuthorizationOptionBadge | UNAuthorizationOptionSound | UNAuthorizationOptionCarPlay);
        UNUserNotificationCenter *center = [UNUserNotificationCenter currentNotificationCenter];
        center.delegate = self;
        [center requestAuthorizationWithOptions:options completionHandler:^(BOOL granted, NSError *error){
          NSLog(@"GRANTED: %i, Error: %@", granted, error);
        }];
      } else {
        // Fallback on earlier versions - iOS 8 & 9
        UIUserNotificationType types = UIUserNotificationTypeAlert | UIUserNotificationTypeSound |
        UIUserNotificationTypeBadge;
        UIUserNotificationSettings *settings = [UIUserNotificationSettings settingsForTypes:types categories:nil];
        [[UIApplication sharedApplication] registerUserNotificationSettings:settings];
      }

* * *

## 

4\. Passing the push token to Appier's servers

If the user grants your app permission to send push notifications, a push token will be generated by APNs or FCM . Follow the steps for one of the three options below to use APNs or FCM to pass the token to the Appier:

  * Option A: Using APNs
  * Option B: Using FCM with Firebase Native iOS SDK
  * Option C: Using FCM with React Native Firebase



### 

Option A: Using APNs

If your app is using APNs, copy the following methods and paste then inside your `AppDelegate` class the push token to the Appier's server.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // add these delegate methods to your AppDelegate class
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken deviceToken: Data) {
      let QG = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
      print("My token is: \(deviceToken.description)")
      QG.setToken(deviceToken as Data)
    }
    
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didFailToRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithError error: Error) {
      print("Failed to get token, error: \(error.localizedDescription)")
    }
    
    
    // add these delegate methods to your AppDelegate class
    
    - (void)application:(UIApplication*)application didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:(NSData*)deviceToken
    {
      NSLog(@"My token is: %@", deviceToken);
      [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] setToken:deviceToken];
    }
    
    - (void)application:(UIApplication*)application didFailToRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithError:(NSError*)error
    {
      NSLog(@"Failed to get token, error: %@", error.localizedDescription);
    }

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> If you requested for a push token using `registerForRemoteNotification` before the Appier SDK is initialized, save the token and send it when you initialize the SDK.

### 

Option B: Using FCM with Firebase Native iOS SDK

If your app is integrated with Firebase, follow the steps for [registering notifications for iOS apps using FCM](doc:registering-push-notifications-for-ios#option-2-for-ios-apps-using-fcm).

### 

Option C: Using FCM with React Native Firebase

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
>   * Users can only receive push notifications in the background if you are using React Native Firebase. See <https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/usage#message-handlers>.
>   * To integrate React Native Firebase, we recommended using React Native SDK 0.60.0 or later.
> 


  1. Complete the following setup steps as described in the React Native Firebase documentation:
     1. Complete the steps described in [Getting Started](https://rnfirebase.io/).
     2. Under the [Cloud Messaging](https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/usage) section, complete the instructions provided in the following pages (Note: Skip for "iOS Notification Images" to prevent conflicts with `AppierExtensionFramework`):
        1. [Usage](https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/usage). Install the following module versions:
           1. Dependencies
                  
                  "@react-native-firebase/app": "^15.6.0"
                  "@react-native-firebase/messaging": "^15.6.0"

        2. [iOS Project Setup](https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/usage/ios-setup)
        3. [iOS Permissions](https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/ios-permissions)
        4. (Optional) [Notifications](https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/notifications)
        5. (Optional) [Server Integration](https://rnfirebase.io/messaging/server-integration)
  2. Pass the token to Appier. In your app's `App.js` file, call `setFCMToken()` in two locations:



JavaScript
    
    
    import messaging from '@react-native-firebase/messaging';
    
    // Call setFCMToken()
    await messaging().registerDeviceForRemoteMessages();
    const fcmToken = await messaging().getToken();
    RNAiqua.setFCMToken(token);
    
    ...
    
    // Call setFCMToken()
    messaging().onTokenRefresh((token) => {
      RNAiqua.setFCMToken(token);
    });

* * *

## 

Checkpoint

  1. At this checkpoint, make sure your app builds correctly and run the app on a physical iOS device.
  2. When the app is launched, you should be prompted to subscribe to notifications.

# [iOS] Adding Required Extensions

A rich push notification is a push notification that includes an image, video, GIF, audio, carousel, or slider. With the release of iOS 10, `AppierFramework` and `AppierExtensionFramework` were introduced to support rich push notifications and notification UI customization.

This guide will explain how to set up the **Notification Service Extension** and **Notification Content Extension**. These extensions are required for:

  * Sending rich push notifications (notifications using creative types such as banners, carousels, and sliders)
  * Tracking impression events for all push notifications, regardless of the creative type used



* * *

## 

1\. Save your app group ID

The App Group ID will be used in your main app target as well as the two extension targets you'll create. The App Group ID must be the same ID used when you [enabled the App Group](doc:enabling-capabilities).

![](https://files.readme.io/6a42caf-step-1-1.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Add the extensions

  1. Add a notification service extension target. Under to **File > New > Target**, select **Notification Service Extension** , then click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/8551224-add-notification-service-extension.png)

  2. For **Product Name** , enter "AppierNotificationServiceExtension" and click **Finish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/7639c33-step-2-2.png)

  3. After clicking **Finish** , you'll be prompted to activate the "AppierNotificationServiceExtension" scheme. Select **Cancel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/de46031-do-not-use-scheme-appiernotificationserviceextension.png)

  4. Add a notification content extension target. In Xcode, navigate to **File > New > Target**, select **Notification Content Extension** , and click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/2ecf0b1-add-appier-notification-content-extension.png)

  5. For **Product Name** , enter "AppierNotificationContentExtension" and click **Finish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/a3d2394-step-2-5.png)

  6. After clicking **Finish** , you'll be prompted to activate the "AppierNotificationContentExtension" scheme. Select **Cancel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/5912710-do-not-use-scheme-appiernotificationcontentextension.png)

* * *

## 

3\. Install the extensions with CocoaPods

Add the following lines to your Flutter project's Podfile.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Latest bridged SDK version
> 
> Refer to the release notes corresponding to your Flutter SDK version to find the bridged iOS SDK version.
> 
>   * [Development Flutter SDK Versions](doc:flutter-sdk-release-notes)
>   * [Stable Flutter SDK Versions](doc:flutter-sdk-release-notes-stable)
> 


Podfile (Flutter)
    
    
    target 'Runner' do
      ...
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end
    
    target 'AppierNotificationServiceExtension' do
      use_frameworks!
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end
    
    target 'AppierNotificationContentExtension' do
      use_frameworks!
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end
    
    post_install do |installer|
      ...
    end

Ensure that the target names in the Podfile match the product names you used when creating the extensions (`AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`).

After adding the extensions to the Podfile, run the following commands in the `ios/` directory to install the extensions:

Shell
    
    
    $ pod repo update
    $ pod install

* * *

## 

4\. Set up the notification service extension

Modify your UNNotificationServiceExtension, then configure your Xcode project settings.

### 

1\. Modify UNNotificationServiceExtension

The required code changes depend on whether you're inherit the Appier SDK's notification service extension class, `QGNotificationService`, or if you want to customize UNNotificationServiceExtension.

If you're inheriting the Appier SDK’s UNNotificationServiceExtension (`QGNotificationService`), then open the `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` folder and replace the contents of the `NotificationService.*` files with the following:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // NotificationService.swift
    
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationService: QGNotificationService {
        override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
            super.didReceive(request, withContentHandler: contentHandler)
        }
        
        override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
            super.serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire()
        }
    }
    
    
    // NotificationService.h
    
    #import <UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>
    #import <AppierExtension/AppierExtension.h>
      
    @interface NotificationService : QGNotificationService
    @end
    
    
    
    // NotificationService.m
    
    #import "NotificationService.h"
      
    @implementation NotificationService
      
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler {
        [super didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:contentHandler];
    }
    
    - (void)serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire {
        [super serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire];
    }
    
    @end

Otherwise, if you're using a custom UNNotificationServiceExtension implementation, override the following methods:

  * Swift: `didReceive(_:withContentHandler:)` and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire()`
  * Objective-C: `didReceiveNotificationRequest:withContentHandler:` and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire`



The following code sample demonstrates one way to override the appropriate methods in your notification extension:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationService: UNNotificationService {
      
      var contentHandler: (UNNotificationContent) -> Void
      var bestAttemptContent: UNMutableNotificationContent
      
      override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
        self.bestAttemptContent = request.content.mutableCopy() as! UNMutableNotificationContent
        self.contentHandler = contentHandler
        
        let isAppierPush = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).isAppierPush(request.content.userInfo)
        if isAppierPush {
          QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).didReceive(request) { content in
            contentHandler(content);
          }
        }
      }
      
      override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
        let isAppierPush = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).isAppierPush(self.bestAttemptContent.userInfo)
        if isAppierPush {
          self.contentHandler(self.bestAttemptContent)
        }
      }
    }
    
    
    @interface NotificationService ()
    
    @property (nonatomic, strong) void (^contentHandler)(UNNotificationContent *contentToDeliver);
    @property (nonatomic, strong) UNMutableNotificationContent *bestAttemptContent;
    
    @end
    
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler
    {
        self.contentHandler = contentHandler;
        self.bestAttemptContent = [request.content mutableCopy];
    
        BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] isAppierPush:request.content.userInfo];
        if (isAppierPush) {
            [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:^(UNNotificationContent *content){
                contentHandler(content);
            }];
        }
    }
    
    - (void)serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire
    {
        BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] isAppierPush:self.bestAttemptContent.userInfo];
        if (isAppierPush) {
            self.contentHandler(self.bestAttemptContent);
        }
    }

### 

2\. Configure your Xcode project settings

  1. Go to the project navigator and select the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** target.  
Navigate to **Signing & Capabilities** > **App Groups** , and then add the app group using your App Group ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/e02b7a5-step-4-2.png)

  2. In the project navigator, select the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** target. Under the **General** tab, change the deployment target of your content extension to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/cf8eb81-step-4-3.png)

  3. Find the `Info.plist` file in the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** folder. Add the following row under **Information Property List** :



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppGroup`| String| Your App Group ID  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/f1f32f5-step-4-4.png)

* * *

## 

5\. Set up the notification content extension

  1. In the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** folder, open the following files and replace the contents of the entire file with the following:



**For Swift:** `NotificationViewController.swift`

NotificationViewController.swift
    
    
    import UIKit
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationViewController: QGNotificationContentViewController {
      override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        // Do any required interface initialization here.
      }
    }

  2. Go to the project navigator and select the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** target.  
Navigate to **Signing & Capabilities** > **App Groups** , and then add the app group using your App Group ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/c4758a9-step-5-2.png)

  3. In the project navigator, select the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** target. Under the **General** tab, change the deployment target of your content extension to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/67e428b-step-5-3.png)

  4. Find the `Info.plist` file in the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** folder. Under **NSExtension > NSExtensionAttributes**, update `UNNotificationExtensionCategory` and add `UNNotificationExtensionDefaultContentHidden` and `UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled` with the following values:



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`UNNotificationExtensionDefaultContentHidden`| Boolean| `YES` or `1`  
`UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled`| Boolean| `YES` or `1`  
`UNNotificationExtensionCategory`| String| `QGCAROUSEL`  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/ea78867-step-5-4.png)

  5. Add the following row under **Information Property List** :



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppGroup`| String| Your App Group ID  
  
`Info.plist` for **AppierNotificationContentExtension** should look like this:

![](https://files.readme.io/dca2e7d-step-5-5.png)

  6. In `MainInterface.storyboard`, remove the default **Label**.

![](https://files.readme.io/dd7b8b1-UI_Label.png)

  7. In `MainInterface.storyboard`, select **View** and change the Background to **System Grouped Background Color**.

![](https://files.readme.io/18f37f9-step-5-7.png)

## 

6\. Send a test push notification

Build the target and follow the instructions in [Sending Test Notification for iOS](doc:test-notification-for-ios) to verify that the rich push notification works as expected.

* * *

## 

Troubleshooting

See the troubleshooting steps below if you encounter issues sending notifications.

  * Ensure that the deployment target of `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension` is set to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/e66aa46-troubleshooting-0.png)

  * Remove `-ObjC/$(inherited)` if it exists in the build settings of the `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`.

  * Ensure that the same App Group ID is used in all three targets.


![](https://files.readme.io/10d571e-troubleshooting-1.png)

  * Under the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets, go to **Build Phases > Compile Sources** to make sure the following files are correctly configured. If not, click **+** to add the files.

![1924](https://files.readme.io/babf7a7-Screen_Shot_2020-12-01_at_3.10.25_PM.png)

AppierNotificationServiceExtension Compile Sources

![1928](https://files.readme.io/2d442d3-Screen_Shot_2020-12-01_at_3.10.32_PM.png)

AppierNotificationContentExtension Compile Sources
