# [iOS] Adding Required Extensions

## 

Overview

A rich push notification is a push notification that includes an image, video, GIF, audio, carousel, or slider. With the release of iOS 10, `AppierFramework` and `AppierExtensionFramework` were introduced to support rich push notifications and notification UI customization.

This guide will explain how to set up the **Notification Service Extension** and **Notification Content Extension**. These extensions are required for:

  * Sending rich push notifications (notifications using creative types such as banners, carousels, and sliders)
  * Tracking impression events for all push notifications, regardless of the creative type used



### 

SDK version requirement

We recommend using **Appier React Native SDK 1.5 or later**. Follow the [migration steps](doc:ios-sdk-migration-for-react-native) to upgrade from version 1.4. If you're using an earlier version, please note the following:

  * If you are using a new App Group ID, ensure that you are using **Appier React Native SDK 1.5** or later, otherwise iOS users will be duplicated.
  * Starting from **Appier React Native SDK 1.5** , `AppierExtensionFramework` is used in the main app target, the Notification Service Extension target, and the Notification Content Extension target.



* * *

## 

1\. Save your app group ID

> ❗️
> 
> ### 
> 
> Caution: Using a New App Group ID
> 
> Ensure that you're using the proper SDK version if you need to use a new App Group ID to avoid unwanted side effects.

The App Group ID will be used in your main app target as well as the two extension targets you'll create. The App Group ID must be the same ID used when you [enabled the App Group](doc:enabling-capabilities).

![](https://files.readme.io/b86ff42-step-1-1.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Add the extensions

  1. Add a notification service extension target. Under to **File > New > Target**, select **Notification Service Extension** , then click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/8551224-add-notification-service-extension.png)

  2. For **Product Name** , enter "AppierNotificationServiceExtension" and click **Finish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/d120ed7-step-2-2.png)

  3. After clicking **Finish** , you'll be prompted to activate the "AppierNotificationServiceExtension" scheme. Select **Cancel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/de46031-do-not-use-scheme-appiernotificationserviceextension.png)

  4. Add a notification content extension target. In Xcode, navigate to **File > New > Target**, select **Notification Content Extension** , and click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/2ecf0b1-add-appier-notification-content-extension.png)

  5. For **Product Name** , enter "AppierNotificationContentExtension" and click **Finish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/ae59780-step-2-5.png)

  6. After clicking **Finish** , you'll be prompted to activate the "AppierNotificationContentExtension" scheme. Select **Cancel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/5912710-do-not-use-scheme-appiernotificationcontentextension.png)

* * *

## 

3\. Install the extensions

Choose an installation method depending on your project settings:

  * **Option 1: Swift Package Manager**
  * **Option 2:Installing with CocoaPods**
  * **Option 3:Installing with React Native Firebase**
  * **Option 4:Manual Installation (Not Recommended)**



### 

Swift Package Manager

No additional steps required; continue to the next step.

### 

Installing with CocoaPods

Add the following lines to your project's Podfile:

Podfile (React Native)
    
    
    target 'PROJECT_TARGET' do
      ...
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<LATEST_BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
      # other pods
    en
    
    # Add the following lines for service and content extensions
    target 'AppierNotificationServiceExtension' do
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<LATEST_BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end
    
    target 'AppierNotificationContentExtension' do
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<LATEST_BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end

Ensure that the target names in the Podfile match the product names you used when creating the extensions (`AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`).

After adding the extensions to the Podfile, run the following commands in the project directory to install the extensions:

Shell
    
    
    $ pod repo update
    $ pod install

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Upgrading the React Native SDK
> 
> When upgrading the React Native SDK, check the relevant [release notes](doc:react-native-sdk-release-notes) to see whether the bridged iOS SDK version was updated. If the bridged iOS SDK version was updated, you'll also need to update the version of `AppierExtensionFramework` in your Podfile to match the iOS SDK version.

### 

Installing with React Native Firebase

Add the following lines to your project's Podfile:

Podfile (React Native)
    
    
    target 'PROJECT_TARGET' do
      ...
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<LATEST_BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
      # other pods
    end
    
    target 'ServiceExtension' do
      use_frameworks! :linkage => :static
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<LATEST_BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end
    
    target 'ContentExtension' do
      use_frameworks! :linkage => :static
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<LATEST_BRIDGED_IOS_SDK_VERSION>'
    end

After adding the extensions to the Podfile, run the following commands in the project directory to install the extensions:

Shell
    
    
    $ pod repo update
    $ pod install

### 

Manual installation (Not recommended)

> ❗️
> 
> ### 
> 
> Warning
> 
> Don't follow the manual installation steps if your project uses CocoaPods or Swift Package Manager (SPM) for package management.

  1. [Download the Appier iOS SDK](doc:ios-sdk-integration-overview).
  2. Add the `AppierExtension.xcframework` folder you downloaded to the main app target. Under the **Build Phases** tab, expand **Link Binary With Libraries** , and click **+**. Go to **Add Other > Add Files** and select the `AppierExtension.xcframework` folder.

![827](https://files.readme.io/6593dc4-Screen_Shot_2021-09-15_at_12.40.08_PM.png)

Add the AppierExtension.xcframework folder to the main app target.

  3. Add the `AppierExtension.xcframework` folder to the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets.

![883](https://files.readme.io/8e7e76a-Screen_Shot_2020-08-27_at_2.12.13_PM.png)

Add the AppierExtension.xcframework folder to the AppierNotificationServiceExtension and AppierNotificationContentExtension targets.

  4. In the main app target, go to **General > Frameworks and Libraries**, select `AppierExtension.xcframework`, and set the **Embed** column to **Embed & Sign**.

![](https://files.readme.io/3d26c88-manual-installation_main_app_target_embed_setting.png)

  5. In the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets, go to **General > Frameworks and Libraries**, then set the **Embed** columns of `AppierNotificationServiceExtension.xcframework` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension.xcframework` to **Do Not Embed**.

![](https://files.readme.io/4563f00-manual-installation_notification_extension_target_embed_settings.png)

* * *

## 

4\. Set up the notification service extension

Modify your UNNotificationServiceExtension, then configure your Xcode project settings.

### 

1\. Modify UNNotificationServiceExtension

The required code changes depend on whether you're inherit the Appier SDK's notification service extension class, `QGNotificationService`, or if you want to customize UNNotificationServiceExtension.

If you're inheriting the Appier SDK’s UNNotificationServiceExtension (`QGNotificationService`), then open the `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` folder and replace the contents of the `NotificationService.*` files with the following:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // NotificationService.swift
    
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationService: QGNotificationService {
        override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
            super.didReceive(request, withContentHandler: contentHandler)
        }
        
        override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
            super.serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire()
        }
    }
    
    
    // NotificationService.h
    
    #import <UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>
    #import <AppierExtension/AppierExtension.h>
      
    @interface NotificationService : QGNotificationService
    @end
    
    
    
    // NotificationService.m
    
    #import "NotificationService.h"
      
    @implementation NotificationService
      
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler {
        [super didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:contentHandler];
    }
    
    - (void)serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire {
        [super serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire];
    }
    
    @end

Otherwise, if you're using a custom UNNotificationServiceExtension implementation, override the following methods:

  * Swift: `didReceive(_:withContentHandler:)` and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire()`
  * Objective-C: `didReceiveNotificationRequest:withContentHandler:` and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire`



The following code sample demonstrates one way to override the appropriate methods in your notification extension:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationService: UNNotificationService {
      
      var contentHandler: (UNNotificationContent) -> Void
      var bestAttemptContent: UNMutableNotificationContent
      
      override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
        self.bestAttemptContent = request.content.mutableCopy() as! UNMutableNotificationContent
        self.contentHandler = contentHandler
        
        let isAppierPush = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).isAppierPush(request.content.userInfo)
        if isAppierPush {
          QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).didReceive(request) { content in
            contentHandler(content);
          }
        }
      }
      
      override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
        let isAppierPush = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).isAppierPush(self.bestAttemptContent.userInfo)
        if isAppierPush {
          self.contentHandler(self.bestAttemptContent)
        }
      }
    }
    
    
    @interface NotificationService ()
    
    @property (nonatomic, strong) void (^contentHandler)(UNNotificationContent *contentToDeliver);
    @property (nonatomic, strong) UNMutableNotificationContent *bestAttemptContent;
    
    @end
    
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler
    {
        self.contentHandler = contentHandler;
        self.bestAttemptContent = [request.content mutableCopy];
    
        BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] isAppierPush:request.content.userInfo];
        if (isAppierPush) {
            [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:^(UNNotificationContent *content){
                contentHandler(content);
            }];
        }
    }
    
    - (void)serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire
    {
        BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] isAppierPush:self.bestAttemptContent.userInfo];
        if (isAppierPush) {
            self.contentHandler(self.bestAttemptContent);
        }
    }

### 

2\. Configure your Xcode project settings

  1. Go to the project navigator and select the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** target.  
Navigate to **Signing & Capabilities** > **App Groups** , and then add the app group using your App Group ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/c3ed69a-step-4-2.png)

  2. In the project navigator, select the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** target. Under the **General** tab, change the deployment target of your service extension to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/47d4f32-step-4-3.png)

  3. Find the `Info.plist` file in the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** folder. Add the following row under **Information Property List** :



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppGroup`| String| Your App Group ID  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/f1f32f5-step-4-4.png)   


* * *

## 

5\. Set up the Notification Content Extension

  1. In the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** folder, open the following files and replace the contents of the entire file with the following:



**For Swift:** `NotificationViewController.swift`

NotificationViewController.swift
    
    
    import UIKit
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationViewController: QGNotificationContentViewController {
      override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        // Do any required interface initialization here.
      }
    }

**For Objective-C:** `NotificationViewController.h` and `NotificationViewController.m`

NotificationViewController.hNotificationViewController.m
    
    
    #import <UIKit/UIKit.h>
    #import <AppierExtension/AppierExtension.h>
      
    @interface NotificationViewController : QGNotificationContentViewController
    @end
    
    
    #import "NotificationViewController.h"
      
    @implementation NotificationViewController
      
    - (void)viewDidLoad {
        [super viewDidLoad];
    }
    
    @end

  2. Go to the project navigator and select the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** target.  
Navigate to **Signing & Capabilities** > **App Groups** , and then add the app group using your App Group ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/ac08265-step-5-2.png)

  3. In the project navigator, select the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** target. Under the **General** tab, change the deployment target of your content extension to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/d8d1183-step-5-3.png)

  4. Find the `Info.plist` file in the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** folder. Under **NSExtension > NSExtensionAttributes**, update `UNNotificationExtensionCategory` and add `UNNotificationExtensionDefaultContentHidden` and `UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled` with the following values:



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`UNNotificationExtensionDefaultContentHidden`| Boolean| `YES` or `1`  
`UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled`| Boolean| `YES` or `1`  
`UNNotificationExtensionCategory`| String| `QGCAROUSEL`  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/ea78867-step-5-4.png)

  5. Add the following row under **Information Property List** :



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppGroup`| String| Your App Group ID  
  
`Info.plist` for **AppierNotificationContentExtension** should look like this:

![](https://files.readme.io/5db3a3c-step-5-5.png)

  6. In `MainInterface.storyboard`, remove the default **Label**.

![](https://files.readme.io/dd7b8b1-UI_Label.png)

  7. In `MainInterface.storyboard`, select **View** and change the Background to **System Grouped Background Color**.

![](https://files.readme.io/18f37f9-step-5-7.png)

## 

Send a test push notification

Build the target and follow the instructions in [Sending Test Notification for iOS](doc:test-notification-for-ios) to verify that the rich push notification works as expected.

* * *

## 

Troubleshooting

See the troubleshooting steps below if you encounter issues sending notifications.

  * Ensure that the deployment target of `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension` is set to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/8b7e033-troubleshooting-0.png)

  * Remove `-ObjC/$(inherited)` if it exists in the build settings of the `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`.

  * Ensure that the same App Group ID is used in all three targets.


![](https://files.readme.io/10d571e-troubleshooting-1.png)

  * Under the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets, go to **Build Phases > Compile Sources** to make sure the following files are correctly configured. If not, click **+** to add the files.

![1924](https://files.readme.io/babf7a7-Screen_Shot_2020-12-01_at_3.10.25_PM.png)

AppierNotificationServiceExtension Compile Sources

![1928](https://files.readme.io/2d442d3-Screen_Shot_2020-12-01_at_3.10.32_PM.png)

AppierNotificationContentExtension Compile Sources

 __Updated 9 months ago

# Android SDK Dependencies

Set up your Android project with the required dependencies.

Refer to this page for the required Appier SDK dependencies to ensure a smooth integration and maintain compatibility with the latest Android and Firebase libraries.

  * Repository configuration
  * Dependencies for development SDK versions (8.x.x)
  * Dependencies for stable SDK versions (7.x.x)
  * Troubleshooting common issues



* * *

## 

Repository configuration

In your project-level `build.gradle`, add the required repositories under `allprojects > repositories` to ensure Appier SDK dependencies can be resolved in all of your project's modules.

build.gradle
    
    
    allprojects {
        repositories {
            google()
            mavenCentral()
        }
    }

* * *

## 

Dependencies for development SDK versions (8.x.x)

### 

Appier SDK dependencies

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation 'androidx.appcompat:appcompat:1.4.2'
    implementation 'androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-livedata-core:2.3.1'
    implementation "androidx.recyclerview:recyclerview:1.2.1"
    implementation "com.android.installreferrer:installreferrer:2.2"
    implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads-identifier:18.2.0'
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:23.0.0'
    implementation('io.socket:socket.io-client:2.1.2') {
      // excluding org.json which is provided by Android
      exclude group: 'org.json', module: 'json'
    }
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib:1.8.22'
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-reflect:1.8.22'
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.5.0'
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-android:1.5.0'

### 

Firebase dependencies

Development Appier SDK versions (8.x.x) have the following Firebase dependencies:

Firebase module| Required version  
---|---  
`firebase-bom`| 26.0.0 or later  
`firebase-messaging`| 21.0.0 or later  
  
#### 

`firebase-bom`

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation('com.appier:appier-android:<8.x.x>') {
        exclude group: 'com.google.firebase'
    }
    // Replace <YOUR VERSION NUMBER> with the Firebase version your project uses (26.0.0 or later)
    implementation(platform('com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:<YOUR VERSION NUMBER>'))
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging'

#### 

`firebase-messaging`

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation('com.appier:appier-android:<8.x.x>') {
      exclude group: 'com.google.firebase'
    }
    // Replace <YOUR VERSION NUMBER> with the Firebase version your project uses (21.0.0 or later)
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:<YOUR VERSION NUMBER>'

* * *

## 

Dependencies for stable SDK versions (7.x.x)

### 

Appier SDK dependencies

buid.gradle
    
    
    implementation 'androidx.appcompat:appcompat:1.4.2'
    implementation 'androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-livedata-core:2.3.1'
    implementation "androidx.recyclerview:recyclerview:1.2.1"
    implementation "com.android.installreferrer:installreferrer:2.2"
    implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads-identifier:18.0.1'
    implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-location:21.3.0'
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.0.1'
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:20.0.1'
    implementation('io.socket:socket.io-client:1.0.2') {
        // excluding org.json which is provided by Android
        exclude group: 'org.json', module: 'json'
    }
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib:1.8.22'
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-reflect:1.8.22'
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.5.0'
    implementation 'org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-android:1.5.0'

### 

Firebase dependencies

Stable Appier SDK versions (7.x.x) have the following Firebase dependencies:

Firebase module| Required version  
---|---  
`firebase-bom`| • 24.7.0 or earlier  
• 26.0.0 or later (without `firebase-messaging` and `firebase-iid`)  
`firebase-iid`| 20.1.0 or earlier  
`firebase-messaging`| 20.1.0 or earlier  
  
#### 

`firebase-bom`

If your app uses `firebase-bom:24.7.0` or earlier:

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation('com.appier:appier-android:<7.x.x>') {
        exclude group: 'com.google.firebase'
    }
    // Replace <YOUR VERSION NUMBER> with the Firebase version your project uses (24.7.0 or earlier)
    implementation(platform('com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:<YOUR VERSION NUMBER>'))
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging'
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid'

If your app uses `firebase-bom:26.0.0` or later (without `firebase-messaging` and `firebase-iid`):

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation('com.appier:appier-android:<7.x.x>')
    // Replace <YOUR VERSION NUMBER> with the Firebase version your project uses (26.0.0 or later)
    implementation(platform('com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:<YOUR VERSION NUMBER>')) {
        exclude group: 'com.google.firebase', module: 'firebase-messaging'
        exclude group: 'com.google.firebase', module: 'firebase-iid'
    }
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:20.1.0'
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.1.0'

#### 

`firebase-iid`

`firebase-iid` is typically included with `firebase-messaging` as a transitive dependency.

However, if you encounter a `java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Failed resolution of: Lcom/google/firebase/iid/FirebaseInstanceId;` error, add the module explicitly in `build.gradle`:

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.1.0'

#### 

`firebase-messaging`

build.gradle
    
    
    implementation('com.appier:appier-android:<7.x.x>') {
        exclude group: 'com.google.firebase'
    }
    // Replace <YOUR VERSION NUMBER> with the Firebase version your project uses
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:20.1.0'
    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:<YOUR VERSION NUMBER>' // 20.1.0 or earlier

* * *

## 

Troubleshooting common errors

Error| Description| Troubleshooting  
---|---|---  
`DuplicatePlatformClasses`| Conflicting library versions.| Exclude the SDK's dependency and declare your own.  
`ClassNotFoundException`| Missing Maven repository.| Ensure your repository configuration is correct.

# Recommendation (Android SDK)

Get recommendations and track scenario performance.

## 

Prerequisites

Before using the API methods to fetch product recommendations, complete the following:

  1. Complete the [required setup](doc:using-the-android-sdk) for the Appier Android SDK.
  2. [Create a recommendation scenario](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20).
  3. [Retrieve the `scenarioId`](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#perform-scenario-operations) for the recommendation scenario.



In addition, the [status of the scenario](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#monitor-scenario-status) must be **Ready** , indicating that the recommendation model has completed training, before recommendation results can be retrieved.

* * *

## 

Fetching recommendations

### 

(Recommended) With `productId`

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * The product ID you pass into the request must match the product ID specified in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed)
>   * `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()` with the `productId` parameter is only supported in Android SDK 6.5.1 or later
> 


Java
    
    
    /**
    * Recommendation v2
    * Get Recommendation data using a Scenario created in your dashboard
    * and using some optional query parameters. If the ScenarioId is null
    * or invalid, the response of the Completion callback will be null.
    *
    * @param scenarioId ScenarioId for the scenario created
    * @param productId productId for the query
    * @param queryParameters filter condition or other query parameters
    * @param completion Completion callback with the recommendation data
    */
    public void getRecommendationWithScenarioId(String scenarioId,
                                                String productId,
                                            JSONObject queryParameters,
                                     CompletionHandler completion)

### 

Without `productId`

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()` without the `productId` parameters is only supported in Android SDK 6.5.0 or later.

Java
    
    
    /**
    * Recommendation v2
    * Get Recommendation data using a Scenario created in your dashboard
    * and using some optional query parameters. If the ScenarioId is null
    * or invalid, the response of the Completion callback will be null.
    *
    * @param scenarioId ScenarioId for the scenario created
    * @param queryParameters productId as pid or filter condition or other query parameters
    * @param completion Completion callback with the recommendation data
    */
    public void getRecommendationWithScenarioId(String scenarioId,
                                            JSONObject queryParameters,
                                     CompletionHandler completion)

### 

(Deprecated) Returning recommended products only

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Deprecated
> 
> This method is deprecated—we recommend using `getRecomendationWithScenarioId()` with the `productId` parameter.

This method returns a single `JSONArray` containing the recommended products. Fields required for tracking click events (`scenarioId`, `modelId`, and `recId`) on recommended products aren't included in the response.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> This version of `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()` is only supported in Android SDK 6.1.0 or later.

Java
    
    
    /**
    * Recommendation v2
    * Get Recommendation data using a Scenario created in your dashboard
    * and using some optional query parameters. If the ScenarioId is null
    * or invalid, the response of the Completion callback will be null.
    *
    * @param scenarioId ScenarioId for the scenario created
    * @param queryParameters product Id as pid or filter condition or other query parameters
    * @param completion Completion callback with the recommendation data
    *
    * @deprecated reason this method is deprecated <br/>
    *         use {@link #getRecommendationWithScenarioId(String, JSONObject, CompletionHandler)} instead
    */
    @Deprecated
    public void getRecommendationWithScenarioId(String scenarioId,
                                            JSONObject queryParameters,
                                            Completion completion)

* * *

## 

Example usage (with `productId`)

The following example uses the recommended method of retrieving recommendation results: `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()` with the `productId` parameter.

### 

Parameters

  * `scenarioId`: The scenario ID of the recommendation scenario retrieved from the AIQUA Dashboard.
  * `productId`: Required by some recommendation models. See the [recommendation model reference](doc:recommendation-models#model-reference) for a list of all models and the data they require.
  * `queryParameters`: A JSON object containing optional query parameters.
  * `completion`: The completion handler that will handle the response.



#### 

`queryParameters`

`queryParameters` is a JSON object containing optional query parameters that you can use to specify what type of recommendation results you want to receive.

  * `user_id`: Required to [filter results based on a user's activity](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#exclusion-rules).
  * `num`: Specifies the maximum number of recommended products to be returned. If the number of available products is less than `num`, all available products will be returned. The default value is 20 and the maximum value is 50.
  * `filter`: An object containing filtering rules to be applied to recommendation results. In the following example, only products with a product category equal to "3C > Mobile" will be returned. To learn more about creating recommendation filters, see [Product Filter Rules](doc:filtering-recommendation-results#api-calls).



JSON
    
    
    {
      "version": 2,
      "filterRule": {
        "operator": "OR",
        "ruleList": [
          {
            "operator": "AND",
            "conditionList": [
              {
                "key": "category",
                "value": [
                  "3C > Mobile"
                ],
                "operator": "in",
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }

#### 

`completion`

`completion` is the `CompletionHandler` you've implemented to handle recommendation responses.

### 

Sample request

JavaKotlin
    
    
    String scenarioId = "<SCENARIO_ID>";
    String productId = "<PRODUCT_ID>";
    JSONObject queryParameters = new JSONObject();
    try {
        // Example filter string
        String filterString = "{\"version\":2,\"filterRule\":{\"operator\":\"OR\",\"ruleList\":[{\"operator\":\"AND\",\"conditionList\":[{\"key\":\"category\",\"value\":[\"3C > Mobile\"],\"operator\":\"in\"}]}]}}";
        JSONObject filter = new JSONObject(filterString);
        queryParameters.put("num", 3);
        queryParameters.put("user_id", "<USER_ID>");
        queryParameters.put("filter", filter);
    } catch (JSONException e) {
        Log.e(LOG_TAG, "Generate JSON query exception", e);
    }
    
    QG.getInstance(mContext).getRecommendationWithScenarioId(
            scenarioId,
            productId,
            queryParameters,
            new CompletionHandler() {
                @Override
                public void onComplete(JSONObject response) {
                    if (response != null) {
                        Log.d(LOG_TAG, "Recommendation response: " + response.toString());
                    } else {
                        Log.d(LOG_TAG, "Recommendation response: null response");
                    }
                }
            });
    
    
    val scenarioId = "<SCENARIO_ID>"
    val productId = "<PRODUCT_ID>"
    val queryParameters = JSONObject()
    try {
        // Example filter string
        val filterString = """
            {
              "version": 2,
              "filterRule": {
                "operator": "OR",
                "ruleList": [
                  {
                    "operator": "AND",
                    "conditionList": [
                      {
                        "key": "category",
                        "value": [
                          "3C > Mobile"
                        ],
                        "operator": "in"
                      }
                    ]
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val filter = JSONObject(filterString)
        queryParameters.put("num", 3)
        queryParameters.put("user_id", "<USER_ID>")
        queryParameters.put("filter", filter)
    } catch (e: JSONException) {
        Log.e(LOG_TAG, "Generate JSON query exception", e)
    }
    
    QG.getInstance(context).getRecommendationWithScenarioId(
        scenarioId,
        productId,
        queryParameters,
        (CompletionHandler { response: JSONObject? ->
            if (response != null) {
                Log.d(LOG_TAG, response.toString())
            } else {
                Log.d(LOG_TAG, "null response")
            }
        })
    )

### 

Sample response

JSON
    
    
    {
      "items": [
        {
          "productId": "TEST_SKU_16",
          "position": 2,
          "image": "<IMAGE_URL>",
          "title": "Mobile_16",
          "description": "hTC",
          "customLabel00": "Foo’s bar",
          "customLabel01": "false",
          "customLabel02": "-10",
          "customLabel03": "200.65",
          "customLabel04": "",
          "url": "<PRODUCT_URL>",
          "category": "3C > Mobile",
          "currency": "TWD",
          "price": "5999",
          "originalPrice": "5999",
          "order": "PRIMARY"
          ... // optional fields are not listed
        }
        ...
      ],
      "recId": "8c4d2657-5a0e-4b77-aa25-e22fa5ba5633",
      "scenarioId": "Aj2MMx5KHzPau2pv4aQ26i",
      "modelId": "5",
      "expType": "normal",
      "respCode": "1000",
      ...
    }

  * `recId`, `scenarioId`, `modelId`, and `productId`: These IDs are used to track clicks on recommended products.
  * `items`: An array containing the recommendation results.



* * *

## 

Tracking clicks and impressions

To track scenario clicks and impressions, your app must use Android SDK 6.5.1 or later.

### 

Tracking clicks

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Conversion tracking
> 
> To track conversions using the [**Item Conversion**](doc:recommendations-20-analytics#conversion-definitions) definition, events must include the `product_id` parameter.

To log click events on recommended products, call `logRecommendationClicked()` with the parameters obtained from the recommendation response (`scenarioId`, `modelId`, `productId`, and `recId`).

JavaKotlin
    
    
    public void logRecommendationClicked(String scenarioId, String modelId, String productId, String recommendationId)
    
    
    fun logRecommendationClicked(scenarioId: String, modelId: String, productId: String, recommendationId: String)

The following example demonstrates how to log a click event for a recommended product.

JavaKotlin
    
    
    try {
        String scenarioId = response.getString("scenarioId");
        String modelId = response.getString("modelId");
        String recId = response.getString("recId");
        JSONArray items = response.getJSONArray("items");
        JSONObject product = items.getJSONObject(index);
        String productId = product.getString("productId");
        QG.getInstance(context).logRecommendationClicked(scenarioId, modelId, productId, recId);
    } catch (JSONException e) {
        Log.e(LOG_TAG, "JSON query exception", e);
    }
    
    
    try {
        val scenarioId = response.getString("scenarioId")
        val modelId = response.getString("modelId")
        val recId = response.getString("recId")
        val items = response.getJSONArray("items")
        val product = items.getJSONObject(index)
        val productId = product.getString("productId")
        getInstance(context).logRecommendationClicked(scenarioId, modelId, productId, recId)
    } catch (e: JSONException) {
        Log.e(LOG_TAG, "JSON query exception", e)
    }

### 

Tracking impressions

The SDK logs a `recommendation_impression` event whenever a non-empty recommendation response is successfully received, regardless of the number of recommended products contained in the response.

# Recommendation (iOS SDK)

Get recommendations and track scenario performance.

## 

Prerequisites

Before using the API methods to fetch product recommendations, complete the following:

  1. Complete the [required setup](doc:using-the-android-sdk) for the Appier iOS SDK.
  2. [Create a recommendation scenario](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20).
  3. [Retrieve the `scenarioId`](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#perform-scenario-operations) for the recommendation scenario.



In addition, the [status of the scenario](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#monitor-scenario-status) must be **Ready** , indicating that the recommendation model has completed training, before recommendation results can be retrieved.

* * *

## 

Fetching recommendations

### 

(Recommended) With `productId`

Here, `productId` can be directly passed as a parameter to get more precise recommendation. However, this `productId` is an optional parameter and can be passed as `nil` if required. Refer to the sample response below for detailed spec.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * The product ID you pass into the request must match the product ID specified in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed)
>   * `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()` with the `productId` parameter is only supported in iOS SDK 7.5.0 and later
> 


Objective-C
    
    
    /*!
     @abstract
     Returns recommendation data with 2.0 url for the user with scenario Id,  product Id and query parameters
    */
    - (void)getRecommendationWithScenarioId:(NSString *)scenarioId
                              withProductId:(NSString *)productId
                        withQueryParameters:(NSDictionary * _Nullable)queryStringDict
                      withCompletionHandler:(void (^)(id _Nullable response))completion;

### 

Without `productId`

This method can be used similar to the first method but it does not have `productId` parameter. It is recommended to use method 1 above in all the use cases.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> This method is supported in iOS SDK versions 7.4.0 and above.

Recommendation 2.0
    
    
    /*!
     @abstract
     Returns recommendation data with 2.0 url for the user with scenario Id and query parameters
    */
    - (void)getRecommendationWithScenarioId:(NSString *)scenarioId 
                        withQueryParameters:(NSDictionary * _Nullable)queryStringDict 
                      withCompletionHandler:(void (^)(id _Nullable response))completion;

* * *

## 

Example usage

### 

Sample request

Below is a sample request using method 1 above with `productId` and category `filter`.

  * Use the scenario ID generated on AIQUA dashboard.
  * `user_id`: required to [filter results based on a user's activity](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#exclusion-rules).
  * `productId`: required for some recommendation models. See the [recommendation model reference](doc:recommendation-models#model-reference) for a list of all models and the data they require.
  * `filter`: An object containing filtering rules to be applied to recommendation results. In the following example, only products with a product category equal to "3C > Mobile" will be returned. To learn more about creating recommendation filters, see [Product Filter Rules](doc:filtering-recommendation-results#api-calls).
  * `num`: Use to specify the maximum number of the recommended products that can be returned.  
If the number of available products is less than `num`, all available products will be returned. The maximum of `num` is 50. If `num` is larger than 50, 50 products will be returned at most. If `num` is not specified, the default is 20 products.



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let parameters: [String:Any] = [
        "num": 10,
        "user_id": "9afdf84f-1d55", // Required if filtering purchased product based on user_id
        "filter": [
            "version": 2, // Required
            "filterRule": [
                "operator": "OR",
                "ruleList": [
                    [
                        "operator": "OR",
                        "conditionList": [
                            [
                                "key": "category",
                                "value": [
                                    "3C > Mobile"
                                ],
                                "operator": "in"
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
    
    let scenarioId = "2t7koCuCDGqBtLMxXXXXXX"
    let productId = "SKU_12435"
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().getRecommendationWithScenarioId(scenarioId, withProductId:productId, withQueryParameters: parameters, withCompletionHandler: { response in
        if response != nil {
            // Process response here
        }
    })
    
    
    NSDictionary *parameters = @{
        @"num": @10,
        @"user_id": @"9afdf84f-1d55", // Required if filtering purchased product based on user_id
        @"filter": @{
            @"version": @2, // Required
            @"filterRule": @{
                @"operator": @"OR",
                @"ruleList": @[
                    @{
                        @"operator": @"OR",
                        @"conditionList": @[
                            @{
                                @"key": @"category",
                                @"value": @[
                                    @"3C > Mobile"
                                ],
                                @"operator": @"in"
                            }
                        ]
                    }
                ]
            }
        }
    };
    
    NSString *scenarioId = @"2t7koCuCDGqBtLMxXXXXXX";
    NSString *productId = @"SKU_12435";
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] getRecommendationWithScenarioId:scenarioId withProductId:productId withQueryParameters:parameters withCompletionHandler:^(id  _Nullable response) {
        if (response) {
            // Process response here
        }
    }];

### 

Sample response

  * The response returns the `recId`, `scenarioId`, `modelId`, and `productId`. You will need these IDs to track clicks on the recommended products.
  * All recommended products will be included in the `items` key.



JSON
    
    
    {
      "items": [
        {
          "productId": "TEST_SKU_16",
          "position": 2,
          "image": "<IMAGE_URL>",
          "title": "Mobile_16",
          "description": "hTC",
          "customLabel00": "Foo’s bar",
          "customLabel01": "false",
          "customLabel02": "-10",
          "customLabel03": "200.65",
          "customLabel04": "",
          "url": "<PRODUCT_URL>",
          "category": "3C > Mobile",
          "currency": "TWD",
          "price": "5999",
          "originalPrice": "5999",
          "order": "PRIMARY"
          ... // optional fields are not listed
        }
        ...
      ],
      "recId": "8c4d2657-5a0e-4b77-aa25-e22fa5ba5633",
      "scenarioId": "Aj2MMx5KHzPau2pv4aQ26i",
      "modelId": "5",
      "expType": "normal",
      "respCode": "1000",
      ...
    }

* * *

## 

Tracking clicks and impressions

To track scenario clicks and impressions, your app must use iOS SDK 7.4.0 or later.

### 

Tracking clicks

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Conversion tracking
> 
> To track conversions using the [**Item Conversion**](doc:recommendations-20-analytics#conversion-definitions) definition, events must include the `product_id` parameter.

To log click events on recommended products, call the following method and pass in parameters obtained from the recommendation response (`scenarioId`, `modelId`, `productId`, and `recId`).

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    func logRecommendationClicked(scenarioId: String, 
                                  modelId: String,
                                  productId: String,
                                  recommendationId: String)
    
    
    - (void)logRecommendationClickedWithScenarioId:(NSString *)scenarioId
                                       withModelId:(NSString *)modelId
                                     withProductId:(NSString *)productId
                              withRecommendationId:(NSString *)recommendationId;

The following example demonstrates how to log a click event for a recommended product.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let sId = response["scenarioId"]
    let modelId = response["modelId"]
    let rId = response["recId"]
    let items = response["items"]
    let firstProduct = items?.firstObject()
    let productId = firstProduct?["productId"] as? String
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().logRecommendationClicked(
        withScenarioId: sId,
        withModelId: modelId,
        withProductId: productId,
        withRecommendationId: rId)
    
    
    NSString *sId = response[@"scenarioId"];
    NSString *modelId = response[@"modelId"];
    NSString *rId = response[@"recId"];
    NArray *items = response[@"items"];
    NSDictionary *firstProduct = [items firstObject];
    NSString *productId = firstProduct[@"productId"];
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] logRecommendationClickedWithScenarioId:sId 
    withModelId:modelId
    withProductId:productId
    withRecommendationId:rId];

### 

Tracking impressions

The SDK logs a `recommendation_impression` event whenever a non-empty recommendation response is successfully received, regardless of the number of recommended products contained in the response.

# Recommendation (React Native SDK)

Get recommendations and track scenario performance.

The React Native SDK provides several API methods to retrieve product recommendations generated by [Recommendation](doc:recommendations-v2).

### 

Prerequisites

Before using the API methods to fetch product recommendations, complete the following:

  1. Complete the [required setup](doc:initial-setup-for-native-android-and-ios) for the Appier React Native SDK.
  2. [Create a recommendation scenario](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20).
  3. [Retrieve the `scenarioId`](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#perform-scenario-operations) for the recommendation scenario.



In addition:

  * Your app must be using React Native SDK 1.5.0 or later
  * The [status of the scenario](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#monitor-scenario-status) must be **Ready** , indicating that the recommendation model has completed training, before recommendation results can be retrieved



* * *

## 

Fetching recommendations

Use `getRecommendation()` to fetch recommendation results. This method returns a `Promise`, and the recommendation results will be returned to the `resolve()` function as a JSON object. Refer to the following sections for the sample request and response.

JavaScript
    
    
    async function getRecommendation(scenarioId, productId, parameters)

Parameter name| Data type| Nullable| Description  
---|---|---|---  
`scenarioId`| string| No| The scenario ID of the recommendation scenario retrieved from the AIQUA Dashboard.  
`productId`| string| Yes| Required by some recommendation models. See the [recommendation model reference](doc:recommendation-models#model-reference) for a list of all models and the data they require.The product ID you pass into the request must match the product ID specified in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed).  
`parameters`| JSON object| Yes| A JSON object containing optional query parameters. See `parameters` for a detailed description of this object.  
  
### 

`parameters`

`parameters` is a JSON object containing optional query parameters that you can use to specify what type of recommendation results you want to receive.

  * `user_id`: required to [filter results based on a user's activity](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#exclusion-rules).
  * `num`: Specifies the maximum number of recommended products to be returned. If the number of available products is less than `num`, all available products will be returned. The default value is 20 and the maximum value is 50.
  * `filter`: An object containing filtering rules to be applied to recommendation results. In the following example, only products with a product category equal to "3C > Mobile" will be returned. To learn more about creating recommendation filters, see [Product Filter Rules](doc:filtering-recommendation-results#api-calls).



filter
    
    
    {
      "version": 2,
      "filterRule": {
        "operator": "OR",
        "ruleList": [
          {
            "operator": "AND",
            "conditionList": [
              {
                "key": "category",
                "value": [
                  "3C > Mobile"
                ],
                "operator": "in",
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }

### 

Sample request

JavaScript
    
    
    var scenarioId = '<SCENARIO_ID>';
    var productId = '<PRODUCT_ID>';
    var parameters = {
      filter: {
        "version": 2,
        "filterRule": {
          "operator": "OR",
          "ruleList": [
            {
              "operator": "AND",
              "conditionList": [
                {
                  "key": "category",
                  "value": [
                    "3C > Mobile"
                  ],
                  "operator": "in",
                  "isCaseSensitive": false
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      user_id: '<USER_ID>',
      num: 10
    }
    RNAiqua.getRecommendation(scenarioId, productId, parameters)
      .then(result => Alert.alert('Success', JSON.stringify(result)), 
            error => Alert.alert('Failure', JSON.stringify(error)));

### 

Sample response

JSON
    
    
    {
      "items": [
        {
          "productId": "TEST_SKU_16",
          "position": 2,
          "image": "<IMAGE_URL>",
          "title": "Mobile_16",
          "description": "hTC",
          "customLabel00": "Foo’s bar",
          "customLabel01": "false",
          "customLabel02": "-10",
          "customLabel03": "200.65",
          "customLabel04": "",
          "url": "<PRODUCT_URL>",
          "category": "3C > Mobile",
          "currency": "TWD",
          "price": "5999",
          "originalPrice": "5999",
          "order": "PRIMARY"
          ... // optional fields are not listed
        }
        ...
      ],
      "recId": "8c4d2657-5a0e-4b77-aa25-e22fa5ba5633",
      "scenarioId": "Aj2MMx5KHzPau2pv4aQ26i",
      "modelId": "5",
      "expType": "normal",
      "respCode": "1000",
      ...
    }

  * `recId`, `scenarioId`, `modelId`, and `productId`: These IDs are used to track clicks on recommended products.
  * `items`: An array containing the recommendation results.



* * *

## 

Tracking clicks and impressions

To track scenario clicks and impressions, your app must use React Native SDK 1.5.0 or later.

### 

Tracking clicks

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Conversion tracking
> 
> To track conversions using the [**Item Conversion**](doc:recommendations-20-analytics#conversion-definitions) definition, events must include the `product_id` parameter.

To log click events on recommended products, call `logRecommendationClicked()` with the parameters obtained from the recommendation response (`scenarioId`, `modelId`, `productId`, and `recId`).

JavaScript
    
    
    function logRecommendationClicked(scenarioId, modelId, productId, recommendationId)

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> `modelId` data type
> 
> Please note that `modelId` is returned as `string` in the recommendation response, but it must be converted to `Number` before being passed into `logRecommendationClicked()`.

The following example demonstrates how to log a click event for a recommendation product.

JavaScript
    
    
    RNAiqua.logRecommendationClicked('Aj2MMx5KHzPau2pv4aQ26i', 12, 'TEST_SKU_1', 'recId');

### 

Tracking impressions

The SDK logs a `recommendation_impression` event whenever a non-empty recommendation response is successfully received, regardless of the number of recommended products contained in the response.

# Recommendation (Web SDK)

Get recommendations and track scenario performance.

## 

Usage

  1. Once the recommendation scenario's status changes to **Ready** on the AIQUA dashboard, copy the scenario ID.
  2. Retrieve recommendations using `appier('getRecommendationByScenario')`, passing in the scenario ID you copied. See Response for detailed response parameters.
  3. Render the recommendation results in an HTML container on your website. See Example usage for code samples.



* * *

## 

Retrieve recommendations

Use `appier('getRecommendationByScenario')` method to retrieve product recommendations.

TypeScript
    
    
    appier('getRecommendationByScenario', options, callback)

Name| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`options.scenarioId`| number| Required. The ID of the recommendation scenario.  
`options.user_id`| string| Required if filtering out purchased products by `user_id`. The value that allows AIQUA to filter out purchased products across platforms based on `user_id`. See [Filtering Recommendation Results](doc:filtering-recommendation-results#defining-api-filter-rules) for details.  
`options.productId`| string| Required for some recommendation models. The product ID of the [selected product](doc:recommendation-models#selected-product), as specified in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications). We recommend setting a default selected product for each page on your website that contains product data.  
  
If a default selected product is not set, then `productId` must be explicitly passed in the request for valid results to be returned.  
`options.category`| string| Only required for the **Category Hot Items** model.  
`options.filter`| object| Optional. Contains filters based on product attributes in the data feed. Only products that match the filter conditions are returned. See [Defining API filter rules](doc:filtering-recommendation-results#defining-api-filter-rules) for details.  
`options.num`| number| Optional. The number of results to return. Accepted values: `1`-`50`. Default value: `20`.  
  
The number of products returned may be less than the number specified if not enough products are generated.  
`callback`| function| Required. The callback method receiving results from the recommendation request.  
  
### 

(Recommended) Setting a default selected product

After setting a default selected product, that product's ID is automatically injected into the `options.productId` parameter if a value isn't explicitly provided in the recommendation request. Setting a default selected product reduces the chances of a recommendation request failing due to missing parameters.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> We recommend setting a default selected product on every page that contains product data, even if the page isn't currently displaying a recommendation scenario.

To set a default [selected product](doc:recommendation-models#selected-product), define the `appierRecommendationGetDefaultProductId()` global function, which should return the product ID of the default selected product. Note that `appierRecommendationGetDefaultProductId()` must be defined before you call `appier('getRecommendationByScenario')`.

JavaScript
    
    
    // Implement the global function appierRecommendationGetProductId(). This function should
    // return the product ID of the default selected product.
    window.appierRecommendationGetDefaultProductId = function(){
      var productId
      ...
      // Logic to assign the product ID of the default selected product to `productId`
      ...
      return productId
    }
    
    ...
    
    // When retrieving product recommendations, appierRecommendationGetProductId() is
    // automatically injected into the `options.productId` parameter if no value
    // is provided
    appier('getRecommendationByScenario', {}, callback)

### 

Response

The response to the recommendation request consists of three parameters.

Name| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`error`| string| The error message. See Troubleshooting for a list of potential error message.  
`recommendationItems`| Array| An array of objects representing recommended products.  
`recommendationMeta`| object| An object containing metadata about this request.  
  
#### 

`recommendationItems`

`recommendationItems` consists of an array of objects. Each object represents a recommended product and contains the product's details, such as its price and ID.

Name| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`productId`| string| The product's `productId` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`url`| string| A modified version of the product's `url` field from your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications). The modified `url` contains additional parameters for tracking recommendation performance.  
`order`| string| The type of recommendation result. One of the following values:  
• `"PRIMARY"`: This result was generated by the selected recommendation model.  
• `"FALLBACK"`: This result was generated by a [fallback rule](doc:recommendation-models#default-fallback-rules).  
• `"PINNED"`: This result is a [pinned product](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#add-pinned-products).  
• `"DESIGNATED_FALLBACK"`: This result is the default selected product.  
`position`| integer| The ranking of the product based on relevance, where the item with `position = 0` is the most relevant result.  
  
If you enabled the [**Shuffle** setting](creating-scenario-recommendation-20#shuffle-recommended-products) when creating the scenario, results will be returned in a random order.  
  
If you don't enable the **Shuffle** setting, results are returned in ascending order by the value of `position`, with the most relevant result in the first position and the least relevant in the last position.  
`image`| string| The product's `image` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`title`| string| The product's `title` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`description`| string| The product's `description` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`customLabel00`, `customLabel01`, `customLabel02`, `customLabel03`, `customLabel04`| string| Custom labels specified in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed).  
`category`| string| The product's `category` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`currency`| string| The product's `currency` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`price`| string| The product's `price` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
`originalPrice`| string| The product's `originalPrice` field in your [product data feed](doc:product-data-feed#data-specifications).  
  
An example `recommendationItems` response containing two recommended products looks like this:

JSON
    
    
    [
      {
        "productId": "1234",
        "order": "PRIMARY",
        "position": 0,
        "image": "https://www.example.com/files/products/image.jpg",
        "title": "T-shirt",
        "description": "This is a description for product A",
        "customLabel00": "4",
        "customLabel01": "blue-gray",
        "url": "https://www.example.com.tw/product/1234",
        "category": "clothes,spring,summer,men",
        "currency": "TWD",
        "price": "350",
        "originalPrice": "350"
      },
      {
        "productId": "1235",
        "order": "PRIMARY",
        "position": 0,
        "image": "https://www.example.com/files/products/image2.jpg",
        "title": "Shorts",
        "description": "This is a description for product A",
        "customLabel00": "6",
        "customLabel01": "white",
        "url": "https://www.example.com.tw/product/1235",
        "category": "clothes,spring,summer,men",
        "currency": "TWD",
        "price": "450",
        "originalPrice": "600"
      },
    ]

#### 

`recommendationMeta`

The `recommendationMeta` object contains additional metadata associated with the recommendation request.

Name| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`scenarioId`| string| The ID of the scenario.  
`modelId`| string| The ID of the recommendation model used by the scenario.  
`recommendationId`| string| The ID of this recommendation request.  
`respCode`| string| One of the following values:  
• `1000`: At least one result returned was generated by the scenario's AI model.  
• `1100`: At least one result was returned, but results were generated from fallback rules, pinned products, or selected fallback products.  
• `2000`: No results returned, potentially due to filter conditions or an A/B test with no results.  
  
A sample `recommendationMeta` response looks like this:

JSON
    
    
    {
      "scenario_id": "1111",
      "modelId": "2222",
      "recommendationId": "3333",
      "respCode: "1000",
    }

* * *

## 

Example usage

Refer to the following example recommendation requests to learn how to use product recommendations generated by a scenario.

  * Print IDs of recommended products
  * Display recommended product details on a web page



### 

Example: Print IDs of recommended products

The following code sample demonstrates how to retrieve and print the `productId` for products recommended by the scenario with a `scenarioId` of `123`.

JavaScript
    
    
    appier(
      'getRecommendationByScenario',
      { scenarioId: '123' },
      (error, recommendationItems, recommendationMeta) => {
        if (error === null) {
          // Get data from response
          recommendationItems.forEach(recommendationItem =>
            console.log(recommendationItem.productId)
          );
        }
      }
    );

### 

Example: Display recommended product details on a web page

The following code sample demonstrates how to generate HTML to display products recommended by the scenario with a `scenarioId` of `123`, then inject the HTML into an element with the ID `promo-banner__products`.

JavaScript
    
    
    appier(
      'getRecommendationByScenario',
      { scenarioId: '123' },
      (error, recommendationItems, recommendationMeta) => {
        if (error === null) {
          let content = '';
          
          // Construct HTML content from each recommended product
          recommendationItems.forEach(recItem => {
            const { title, url, image } = recItem;
            content += `
            <div class="promo-banner__product">
              <img class="promo-banner__product-image" src="${image}" alt="${title}" />
              <a href="${url}" target="_self">
                <h3 class="promo-banner__product-title">${title}</h3>
              </a>
            </div>`;
          });
          
          // Inject the constructed HTML into the target element on the page
          document.getElementById('promo-banner__products').innerHTML = content;
        }
      }
    );

* * *

## 

Tracking clicks and impressions

### 

Tracking clicks

  * The URL returned in `recommendationItems` contains additional parameters for click tracking. AIQUA automatically tracks click and impression events for this URL.
  * To track conversions using the [**Item Conversion**](doc:recommendations-20-analytics#conversion-definitions) definition, events must also include the `product_id` parameter.



### 

Tracking impressions

The SDK logs a `recommendation_impression` event whenever a non-empty recommendation response is successfully received, regardless of the number of recommended products contained in the response.

* * *

## 

Troubleshooting

Error message| Troubleshooting notes  
---|---  
`"scenarioId" parameter is missing`| Ensure that the `options.scenarioId` parameter is present in your request.  
`"uid" parameter is missing`| Ensure that the `options.user_id` parameter is present in your request.  
`Invalid parameter: "user_id" should be string or number`| Ensure that the data type of `user_id` is a string or number.  
`Invalid parameter: "category" should be string `| Ensure that `options.category` is a string.  
`Invalid filter parameter: "exclude" should be string array`| Ensure that the exclude format of the filter passed in `options.filter`is a string array.  
`Invalid v2 filter parameter: "filter.filterRule.ruleList" should be array`| Ensure that `options.filter.filterRule.ruleList` is an array.  
`Failed to serialize custom parameters`| Ensure that `options.filter` has the correct format. For details, see [Defining API filter rules](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/filtering-recommendation-results#defining-api-filter-rules).  
`Scenario not found`| Ensure that a scenario with the specified scenario ID exists.  
`This scenario is preparing, not ready to be served yet`| Wait for the scenario's status to change to **Ready**.  
`Wrong Parameters`| Ensure that all parameters are correct.

# How do I segment by notification ID?

## 

Overview

If you want to segment based on users’ past interaction with the notifications of a particular campaign (e.g. include users who have clicked on notifications from campaign A), you'll need to segment by condition using the notification ID (`notificationId`) as the event parameter.

This section explains how to retrieve notification IDs for different campaign types and how to use these IDs for segmentation.

  * Regular merged push campaigns
  * Experiment campaigns
  * Non-experiment campaigns



* * *

## 

Regular merged push campaigns

You can retrieve the notification ID for regular merged push campaigns from the following locations:

  * [Campaign edit page](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/how-do-i-segment-by-notification-id-copy#from-the-campaign-edit-page)
  * [Campaign performance page](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/how-do-i-segment-by-notification-id-copy#from-the-campaign-performance-page)



For campaigns sent to multiple channels (e.g. Android, iOS, and web), clicking the **Copy notification IDs** button will copy a comma-separated list of notification IDs, where each ID corresponds to a single channel and the order of channels is Android, iOS, then web. For example:

Channels| Description  
---|---  
Android, iOS, and Web| If you select all available channels (Android, iOS, and web), the notification IDs for the variant will be listed in the following order: 1571600000, 1571610000, 1571620000.• 1571600000 is the Android notification ID.  
• 1571610000 is the iOS notification ID.  
• 1571620000 is the web notification ID.  
Android, Web| If you only selected Android and Web, the IDs will be listed in the following order: 7600210000, 7600220000.• 7600210000 is the Android notification ID.  
• 7600220000 is the web notification ID.  
  
### 

1\. Retrieve the notification IDs

#### 

From the campaign edit page

  1. Go to the campaign list and click the pencil icon to edit the campaign.

![](https://files.readme.io/878a395c68c62c3a378c3f2292d586de944edffa37372ed4c2c462b69d72fb09-eidt.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes
> 
> You must save the campaign to generate the notification IDs.

  2. Navigate to the **Creative** section. Click on a variant, then click **Copy notification ID**.

![](https://files.readme.io/19b38c817065eadd7e9c800afddcd1f791fbbd577cfd9bbb84a97864e0d9747c-Creative_to_copy_ID.png)
  3. Alternatively, go to the final step, **Review & launch**. Click the copy icon corresponding to a variant to copy its notification IDs.

![](https://files.readme.io/1ea337c7c26ef5c7212751e5d04291a09d085dc0dbfba639d2e3c9a3a07204c7-Reviewlaunch_to_copy_ID_1.png)



#### 

From the campaign performance page

  1. Go to the campaign list and click the campaign name to view the performance page.

![](https://files.readme.io/0e8317be07e7446583b5b847194cca1067f4fd1aec028c40949cff7a3dfbb8dc-Campaign_name.png)
  2. In the performance page, open the **Campaign details** tab. Click the copy icon corresponding to a variant to copy its notification IDs.

![](https://files.readme.io/b3751ac83fde03c923e4fb7aad2d5bcc58196c40486f0ce22497008e5c87dd64-Copy_notification_ID_from_Campaign_details_1.png)
  3. If the campaign execution has been triggered, you can also open the **Experiment analysis** tab on the performance page. Click the copy icon corresponding to a variant from **Performance analysis** section to copy its notification IDs.

![](https://files.readme.io/538fcd4dadd4a541e813b36c51a9bdb081c2e6c670bbfa06eefd7eb48446274f-Experiment_analysis_to_copy_ID.png)



### 

2\. Segment by notification ID

After retrieving the notification ID, refer to the [Segment by Condition (User Events)](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/defining-segments#user-events) guide to create a segment. Follow the steps provided to add new conditions with the notification ID:

  1. In the event drop-down list, select a notification-related event, such as `notification_received` or `notification_clicked`.

![](https://files.readme.io/9d95b4c397e6d8f3afc03bc4b2535ade94c85847343e7fd7a96ce507eadb0af8-Segment_by_events.png)
  2. Click **Add Filter** , set the event parameter to `notificationId`, and then enter the notification ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/539240dcd3a22223aae035871a7f1305d7f31dbe06c2ee3b9146be6d04dba8f5-segment_by_notificationId.png)



* * *

## 

Experiment campaigns

Use each variant's campaign ID to generate a notification ID that can be used for segmentation. This method of retrieving the notification ID is applicable to the following campaign types:

  * Regular push (non-merged) campaigns
  * Regular email campaigns
  * In-app campaigns
  * In-web campaigns



### 

1\. Retrieve the variant's campaign ID

Go to the campaign list, click the **Edit** button for the campaign, and find the variant's campaign ID by hovering over the variant name.

![](https://files.readme.io/38337cc7b4a4f70a3aed78be589ac22dbd697583409f279a197f035e8773d2a0-Retake__copy_Campaign_ID.png)

### 

2\. Convert the variant's campaign ID to a notification ID

Next, convert the variant's campaign ID to a notification ID using the following formula:`Notication ID = Campaign ID x 10,000`.

For example, if the variant's campaign ID is `111111`, then its notification ID would be `1111110000` (`111111` x `10,000`).

### 

3\. Segment by notification ID

After retrieving the notification ID, refer to [Segment by Condition (User Events)](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/defining-segments#user-events) for guidance on creating a segment. Follow the steps provided to add new conditions with notification ID:

  1. In the event drop-down list, select a notification-related event, such as:

     * `qg_inweb_displayed`
     * `qg_inweb_clicked`
     * `qg_inapp_displayed`
     * `qg_inapp_clicked`
     * `qg_email_opened`
![](https://files.readme.io/f46192070be3287f49fb94c0409b243f1f5349aedec8ec65030a426ee5d86dac-Segment_by_events2.png)
  2. Click **Add Filter** , set the event parameter to `notificationId`, and then enter the notification ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/a9caa11b13d90513a9c3a03b7737a914eb34dee58139061b8007651674356f6b-segment_by_notificationId.png)



* * *

## 

Non-experiment campaigns

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes
> 
> Not applicable for non-experiment merged push campaign.

### 

1\. Retrieve the campaign ID

For non-experiment campaigns, go to campaign list, click the **Edit** button of the campaign, and find the campaign ID in the URL.

![](https://files.readme.io/8db1f100c8be4eb44908e2100617f993a6f532547b13e774017465980f19e24c-Retake__copy_Campaign_ID_from_url.png)

### 

2\. Convert the campaign ID to a notification ID

Next, convert the campaign ID to a notification ID as described below.

  * If Campaign ID >= 188800, then the Notification ID = Campaign ID * 10000
    * e.g. campaign ID is 198765, the `notificationId` will be 1987650000.
  * If Campaign ID < 188800, then the `Notification ID = Campaign ID * 1000
    * e.g. campaign ID is 87654, the `notificationId` will be 87654000.



### 

3\. Segment by notification ID

After retrieving the notification ID, refer to [Segment by Condition (User Events)](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/defining-segments#user-events) for guidance on creating a segment. Follow the steps provided to add new conditions with the notification ID:

  1. In the event drop-down list, select a notification-related event, such as:

     * `notification_received`
     * `notification_clicked`
     * `qg_inweb_displayed`
     * `qg_inweb_clicked`
     * `qg_inapp_displayed`
     * `qg_inapp_clicked`
     * `qg_email_opened`
![](https://files.readme.io/b781f78b3af288c54022c519db5d3e1118ec42b7e7385ea4e9ebf1ae025cce7c-Segment_by_events2.png)
  2. Click **Add Filter** , set the event parameter to `notificationId`, and then enter the notification ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/c9bdfa426e05701f5e02146f362f686d32623a77807f0f95cb99f9e66bcb269a-Event_parameter__notification_ID_2.png)

# Create a Segment

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> New segment experience
> 
> If you've recently onboarded to AIQUA, you'll see the new segment experience. Refer to the [Enterprise Resource Center](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/segments-getting-started) to learn how to use the new experience.
> 
> If you don’t see the new change yet, don’t worry. We’ll begin rolling out the new experience to all users in 2026. Your customer success manager will reach out to you when your account is ready.

Audience segmentation is the process of dividing users who share the same user events and/or attributes into subgroups based on the criteria you've defined. Creating audience segments allows you to send relevant messages to each group of users, instead of indiscriminately sending the same campaigns to all users.

![](https://files.readme.io/6563f19-Screen_Shot_2020-08-05_at_7.19.59_PM.png)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> Before you create audience segments, see [User Data Collection](doc:user-data-collection) to read about how to collect user data and used in AIQUA.

Refer to the following guides to learn how to create segments in AIQUA:

  * [Conditions (Beta)](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/creating-a-segment#/): Create a unified segment by specifying user event and attribute conditions. Unified segments are synced across both AIQUA and AIRIS instances within the same project, reducing the time needed to start sending campaigns and generating reports.
  * [Conditions](doc:segments-create-conditions): Create a segment by specifying user event and attribute conditions.
  * [Mapping with User List](doc:segments-create-mapping-with-user-list): Create a segment by uploading a list of user IDs that map with existing users in the AIQUA database.
  * [Offline Events](doc:segments-create-offline-events): Create a segment from data uploaded via API.
