# Conditions

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> New segment experience
> 
> If you've recently onboarded to AIQUA, you'll see the new segment experience. Refer to the [Enterprise Resource Center](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/segments-getting-started) to learn how to use the new experience.
> 
> If you don’t see the new change yet, don’t worry. We’ll begin rolling out the new experience to all users in 2026. Your customer success manager will reach out to you when your account is ready.

You can divide your users into smaller groups using user events or user attributes as segmentation conditions.

* * *

## 

Segment by conditions

  1. Go to **Segment** > **Segment list** , and click the **\+ Create segment** > **Conditions** in the top-right corner.

![](https://files.readme.io/837a6d961c3d012a7111edb0ecae9747fb26212a9183e9e555fccf07bef34bb2-Group_27_1.png)

  2. Enter a **Segment name**. Adding a description is optional.

![](https://files.readme.io/33f44078cc827dfd3bed985549f4857d3ec73472f91abb036406705cebeea99b-image_15.png)

  3. Under **Users to include** , click **\+ Add condition group** , then click **\+ Add condition** and set condition as you like.

![](https://files.readme.io/0aee108601f5350ae9c9a1aef2a57d62052c09b1c65d80a187279992543a5235-image_14.png)

* * *

## 

Include and exclude users

There are two sections:

  * **Users to include** : This section allows you to include users who have the specified user attributes or have performed the specified user events.
  * **Users to exclude** : This section allows you to define the criteria to remove certain users already included in the **Users to include** section.



If you don't add any condition group under **Users to include** , the segment will include all audiences. If you didn't set an include condition, but set an exclude condition, the segment will include all audiences minus the users who meet the exclude condition.

![](https://files.readme.io/e042a1d23dce97fa3cec6ff136d7c9fff1a8e8ad458f9d73f9031c92ccb5c555-image_18_1.png)

* * *

## 

Add conditions

You can add one or multiple conditions. If you select ​**Any** , users who match any of the conditions will be considered a match. If you select **All** , users need to match all conditions to be considered a match.

To add conditions, click the **\+ Add condition** button.

![](https://files.readme.io/2055458b8be66d2964cb84ba0d0c59727bbab213a56a3099a6540f1d3ae9dcc5-Group_14_5.png)

### 

User attributes

When creating a condition based on a user attribute, you must select an operator, and type the value. See the operators section below.

![](https://files.readme.io/c9eede196ba6dfcec255c0187ce3ddbcd05f5f722032d38b2154b62cbc111fce-Group_16_3.png)

### 

User events

When creating a condition based on a user event, you can select an event without choosing an event parameter. Optionally, if you want to further narrow down on the condition, click **\+ Add filter** to specify the event parameter, operator, and value. See the operators section below.

![](https://files.readme.io/0af8fbb75023f13c6ad23f8d6b3fd0ef6a4cf6007044f044e10d008328e542bc-Group_17_2.png) ![](https://files.readme.io/a3f1b7ec11f2eae0cd57c550bc363604ddaa4a76fab7890f13c16a9b837e84d0-Group_18_5.png)

You can define event conditions for users, including a specific time range for when the event occurred. Select a parameter, an operator, and a time period value.

  * This setting applies to all the user events set as condition except for events where you have set `Lifetime count` as the event parameter.
  * This setting does not apply to user attributes that are set as condition.
  * If the number entered exceeds the data retention period (180 days by default), the data retention period will be applied.
  * Do not set the number to 0.

![](https://files.readme.io/d1846eb9bf51c1f7b9d793502873e75036d2aa9dffcf127384c121f80906e637-Group_25_1.png)

### 

Event parameters

For some of the default events collected by Appier SDK, you might see the following event parameters.

Event parameters| Description  
---|---  
`notificationId`| This is the ID of the notification you have sent. This parameter is available for some default events that are related to campaigns, such as `notification_clicked`.See [How do I segment by notification ID?](doc:how-do-i-segment-by-notification-id)  
`Campaign Name`| This is the name of the campaign. Campaigns from the last 7 days will be shown in the dropdown list.  
`Lifetime count`| This feature needs to be activated by Appier Support.This is the number of times the event is completed in the user's lifetime based on events collected by the Appier SDK. The `Lifetime count` is not subjected to the time range specified in the user events .  
`referrer`| This is the URL of the webpage that sends visitors to your site using a link. This parameter is available for some default events that are related to website visits, such as `page_viewed`.  
`url`| This is the URL of the current webpage the user is accessing. This parameter is available for some default events that are related to website visits, such as `page_viewed`.  
  
Below are the event parameters of the default event `aiq_journey_map_exit`, an event that is generated when the user is exited out of a journey map campaign.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> The event `aiq_journey_map_exit` is only generated in journey maps created after August 2021.

Event parameters| Description  
---|---  
`exit_times`| The number of times the user is exited out of a single journey map campaign.Here's an example of how to segment users who are exited out of a journey map campaign more than three times: `aiq_journey_map_exit exit_times once > "3"`  
`exit_reason`| `exit_node`: Users are exited out of the journey map campaign after entering an exit node.`exit_criteria`: Users are exited out of the journey map campaign after meeting the overall exit criteria.`excluded_after_segment_refresh`: Users are exited out of the journey map campaign because they no longer fulfill the conditions of the audience segment selected.  
`journey_map_id`| The campaign ID of the journey map. To find the campaign ID, go to campaign list, click the edit button of the campaign, and find the campaign ID in the URL.Here's an example of how to segment users who are exited out of a journey that has the campaign ID "12345": `aiq_journey_map_exit journey_map_id once = "12345"`  
`journey_map_name`| The campaign name of the journey map.  
  
* * *

## 

Data type and operators

After you have selected an attribute or an event parameter, you will see the operator dropdown list. Depending on the data type of the attribute or event parameter, different operators or filters will be available.

  * String
  * Number
  * Boolean
  * Date / Time



### 

String

If the data type of the attribute or the event parameter is set to string, that is text, you will see the following operators in the dropdown list. The value entered is not case-sensitive.

![](https://files.readme.io/b23f99a31329fa1407a99f063dbb1735807dc20d1c0337f4d0e0e11e1bee03b0-image_28.png)

Operators| Description  
---|---  
equals| The value has to be exactly the same to be considered a match.   
Example: If condition is `product_name equals "Blue Jeans"`   
• "Blue Jeans" is a match   
• "Classic Blue Jeans" is not a match   
• "Jeans" is not a match  
is any of| The value has to be an exact match with at least one of the values you have entered. You can directly paste a list of comma-separated values or a list from a spreadsheet.   
Example: If the condition is `product_name is any of "apple" or "juice" or "banana cake"`   
• "apple" is a match  
• "apple juice" is not a match  
• "banana" is not a match  
contains| If the parameter value collected contains the value you have entered, it will be considered a match.  
Example: If condition is `product_name contains "Blue Jeans"`   
• "Classic Blue Jeans" is a match  
• "Blue Denim Jeans" is not a match  
If condition is `product_name contains "Jean"`   
• "JeanS" is a match  
exists| If you choose exists, you don't need to input a value.   
When the operator is set to exists, note that users with empty string or null value for this parameters are considered as meeting the condition.  
For example, if you set the include condition to `phoneNo` exists, this segment will include users with an empty value for the `phoneNo` profile parameter.  
  
### 

Number

If the data type of the attribute or the event parameter is set to number you will see the following operators in the dropdown list.

![](https://files.readme.io/90cbc769bd96f1a34a07fb1ff5f3e873a541f7ac887707aefe7e6101550bebf2-image_29_1.png)

Operators| Description  
---|---  
`>=`| Greater than or equal to  
`<=`| Less than or equal to  
`>`| Greater than  
`<`| Less than  
`=`| Equal to  
`!=`| Not equal to  
  
### 

Boolean

If the data type of the attribute is set to boolean, you can select `true` or `false`. The following default attributes in the condition dropdown list are boolean.

  * `aiq_push_enabled`
  * `email_hard_bounced`
  * `email_unsubscribe`

![](https://files.readme.io/e8ab947de661b6e156cba4af412c56694b74638f5c7bdcffa0448d25bb7254ba-image_30_1.png)

### 

Date / Time

Currently, the date / time related filters are only supported for the following default attributes:

  * `line_first_sync_time`: The date when the user is detected as a follower of the LINE channel.
  * `line_unfollow_time`: The date when the user is detected as no longer following the LINE channel.



You can use the above LINE-related user attributes to segment users based on the date they follow or unfollow your LINE channel.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> AIQUA detects for new LINE followers and unfollowers once a day. The detected date may be one day later than users’ actual followed or unfollowed date.

When `line_first_sync_time` or `line_unfollow_time` is selected, the following filters are available:

Filters| Description  
---|---  
In the past X days| Includes today.  
In the next X days| Includes today.  
Before| Does not include today or the selected date.  
After| Does not include today or the selected date.  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/85747d6-Screen_Shot_2021-03-17_at_5.28.30_PM.png)

For example, you can send a campaign with welcoming message to your new LINE users. To do this, create a segment with the following settings: `line_first_sync_time is in the past "1" day(s)`.

![](https://files.readme.io/0e46557a6d510232a6493603039a9870096a827951ff60f0fe5ab300e6f7de78-image_31.png)

* * *

## 

Segmentation examples

  * Example 1: Reduce cart abandonment
  * Example 2: Target interested users
  * Example 3: Re-engage inactive users



### 

Example 1: Reduce cart abandonment

Segment by users who added jeans-related products to cart, but didn't purchase in the past week.

  * **Users to include**
    * `product_added_to_cart and product_category contains "jeans"`
    * `Count >= 1, Time: Past 1 week(s)`
  * **Users to exclude**
    * `product_purchased and product_category contains "jeans"`
    * `Count >= 1, Time: Past 1 week(s)`

![](https://files.readme.io/1ed86cfcfc11d7bf31b6ca78b9463e05f8aa659ea79f531525e6dc7a03b5df18-Conditions__Reduce_cart_abandonment.png)

### 

Example 2: Target interested users

Segment by users who have clicked on a particular campaign with the campaign name "ABC" in the past week.

  * **Users to include**
    * `notification_clicked and Campaign Name = "ABC"`
    * `Count >= 1, Time: Past 1 week(s)`

![](https://files.readme.io/e42ef577698842396ed9ce0dd3a716ae144ecf0f8a9c2b24115399cc7c81bf49-Conditions__Target_interested_users.png)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> If you do not see the campaign name listed in the dropdown list, you can also segment based on notification ID. See [How do I segment by notification ID?](doc:how-do-i-segment-by-notification-id)

### 

Example 3: Re-engage inactive users

Segment by VIP users who have purchased in the last 30 days, but not in the past 7 days.

  * **Users to include** (under **Condition group 1** , set **Match: All**)
    * `member_status equals "VIP"`
    * `product_purchased`
    * `Count >= 1, Time: Past 1 month(s)`
  * **Users to exclude**
    * `product_purchased`
    * `Count >= 1, Time: Past 1 week(s)`

![](https://files.readme.io/6c01433a574c4ac942c8e0e23ebebcd5e2a867b6a34cbdc3f0822d4d9a896a76-Conditions__Re-engage_inactive_users.png)

# Mapping with User List

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> New segment experience
> 
> If you've recently onboarded to AIQUA, you'll see the new segment experience. Refer to the [Enterprise Resource Center](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/segments-getting-started) to learn how to use the new experience.
> 
> If you don’t see the new change yet, don’t worry. We’ll begin rolling out the new experience to all users in 2026. Your customer success manager will reach out to you when your account is ready.

You can create segments by uploading a list of users directly to the [AIQUA dashboard](https://aiqua.appier.com/create_segment/by_upload). Your list must contain a unique identifier for each user, such as email, ID, or phone number. AIQUA will add only the identifiers that match existing users in the database to your segment.

For example, if you have a list of emails from customers who attended an event, you can upload this list to create a segment. Any emails that don't match existing users in the AIQUA database won't be included in the segment.

* * *

## 

Prepare the upload file

The upload file must meet the following requirements:

  * The file must include one unique identifier, for example, email, on each line without any spaces, tabs, or commas.
    * Do not include a header row.
    * Do not include other user attributes or more than one identifier in the file.

![](https://files.readme.io/ff3b886-Screen_Shot_2022-05-03_at_10.15.42_AM.png)

  * The file must be a UTF-8 .txt or .csv file and without BOM.
  * The file should contain the value of the **Audience Parameter** you select on the AIQUA dashboard. See step 3 below.
  * The maximum file size is 100 MB. If the file exceeds 100 MB, break the file into smaller components and upload them. Note that each component will form a separate segment.



* * *

## 

Upload the user list

  1. Go to **Segments** > **Segment list** , and click the **\+ Create segment** > **Mapping with User List** in the top-right corner.

![](https://files.readme.io/d8a31d93bc5f205e799da1816cc594ec8c27903275f9bfd84ca00d817f52738f-Group_30_1.png)

  2. Enter a **Segment Name**. Adding a description is optional.

![](https://files.readme.io/9f723b884bdd4e18e51371bc3c4c2b009ec3665ea63766871611100dd97a5894-segment-by-mapping-with-user-list.png)

  3. Use the **Audience Parameter** dropdown list to choose the unique identifier to match your users with AIQUA's database.
  4. Under **Upload Audience File** , click **Choose file** to upload an audience file.
  5. Once file upload is done, click **Save**.

# Offline Events

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Beta
> 
> Offline event segmentation is a beta feature.

You can segment audiences based on API-uploaded offline event data from your own files, CRM, or other data sources. A typical example of offline event data is transaction data from your physical stores.

  1. First, your developer needs to create an offline segment source and upload an offline event file using the [Offline Event API v2](ref:getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2). An offline segment source serves as the underlying data source for offline segmentation.
  2. Next, on the AIQUA dashboard, select an offline segment source and set segmentation conditions to create the final offline event segment.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * Offline event segments can only be used in:
>     * Regular campaigns: Push, Email, SMS, LINE, and Kakao.
>     * [Journey maps](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/getting-started-with-journey-maps)
>   * Up to three offline source segments can be created.
>   * Each offline event entry must have a `user_id`. If the uploaded `user_id` does not match with any existing `user_id` in the AIQUA database, the entry will be stored in the database, but cannot be used in segmentation and campaigns until it has been matched with a user.
>   * Offline event segments cannot be used when creating campaigns via API or sending notifications via API.
> 


* * *

## 

Segment by offline events

  1. Go to **Audience** > **Segment list** , and click the **\+ Create segment** > **Offline events** in the top-right corner.

![](https://files.readme.io/5f63288ba87388abefc4f23777a97c47023e6158f20c80940e3868eb21e0041f-Create-segment-offline-events.png)

  2. Enter a segment name.
  3. Under **Segment Source** , select an offline segment source from the dropdown. The dropdown will only show offline segment sources with valid data.

![](https://files.readme.io/6be21c85820b7e9cdccd824fa30217be40eac2cba4e7017fcc964a49a96ac930-2-select-offline-data-source.png)

  4. Select **Set the Condition** and click **\+ Add New Condition** to start creating a segmentation condition. For example, you can create a condition to include users who have completed `product_purchased` events with the `product_name` parameter containing "shoes" in the past day.

![](https://files.readme.io/67e6bc62083eb2251c8729142f0f71ea6d9be06b87295fd8e2019dfa812d0517-3-offline-event-segment-conditions.png)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> To include every user from the offline segment source in the segment, select **All Audiences**.

  5. If needed, you can set **And Exclude** conditions to explicitly exclude users who have specified offline events.
  6. Click **Save**.



On the **Segment list** , you'll be able to see the segment with the **Source** set to **Offline event**.

![](https://files.readme.io/1225e0e35a90165e21ea634c8a3bffe1a387ef265032d4cc8770cd5cb5eb8afa-list-offline-event.png)

Users who matched with a `user_id` in the uploaded offline events are tallied in the segment list table based on the channels they can receive campaigns from. For example, if a matched user has an email address and phone number recorded in the database, the user will be counted in the **Email subscribers** and **Phone numbers** columns.

# Segment List

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> New segment experience
> 
> If you've recently onboarded to AIQUA, you'll see the new segment experience. Refer to the [Enterprise Resource Center](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/segments-getting-started) to learn how to use the new experience.
> 
> If you don’t see the new change yet, don’t worry. We’ll begin rolling out the new experience to all users in 2026. Your customer success manager will reach out to you when your account is ready.

To view all of your AIQUA segments, go to **Audience > Segment list**. From the segment list page, you can search for segments, view user counts, and execute various segment operations.

![](https://files.readme.io/921002cc6a4d6b67262cb2ac5afc76cd71c096dac533a6edb9e8f1ac8a37042a-Segment-list-new.png)

You can click on the segment's name to view the details page which contains the user count and segment trend.

### 

Limitations for in-web and in-app campaigns

Only the **All Users** and **New Users** default segments will include new users who visited the website or launched the app for the first time in the past 24 hours.

For all other segments, it can take up to 24 hours for users to be included in the segment after they meet segmentation conditions.

* * *

## 

Segment sources and segment types

Segments can be created from multiple sources, and the segment's type depends on the source from which it was created. The daily refresh settings for a segment are determined by the segment's type.

### 

Segment sources

Segment source| Description  
---|---  
**Default**|  Default segment are predefined and automatically created by AIQUA:• **All Users / All Audiences** : Includes all valid users in the database.  
• **Test Segment** : Used for receiving test notifications when you're creating a campaign. See [Test Segment](doc:segments-test-segment) for details.   
• **[LINE] All Followers** : This segment is automatically created after your [LINE official account is connected](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line). It includes all LINE followers in the integrated LINE channel and excludes users who have unfollowed or blocked the LINE channel. See [LINE Segment FAQs](doc:line-segment-faqs) for detail.  
**Condition**|  Segment created by [specifying segmentation conditions](doc:segments-create-conditions).  
**Condition (beta)**| [Unified segments created by specifying segmentation conditions](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/creating-a-segment). Unified segments are synced between AIQUA and AIRIS instances within the same project.  
**Mapping with User List**|  Segments created via:

  * [Mapping with a user list](doc:segments-create-mapping-with-user-list)
  * AIXON import
  * AIRIS import

  
**Offline Events**|  Segments created using uploaded [offline event data](doc:segments-create-offline-events).  
**Split Users**|  Segments that are [splitting users](doc:campaigns-getting-started-email-ip-warmup#split-users-into-multiple-segments) for IP warmup.  
  
### 

Segment types

AIQUA categorizes segments into two types: dynamic segments and static segments. Each segment type has different refresh behavior, and a segment's type is determined by that segment's source.

![](https://files.readme.io/b30be6f-segment-types.png)

#### 

Dynamic segments

Segment source| Refresh behavior  
---|---  
• **Default**  
• **Condition**|  User counts for dynamic segments that have been created, edited, or used in the last three days are automatically refreshed each day.After three days of inactivity, a dynamic segment will stop automatically refreshing its user counts until the segment has been edited or used in a campaign again.  
  
Dynamic segments can have one of the following statuses indicating its current refresh behavior:

  * **Daily refresh** : This segment is automatically refreshed daily. Dynamic segments that have been created, edited, or used in the last three days will have this status.
  * **Refresh paused** : This segment is no longer being automatically refreshed daily. To enable automatic daily refresh, edit or use this segment.

![](https://files.readme.io/6bb4739-dynamic-segment-statuses.png)

In addition, dynamic segments can always be manually refreshed by clicking the refresh button next to the segment's name.

![](https://files.readme.io/65bc864-segment-manual-refresh.png)

#### 

Static segments

User counts for static segments are not automatically refreshed.

Segment source| Refresh behavior  
---|---  
**Offline event**|  User counts are refreshed when new offline event data is uploaded.  
**Split user**|  User counts can't be refreshed after creation.  
**Mapped**|  User counts are refreshed when segmentation conditions are edited.  
  
* * *

## 

User and subscriber count

The segment list shows the user and subscriber count in each segment.

![](https://files.readme.io/814db4e189e4b37789bc7517ba57c1b8d9d36d5ebe4fce2e6b8b4f486b2f51ea-segment-list-users-count.png)

Note that if the channel is not integrated, "\--" will be displayed instead of the user count.

Columns| Description  
---|---  
**Android users**|  Indicates the number of users who currently have your Android app installed. The number does not include users who have already uninstalled the app.In in-app campaigns, this is the number of users AIQUA can show the campaign to if the conditions are met.  
**Android subscribers**|  Indicates the number of Android users who did not opt out of push notifications of this app in the device settings. A user's subscription status is updated each time the user opens the app.Android users are subscribed to app push by default when they install the app. They can opt out by disabling the push notifications of that app in device settings.For Android users who are using Android SDK 5.5.2 or earlier versions, all valid users are included regardless of their opt-in status in the device settings.For app push campaigns, this is the number of users AIQUA can send the campaign to if the conditions are met.  
**iOS users**|  Indicates the number of users who currently have your iOS app installed (production environment). The number does not include users who have already uninstalled the app.In in-app campaigns, this is the number of users AIQUA can show the campaign to if the conditions are met.  
**iOS subscribers**|  Indicates the number of iOS users who opted in to push notifications of this app (production environment). A user's subscription status is updated each time the user opens the app.For iOS users who are using iOS SDK 4.4.1 or earlier versions, all valid users are included regardless of their opt-in status.For app push campaigns, this is the number of users AIQUA can send the campaign to if the conditions are met.  
**iOS dev users**|  Follows the same description as **iOS users** , except it's based on your iOS app in development or testing environment.  
**iOS dev subscribers**|  Follows the same description as **iOS subscribers** , except it's based on your iOS app in development or testing environment.  
**Web users**|  Indicates the number of users who have a cookie history of visiting the website. In addition to desktop users, web users also include users who are visiting the website from the browsers of their mobile devices.  
**Web subscribers**|  Indicates the number of web users in the segment who are subscribed to web push notifications.The number does not include web users who have a push token, but are detected by the push service provider, for example, Google Cloud Messaging, as no longer subscribed to web push. However, when sending web push campaigns, AIQUA will still try to send campaigns to these users.  
**Email subscribers**|  Indicates the number of users in a segment who have an email address. The number does not include users who have unsubscribed from email campaigns or users with a hard-bounced email address.Each unique email address is only counted once. For example, if an Android user and an iOS user have the same email address, they will be counted as one email subscriber.  
**Phone numbers**|  Indicates the number of phone numbers in a segment. This number is relevant for SMS and Kakao campaigns.Each unique phone number is only counted once. For example, if an Android user and an iOS user have the same phone number, they will be counted as one phone number.  
**LINE subscribers**|  Indicates the number of LINE users in the segment who are followers of your LINE channel. Each unique LINE UID is only counted once. Users who have unfollowed or blocked the LINE channel are not included.See [LINE Segment FAQs](doc:line-segment-faqs) for more details.  
  
* * *

## 

Filter the segment list

The list of segments displayed in the segment list can be filtered by source and tag.

![](https://files.readme.io/e7950b0-segment-list-filters.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * The source filter option **Split user** is only available for accounts with the [split user feature](doc:campaigns-getting-started-email-ip-warmup#split-users-into-multiple-segments) enabled.
>   * The tag filter is only available for accounts with the upgraded segment creation experience enabled.
> 

> 
> To enable the split user feature and upgraded segment creation experience, please contact your customer success manager.

* * *

## 

Action buttons

![](https://files.readme.io/8c765ec-segment-action-buttons.png)

  * **Edit segment** : Lets you edit the segment. When the segment is edited, the user and subscriber counts will be refreshed.
  * **Duplicate** : Lets you duplicate the segment. The duplicated segment is created above the segment on the dashboard.
  * **Sample User** : Lets you view a random sample of user profiles to verify that the segment has users. You can view the user's **GCM ID** , **User ID** , **User details** , and **Device details**.
  * **Export Reports** : Exports user data for the segment to a CSV file. For details on file formats and column definitions, see [Export Segment Reports](doc:segments-export-segment-reports).
  * **View Activity Logs** : Lets you view all activities related to the selected segment.
  * **Delete** : Lets you delete the segment if the segment is not being used by any campaigns.



* * *

## 

User count and segment trend

Click on a segment's name in the segment list page to view that segment's user count and trend chart.

  * **User count** : Displays the number of users in the segment by channel type.
  * **Segment trend** : Displays the change in the number of users in the segment overtime, based on the specified date range. You can hover over a specific date to see the segment size for that day.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> If there are missing data points within the selected date range, linear interpolation will be used to plot a line between the known data points.

![](https://files.readme.io/a8bc84d-segment-list-segment-trend.png)

# Test Segment

When creating campaigns, you can send a test creative to yourself to preview the campaign using the **Test Your Creative** button.

![](https://files.readme.io/c2a67c7de58f75a8a3a787a88d7a5972851b4da0111658036a8426a8f03b03a5-test-creatives.png)

To receive test creatives, you need to first add your devices to the **Test Segment**.

![](https://files.readme.io/0686cede7d89dfd90f52b821788d0a809ee30c1735a9a462a53cb210b6e964c0-test-segment.png)

The test segment’s purpose is to receive test campaigns, which have different settings than standard campaigns. When sending test campaigns using the **Test Your Creative** button:

  * The unsubscribed email list and user consent settings for push notifications are ignored.
  * Blackout window settings are ignored.
  * Frequency caps don't apply.



Refer to the sections below to see how to add your device to the test segment for different campaign types:

  * Web push
  * App push and in-app campaigns
  * LINE campaigns
  * Kakao and SMS campaigns
  * Email campaigns



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> For in-web campaigns, you can use the [**Preview on Website**](doc:campaigns-in-web-create#preview-on-website) feature to preview the creatives.

* * *

## 

Web push

Add your web profile to the test segment using your `userId`.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisite
> 
> Make sure your website is integrated with Appier Web SDK.

  1. Go to the website on your test device.
     * Windows desktops and Android devices: Use a Chrome or Firefox browser.
     * MacOS desktops: Use a Chrome browser.
     * iOS devices: Web push is not supported on iOS devices.
  2. In the browser's address bar, enter your website URL, and append a "_?_ " followed by a unique identifier. For example, if your website is <https://www.appier.com/en/index.html>, you can use <https://www.appier.com/en/index.html?xyz> as your unique url.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Tags entered in a URL after a ‘?’ does not affect the landing page. For example, all of the URLs listed below direct the user to the same landing page.
> 
> <https://www.appier.com/en/index.html>
> 
> <https://www.appier.com/en/index.html?abcdef>
> 
> <https://www.appier.com/en/index.html?tag=abcdef>
> 
> <https://www.appier.com/en/index.html?utm_source=ads123>

  3. Visit the unique URL at least twice. Each time, wait for the page to completely load. The AIQUA pixel will capture your test device in this step.
  4. On the AIQUA dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner, and select **Recent Activity**.
  5. Find the event with your unique URL and copy the **User ID**.

![](https://files.readme.io/9be6181-TestSegment_Web_copy.png)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> If you do not see your event, you may need to wait a few minutes or click **Refresh**. You can also enter the unique URL in the search bar to search.

  6. Go to **Audience** > **Segment List** and click the edit icon of the **Test Segment**.
  7. Under **User who match conditions** > **Include Users** , click **\+ Add New Condition**.
  8. In the new field that appears, select `userId`, select `=`, and paste the ID you previously copied.

![](https://files.readme.io/2d770b27c922cd743ebca924fecca482111496a401ea860e470320f643efcc7e-add-new-condition.png)

  9. Click **Save**.

## 

App push and in-app campaigns

### 

Android devices

Add your Android device to the test segment using the device's `advertiserId`.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
> Make sure your app is integrated with Appier Android SDK.

  1. On your Android test device, go to **Menu > Settings > Google > Ads > Advertiser ID** to find your Advertiser ID.
  2. Go to **Audience** > **Segment List** and click the edit icon of the **Test Segment**.
  3. Under **User who match conditions** > **Include Users** , click **\+ Add New Condition**.
  4. In the new field that appears, select to `advertiserId`, select `equals`, and enter the Advertiser ID.
  5. Click **Save**.

![](https://files.readme.io/e3555ae9e903b174417b9fbbdaff4c49742e4aa63be257b6fb9c77f600e3fdf6-android-add-condition.png)

### 

iOS devices

Add your iOS device to the test segment using the `userId`.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
>   * Make sure your app is integrated with Appier iOS SDK.
>   * Log a uniquely identifying attribute, like `email` or `phoneNo`, so that you can use this attribute to identify your test device later. User attributes can be logged using [these methods via iOS SDK](doc:logging-user-profile-information-for-ios-sdk).
> 


#### 

Retrieve the `userId`

  1. Launch your app and allow notifications.

![](https://files.readme.io/52d1ac1-ios_notification_prompt.png)

  2. From the AIQUA dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner and select [**Recent Users**](https://aiqua.appier.com/recent_users).
  3. After a few minutes, your profile should appear under **iOS production** or **iOS development** (select the environment you are using).
  4. Search for your device using the uniquely identifying attribute you have logged.
  5. Copy the value under **User ID** column.

![](https://files.readme.io/95b6bd7-get_userid.png)

#### 

Add the device to the test segment

  1. Go to **Audience** > **Segment list** and click the edit icon of the **Test Segment**.
  2. Under **User who match conditions** > **Include Users** , click **\+ Add New Condition**.
  3. In the new field that appears, select `userId`, select `=`, and paste the **User ID** you previously copied.

![](https://files.readme.io/c903f932719cc4db766fff6d343455d375eeb990958fcb2d539df2c12a7fb951-ios-add-condition.png)

  4. Click **Save**.



* * *

## 

LINE campaigns

Add your LINE account to the test segment using your account's `line_uid`.

You need to be able to access LINE Developers console. Your developer can grant access to you by clicking **Invite by email** in the Roles tab of the channel.

![](https://files.readme.io/896a01b-Test_LINErole.png)

  1. Log in to [LINE Developers console](https://developers.line.biz/console/), select your business under Providers and click your LINE channel.

![](https://files.readme.io/64ed63c-Test_LINE.png)

  2. Under the Basic Settings tab, scroll down to find and copy your user ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/67f0c3c-Test_LINEuser.png)

  3. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Audience** > **Segment list** and click the edit icon of the **Test Segment**.
  4. Under **User who match conditions** > **Include Users** , click **\+ Add New Condition**.
  5. In the new field that appears, select `line_uid`, select `equals`, and paste your LINE user ID.
  6. Click **Save**.



* * *

## 

Kakao and SMS campaigns

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
>   * The phone number needs to be in AIQUA's database already. You can add the phone number to AIQUA using one of these methods:
>     * [Upload User Attributes via AIQUA dashboard](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes)
>     * [Upload Offline Users via API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users)
>   * For Kakao, make sure you have opted in to your Kakao Talk Channel so that you can receive notifications.
> 


Add your phone number to the test segment using `phoneNo` as the user attribute.

  1. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Audience** > **Segment list** and click the edit icon of the **Test Segment**.
  2. Under **User who match conditions** > **Include Users** , click **\+ Add New Condition**.
  3. In the new field that appears, select `phoneNo`, select `equals`, and type your phone number with the country code (for example, 886912345678 where 886 is the country code).
  4. Click **Save**.



* * *

## 

Email campaigns

Add your email address to the test segment using `email` as the user attribute.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
> The email address needs to be in AIQUA's database already. You can add the email address to AIQUA using one of these methods:
> 
>   * [Upload User Attributes via AIQUA dashboard](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes)
>   * [Upload Offline Users via API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users)
> 


  1. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Audience** > **Segment list** and click the edit icon of the **Test Segment**.
  2. Under **User who match conditions** > **Include Users** , click **\+ Add New Condition**.
  3. In the new field that appears, select `email`, select `equals`, and then type your email address. Use lowercase letters in the email address.
  4. Click **Save**.

# Upload User Attributes

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Beta
> 
> This is a BETA feature.

The **Upload User Attributes** feature on the AIQUA dashboard allows you to add and update user attributes to AIQUA by uploading a CSV file. For example, you can upload offline user data from your CRM system or upload email lists you have collected from marketing events.

Once uploaded, AIQUA will try to match the uploaded user attributes with existing Android, iOS, and web users onboarded via SDK. If an identifier matched (based on `user_id`, `email`, or `phoneNo`), AIQUA merges the uploaded offline user with the SDK-collected online users.

This merging enriches your user data and allows you to reach previously offline users through other marketing channels such as push notifications.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> Each user record must have one of the following identifiers: `user_id`, `email`, `phoneNo`. The assigned value must be a string (text).
> 
> If more than one identifier presents in a record, only one identifier is used to match users based on the following priority:
> 
>   * First priority: `user_id`
>   * Second priority: `email`
>   * Third priority: `phoneNo`
> 

> 
> In case the identifiers of the offline user do not match with any Android, iOS, or web users, the uploaded user is stored in a common database for offline users. They can be segmented, based on their user attributes, and used only for email and SMS campaigns.
> 
> AIQUA will try to match the remaining unmatched offline users once per day since new online users will continue to be onboarded through SDK.

Here's an example of how the merging process works after an upload.

  1. The following SDK-collected user profile exists in the Android database:



phoneNo| email| city  
---|---|---  
0911222333| [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#95fffafdfbd5f0edf4f8e5f9f0bbf6faf8)| Taipei  
  
  2. Then, an CRM offline user profile is uploaded. This CRM user shares the same email address with the above Android user.



user_id| email| birthday  
---|---|---  
u2314| [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#e08a8f888ea08598818d908c85ce838f8d)| 1980-01-31  
  
  3. After a batch job, the Android and CRM user profiles are merged as an online user in the Android database into the following profile.



user_id| email| phoneNo| city| birthday  
---|---|---|---|---  
u2314| [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#eb81848385ab8e938a869b878ec5888486)| 0911222333| Taipei| 1980-01-31  
  
An uploaded user profile updates a matching SDK-collected user only once. This uploaded user profile is archived once done updating each SDK user profile.

* * *

## 

Step 1: Prepare a CSV file for your user profiles

To access this feature, go to AIQUA dashboard, select **Audience** > **Segment list** and click on the three vertical dots and select **Upload user attributes**.

![](https://files.readme.io/5fb94c7444a1674ff1f724eafd470ed20c139ca25c1561bd844dec246ac913db-upload-user-attributes.png)

On the upload user attributes page, click **Download Example CSV** to see how your CSV file must look like before uploading it to AIQUA.

![](https://files.readme.io/2cedb9fda2434c830baa0042462e276b13fe3f8776243e3121e4f44e4de10df3-download-example-csv.png)

Follow these formats and standards when creating your CSV file:

  * Include a header record. The first record is treated as a header and skipped for the import.
  * Include one of these required fields: `user_id`, `email`, `phoneNo`.
  * Use a comma (,) to separate values.
  * Each record must have the same number of comma-separated fields.
  * Fields that have a line break, double quote, or commas must be enclosed by quotes. If they're not, the file might not get processed correctly.
  * The supported encoding is UTF-8 without BOM. Do not use UTF-8 BOM or other encodings.
  * The maximum CSV file size is 100 MB.



* * *

## 

Step 2: Upload the CSV file

After preparing your CSV file, refer to the following steps to upload.

  1. Click **Upload CSV File** and choose the CSV file you'd like to upload.

![](https://files.readme.io/bafbe7d67417d9e9fd909a470082babd0971eff71a9c9713d2c7ed33370bf3a0-upload-csv-file.png)

  2. You'll see a preview of the user profiles you uploaded, as below:
     * **Column title** : This indicates the entries you included in the first row of your CSV file.
     * **Content example** : This displays all the entries you included under each column title.

![](https://files.readme.io/23ff0d1743b63fd08619dda69cabeff37258da061cd4c7222d136be7e0bab0ee-preview-upload-user-attributes.png)

  3. Under **Attributes** , assign an existing attribute for the values. The data type of this existing attribute is shown.


  * If the attribute is not an existing attribute in AIQUA, click **Create new attribute** to create a new attribute and set the **Data type** to either text or number.
  * If you do not wish to update this attribute to AIQUA, click **Skip this column**.


  4. When you're done setting up your attributes, click **Save**.



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> Submitted attributes may no longer be edited.

  5. Copy and save the tracking number displayed upon submission.

![](https://files.readme.io/81af0608c7f70e1c0e44c9c8ec317bb0a96f905d041ae8c9f1e3dc135caea0b3-track-upload-user-attributes.png)

Using an API call, you can check the status of your upload by using the tracking number shown above as the `job_id`. See details in this [guide](ref:create-an-offline-user-upload-job).

# (Optional) Receiving Key-Value Pairs

In addition to the default AIQUA campaign fields such as the title, message, and icon URL, you can send custom data to your app by including key-value pairs in your Android push campaigns.

For example, if you're using an in-house analytics tool to measure campaign performance, you can include key-value pairs in your push campaigns to pass any additional parameters required by your analytics tool.

  1. Add key-value pairs in your campaign
  2. Create an intent filter
  3. Receive key-value pairs in an activity



* * *

## 

1\. Add key-value pairs in your campaign

On the AIQUA dashboard, navigate to **Campaigns > Message campaigns**, then go to the campaign creation or settings page for the campaign you want to add key-value pairs for.

Under **Creative** > **Template** , enable **Include key-value pairs** , then add the key-value pairs you'd like to include.

* * *

## 

2\. Create an intent filter

Key-value pairs are sent via the push notification's deep link intent filter. When the notification is clicked and the redirection to the deep link occurs, the key-value pairs are passed to your app as well.

Follow the instructions in [Implementing Deep Links](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-android) to create a filter for the activity in your app that will handle these key-value pairs.

* * *

## 

3\. Receive key-value pairs in an activity

Refer to the instructions for receiving key-value pairs that correspond to the Android SDK version your app uses:

  * SDK 8.3.0 and later
  * SDK 8.2.5 and earlier



### 

SDK 8.3.0 and later

To receive key-value pairs from push campaigns when a user clicks on a push notification, register your `NotificationListener` in the `Application` class, then access key-value pairs in the `keyValuePairs` (`Map<String, Any>？`) property of the `Notification` object.

KotlinJava
    
    
    import com.appier.sdk.push.notification.Notification
    import com.appier.sdk.push.notification.NotificationListener
    class MyApplication: Application() {
        override fun onCreate() {
            Appier.initialize(this);
            Appier.setNotificationListener(
                object : NotificationListener {
                    override fun onClicked(notification: Notification) {
                        notification.keyValuePairs?.forEach { item ->
                            println("${item.key}:${item.value},")
                        }
                    }
                }
            )
        }
    }
    
    
    public class MainApplication extends Application {
        @Override
        public void onCreate() {
            super.onCreate();
            Appier.initialize(this);
    
            Appier.setNotificationListener(notification -> {
    
                Map<String, Object> keyValuePairs = notification.getKeyValuePairs();
    
                if (keyValuePairs != null) {
                    for (String key : keyValuePairs.keySet()) {
                        System.out.println("key: " + key + ", value: " + keyValuePairs.get(key));
                    }
                }
            });
        }
    }

### 

SDK 8.2.5 and earlier

Finally, implement two callbacks in your app: `onNewIntent()` and `onCreate()`. These methods will catch and process the deep link intents when a user clicks on the campaign.

#### 

`onNewIntent()`

When the activity is in the foreground, any caught intents will be sent to `onNewIntent()`.

The following example demonstrates how to implement an intent handler and retrieve the value of `myKey` from the intent in `onNewIntent()`:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    @Override
    public void onNewIntent(Intent intent) {
        super.onNewIntent(intent);
        processIntent(intent);
    }
    
    private void processIntent(Intent intent) {
        if (intent != null && intent.hasExtra("myKey")) {
            String value = intent.getStringExtra("myKey");
            // Do anything to the value
        }
    }
    
    
    override fun onNewIntent(intent: Intent) {
        super.onNewIntent(intent)
        processIntent(intent)
    }
    
    private fun processIntent(intent: Intent?) {
        intent?.apply {
            if (hasExtra("myKey")) {
                val value = intent.getStringExtra("myKey")
                // Do anything to the value
            }
        }
    }

#### 

`onCreate()`

If the activity hasn't been created, `onCreate()` will be invoked instead of `onNewIntent()`, so you'll also need to override `onCreate()` to process caught intents.

The following example demonstrates how to implement an intent handler and retrieve the value of `myKey` from the intent in `onCreate()`:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    @Override
    protected void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);
        processIntent(getIntent());
    }
    
    private void processIntent(Intent intent) {
        if (intent != null && intent.hasExtra("myKey")) {
            String value = intent.getStringExtra("myKey");
            // Do anything to the value
        }
    }
    
    
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        processIntent(intent)
    }
    
    private fun processIntent(intent: Intent?) {
        intent?.apply {
            if (hasExtra("myKey")) {
                val value = intent.getStringExtra("myKey")
                // Do anything to the value
            }
        }
    }

# (Optional) Storing Push Notifications

With Appier iOS SDK, you can store the push notifications you have sent to users, and retrieve these data later. You can use the following methods to enable notification storage, retrieve stored notifications, set the maximum limit for storage, and delete stored notifications.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * This feature is supported for iOS SDK 5.2.1 or later.
>   * The SDK will only save the notifications sent from AIQUA servers.
>   * It is required to integrate QGNotification SDK and initialize the SDK with AppGroup assigned.
> 


* * *

## 

Enabling/disabling push notification storage

By default, the SDK disables push notification storage at every launch.

  * **To enable it:** After [initializing the iOS SDK](doc:initializing-the-ios-sdk) using `[[QGSdk getSharedInstance] onStart...]`, call the method below.
  * **To disable it:** Simply remove this method.



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().enablePushNotificationStorage()
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] enablePushNotificationStorage];

* * *

## 

Retrieving stored notifications

The following code shows you how to retrieve stored notifications. You will get an array of dictionary if existed; `Nil` will be returned if there are no stored push notifications.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let list = QGSdk.getSharedInstance().fetchSavedPushNotifications()
    
    
    NSArray* list = [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] fetchSavedPushNotifications];

* * *

## 

Setting the maximum number of stored notifications

By default, the maximum number of notifications that can be stored is 20. After [initializing the iOS SDK](doc:initializing-the-ios-sdk) using `onStart`, you can call the following method to set a different limit.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().setPushNotificationStorageLimit(100)
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] setPushNotificationStorageLimit:100];

If the limit you set is smaller than the existing limit, for example changing from 100 to 80, the oldest 20 notifications will be deleted.

* * *

## 

Deleting all stored notifications

You can delete all stored push notifications:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().deleteSavedPushNotifications()
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] deleteSavedPushNotifications];

* * *

## 

Deleting a stored notification

You can delete a specific notification by index from the list returned by the SDK. For example, to delete the fourth notifications, set the index to `3`:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().deleteNotification(at: 3)
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] deleteNotificationAtIndex:3];

The SDK will ignore the call if the input index is out of bound or invalid. For example, if there are only two notifications in the example above, the SDK will ignore the call.

# (Optional) Storing Push Notifications

The Appier Android SDK allows you to enable push notification storage and provides APIs for the following operations:

  * Setting the maximum notification storage limit
  * Retrieving stored notifications
  * Deleting stored notifications



## 

Requirements and limitations

  * Your app must be using Android SDK 5.9.4 or later.
  * The Appier SDK can only store notifications sent by AIQUA.



* * *

## 

Enabling push notification storage

Push notification storage is disabled by default. To enable it, call `enablePushNotificationStorage()`.

JavaKotlin
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).enablePushNotificationStorage();
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).enablePushNotificationStorage()

* * *

## 

Setting the notification storage limit

By default, the notification storage limit is set to 20. Messages that exceed the storage limit are deleted, with the oldest messages being deleted first.

Use `setMaxNumStoredNotifications()` to change the storage limit. In the following example, the storage limit is set to 100:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).setMaxNumStoredNotifications(100);
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).setMaxNumStoredNotifications(100)

* * *

## 

Retrieving stored notifications

`getStoredNotifications()` returns a `JSONArray` of the notifications and their fields.

JavaKotlin
    
    
    JSONArray storedNotifications = QG.getInstance(context).getStoredNotifications();
    
    
    val storedNotifications: JSONArray = QG.getInstance(context).storedNotifications

Different types of notifications may include different fields. However, all of them have a `title` and a `message`. They may also have `imageUrl`, `bigImageUrl`, `deepLink` and other fields depending on the notification type. For details on image specifications, refer to the [Android push creative specifications](doc:creatives-android-push).

* * *

## 

Deleting stored notifications

### 

Deleting a single notification

You can delete a single notification by retrieving it's position in the array returned by `getStoredNotifications()` and passing it into `deleteNotificationAtIndex()`. The following example deletes the first stored notification (at position 0) in the array:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Delete the first notification locally stored by the SDK
    QG.getInstance(context).deleteNotificationAtIndex(0);
    
    
    // Delete the first notification locally stored by the SDK
    QG.getInstance(context).deleteNotificationAtIndex(0)

For example, you can use `deleteNotificationAtIndex()` to delete a notification from the app's notification history after a user reads or clicks it.

### 

Deleting all notifications

Delete all locally stored AIQUA notifications using `deleteStoredNotifications()`:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).deleteStoredNotifications();
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).deleteStoredNotifications()

# Sending Test Notifications

Follow the steps below to send a campaign from the AIQUA dashboard to see if your test device can successfully receive a push notification.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Devices running Android 13 or later
> 
> To send push notifications to devices running Android 13 or later, [your app's AndroidManifest.xml must include the `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission](doc:installing-in-android-studio#request-the-notification-permission-for-apps-targeting-api-level-33) for devices running Android 13 or later to receive push notifications.

* * *

## 

1\. Generate a user ID

  1. Open your project in Android Studio and run the app on your device. If your device is running Android 13 or later, accept the app's request to send push notifications.

  2. On the AIQUA dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner, select **Recent users** , and go to the **Android** tab. You should see a new user at the top of the user list. Under **Other fields** , `aiq_push_enabled` should be equal to **true**.

  3. Wait for **Copy GCMID** text to become visible under the **Push token (APNS token / GCM ID)** column, then copy the user ID. If **Copy GCMID** doesn't appear, continue waiting and refreshing the page until it does.




> 📘
> 
> The **Copy GCMID** text is only visible on the dashboard when AIQUA's servers receive the device's push token. Until the device's push token is received, that device can't receive AIQUA push notifications.

![](https://files.readme.io/f2aae03aaf30beb912e24392ec86f6f6cc0c01e6195b493372d520c5e09cea51-Group_33_4.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Create a segment

  1. Create a new segment. Go to **Segments > Segment list > \+ Create segment**, then select **Conditions**.

![](https://files.readme.io/c8298961839348a90434e6d6a6eeac142acc8970576bd2f9b1ada2a2a642b08d-Sending_Test_Notification_1.png)

  2. Enter a name. You'll need the name of this segment when you create the campaign.
  3. Under **Users to include** , click **\+ Add condition group** , then click **\+ Add condition** > **User attributes** , then search for "userId".

![](https://files.readme.io/3cdb27531c0221149539bfebe6be4f9ddd9bcf798a9ad4690ccb476184ee6cc8-Group_36.png)

  4. Set `userId` to the value you obtained from the `app_launched` event.

![](https://files.readme.io/907192275a2ed15c9e41555657f79275111c3effd3d108df828d5f4e7aa0060a-Sending_Test_Notification_3.png)

  5. Click **Save** to return to the **Segment list** page. The segment you just created should have a single user under **Android subscribers**.

![](https://files.readme.io/2aaa7d934e5b9dc92a2e2d23d299811544f1effa420015c6f2228a41ec83297b-Group_34.png)

* * *

## 

3\. Create an Android push campaign

  1. From the left menu, go to **Campaigns > Regular campaigns**. Click **\+ Create campaign > Push**.

![](https://files.readme.io/cf074f47901f2bd63e348024ccaeffb029b3ba82ccec3c2234f088d4bf83f787-Sending_Test_Notification_4.png)

  2. Name your campaign, then select **Android** under **Channel**. Under **Segments** , click **\+ Add segment** to add the segment you created in step 2, then click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/6c270191dbc8d077c5644e59974948464d1df63828917e1556bbdbd59e4271b8-Group_31_1.png)

  3. Under **Variant A** , fill in the fields listed below, then click **Next** :
     1. **Title** : `Hello Push`
     2. **Subtitle** : `1st Push test`
     3. **Message** : `Hello Push 👍`
     4. **Advanced Settings** : Select `Standard` creative.
        1. **Large icon URL** : `https://images.pexels.com/photos/302899/pexels-photo-302899.jpeg`
        2. **Big image URL** : `https://images.pexels.com/photos/302899/pexels-photo-302899.jpeg`

![](https://files.readme.io/2dbec919f21ee8f920878e67ea966eaa399847a456a8438127b8133623380b12-image_34_2.png)

  4. In the **[Schedule campaign](doc:campaigns-regular-create-push#schedule-campaign)** section, select one of the following options for delivering your campaign. Click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/7f9be208da1a947295b466ec17d86c217862614b0c2ea12251c5052887430c3b-Sending_Test_Notification_7.png)

  5. Finally, review and confirm your campaign settings. When you're ready to launch the campaign, click **Publish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/7712a24dfe30a3e953b0806aa34f17494fb89c394e136e249f1f72d8b93d6df5-Group_32_2.png)

* * *

## 

4\. Send the campaign

  1. Find the campaign you just created on the regular campaign list page (**Campaigns > Regular campaigns**), and click the three vertical dots next to the campaign name, then select **Send now**.

![](https://files.readme.io/af1b0312d549dfd7ecb90bd89d4f581d1aa5af3a29ad288b01e19ec3545b900b-Group_35.png)

  2. Your Android device should receive a push notification. Tap the notification to log a `notification_clicked` event.

![](https://files.readme.io/029d144-android-device-push-notification.png)

  3. In the regular campaign list page, the counts for **Impressions** and **Clicks** should have been incremented, indicating that the impression and clicks were properly tracked for the push notification you just sent.

![](https://files.readme.io/37b39cfcbf0fb38a2802f56d6ed450497110f1f7fbdf4989f8df889657351688-impression-clicks.png)

* * *

## 

Troubleshooting

If you didn't receive the push notification on your test device, ensure that the following conditions have been met:

  1. The segment contains the test device you are using.
  2. The mobile device has a stable network connection.
  3. All [required setup steps](doc:using-the-android-sdk) have been completed.
  4. If you're using a [customized implementation of `FirebaseMessagingService`](doc:push-notifications-for-android#custom-firebasemessagingservice-implementation), ensure it has been implemented correctly.



See the sections below for solutions to specific issues you may encounter while sending test push notifications.

### 

The Android Studio error logs show `"Duplicate class..."`

Check for dependency conflicts. See [Android SDK Dependencies](doc:sdk-android-dependencies) for a list of Appier SDK dependencies and solutions for common issues.

### 

The `Copy GCMID` option doesn't appear on the AIQUA dashboard after thirty minutes

Check for a `NoClassDefFoundError` in your system log and follow the steps provided in [Android SDK Dependencies](doc:sdk-android-dependencies) to resolve the error.

### 

On the **Recent users** page, the `aiq_push_enabled` setting is `false`

On your test device, go to your app's notification channel settings and ensure that all notification channels have been enabled:

![](https://files.readme.io/63f695e-android-notification-channel-settings.png)

# User Data Collection

Learn how user data is collected and used in AIQUA.

Collecting data allows you to create personalized, targeted campaigns to drive engagement and boost campaign performance.

  * Segment audiences based on attributes or previous activity.
  * Send campaigns based on user behavior, for example, visiting a product page or adding an item to the shopping cart.
  * Make campaigns personalized for each recipient using dynamic content.
  * Display recommendations tailored to individual user preferences.



Learn more about the kinds of data AIQUA uses and how to collect it in the following sections.

  * User events and attributes
  * Collecting and merging data



* * *

## 

User events and attributes

## 👤 User attributes

Details describing the user. Includes user identifiers. 

Examples

Membership level: Platinum

Email: [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)

Device type: Mobile

## 🛒 User events

Actions the user completed, such as adding an item to their shopping cart, and associated event parameters. Event data is retained for 180 days. 

Examples

Product purchased  **Parameters** • Product ID: SKU-123  
• Price: 10.00  
• Currency: USD  
• Name: Shoes A

Timestamp: Jan 1, 2026, 12:00 PM

Page viewed  **Parameters** • Page Path: /shop/shoes  
• Category: Skincare

Timestamp: Jan 1, 2026, 12:05 PM

Checkout completed  **Parameters** • Value: 3000.00  
• Currency: JPY

Timestamp: Jan 1, 2026, 12:10 PM

### 

User identifiers

AIQUA assigns the unique identifier `userId` to each user who visits your website or installs your app. Here are some common identifiers types AIQUA uses.

Identifier| Description  
---|---  
`userId`| The AIQUA unique identifier assigned to every user.  
`advertiserId`| Identifier for Advertiser for Android devices  
`IDFA`| Identifier for Advertiser for iOS devices.  
`IDFV`| Identifier for Vendor for iOS devices.  
`user_id`| The custom user ID used by your brand, for example, the member ID from your CRM.  
`phoneNo`| The user's phone number.  
`email`| The user's email address.  
  
Each `userId` it treated as a different user. For example, if Jane visits your website from her PC and also installs your app on her Android mobile device and on her iPad, she'll be tracked as three users in AIQUA, each with a different `userId`.

### 

Event parameters

User events include event parameters, which are additional details about the event.

Event

product_added_to_cart

Event parameters

product_name

product_id

product_category

product_image_url

For example, when a website visitor adds a product to their cart, you can use the Appier SDK to log a `product_added_to_cart` event. This event can contain additional parameters such as the `product_name` and `product_id` of the product.

* * *

## 

Collecting and merging data

  * Tracking online user data: Use the Appier SDK to track website and app activity.
  * Uploading offline user data: Upload your existing data to AIQUA.
  * Merging offline and online data: Merge data sources for an enriched customer view.



### 

Tracking online user data

Online user data refers to events and attributes collected from websites and app activity using the [Appier SDK](doc:sdk-getting-started). Work with your developers to integrate the Appier SDK with your website or app to begin tracking online user data. Default data collection starts immediately after integrating the SDK.

Data type| Description  
---|---  
Default user events and attributes| Data that is automatically collected after you integrate the Appier SDK with your website or app—no additional code needed. See [Default Events and Attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) for a complete list of automatically collected data.  
Custom user events and attributes| Custom fields that you define based on your specific requirements. Requires adding SDK logging code into your website or app. See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) to learn more.  
  
### 

Uploading offline user data

Offline user data refers to the data your upload to AIQUA from external sources, such as your in-store (POS) data and CRM. If your offline data contains the correct identifiers, offline data can be merged for existing online users.

  * Offline user attributes: Upload via [Bulk Upload of Offline Users API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users) or the [Upload User Attributes](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes) option on the AIQUA dashboard.
  * Offline user events: Upload via [Offline Event API v2](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2).



### 

Merging online and offline data

Merging online data with offline data enriches the customer view and creates opportunities for more effective marketing use cases.

For example, you can upload purchase data from your physical store (offline data) and merge it with an online mobile app user's profile (online data). With the merged customer view, you can now identify app users who made a recent purchase at a physical store, then send a follow-up push campaign.

## ✨ Merged customer view

Combines digital behavior, physical touchpoints, and data from external sources.

Online data

### Website & app visitors

User events and attributes tracked via SDK.

Examples

Website and mobile app activity Campaign interactions

+

Offline data

### CRM & in-store activity

Historical data uploaded via API or AIQUA dashboard.

Examples

In-store (POS) data CRM attributes External sources

Offline data is merged with online user data using the following identifiers:

  * `user_id`
  * `email`
  * `phoneNo`



If the identifiers contained in offline data don't match with any existing online users, the offline data is saved and the matching process is repeated once per day. If a new online user with a matching identifier is detected, the stored offline data will be merged for that user.

# Account Settings

Manage account-level settings and team members.

Go to **Settings > Account settings** to view your account information, such as your API token and app ID, and configure account-level settings, such as setting frequency caps and conversion events.

![](https://files.readme.io/13982d28cf74b7bd69407f21e8e05362ed7fe27700fe55f5f23636c31a937eb7-account-settings.png)

* * *

## 

General settings

### 

Time zone

Set the account's time zone. This setting affects campaign delivery times and timestamps for reports and performance data.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Analytics dashboard
> 
> Please note that changing the account's timezone may cause unexpected affects to the [analytics dashboard's](doc:analytics-pages-analytics-dashboard) performance metrics calculations. If you'd like to change your account's timezone, please contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#bbdec8c8e4c8cecbcbd4c9cffbdacbcbd2dec995d8d4d6)) for assistance.

### 

Maximum notification send rate

> 📘
> 
> The maximum notification send rate setting is only applicable for message campaigns.

Set the maximum number of notifications that can be sent per second to avoid sending too many message campaigns. You can choose a rate of 100 to 100,000 notifications per second.

### 

Set blackout window

The blackout window allows you to set a time period within which AIQUA won't send campaigns.

The blackout window is based on the actual send time instead of the campaign's scheduled run time. For example, given a campaign scheduled for 3:00 PM and a blackout window starting at 3:01 PM, if campaign delivery can't be completed before 3:01 PM, for example, due to a large audience, notifications that haven't been sent by 3:01 PM will be blocked.

Note that there are some scenarios where users may still receive notifications during the blackout window:

  * While AIQUA doesn't send notifications during a blackout window, users may still receive a notification during a blackout window due to [delayed notifications](doc:why-are-users-receiving-delayed-notifications).
  * The blackout window doesn't apply to users in the test segment when you click the [**Test Your Creative**](doc:creatives#test-creative) button.



To set up the blackout window:

  1. Toggle **Set blackout window**.
  2. Select the channels you want to enable the blackout window for.
     * **Clear push messages queued in push server (FCM or APNs) during blackout window** : If selected, queued push messages will be removed from the server once the blackout window begins. If not selected, queued messages are delivered after the device comes online again, even if it's during blackout window. Messages can be queued if a user's device is turned off or offline at the time of campaign delivery, resulting in the message being queued by the notification service provider (FCM or APNs).
  3. Set the **Start Time** (inclusive) and **End Time** (exclusive) based on the time zone setting of your account.
  4. Click **Save**.



* * *

## 

Conversion and attribution

You can select the conversion events and the attribution models for online events tracked by Appier SDK. [Default events](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) can't be selected as conversion events.

  * **Conversion events** : You can indicate the events that represent conversion for your business, such as `product_purchased`.
  * **Attribution models** : Attribution models determine whether an event is attributed to a campaign. The attribution models selected here affect the conversion count and conversion value shown in the campaign list.



For details on conversion events and attribution models, see [Understanding Event Attribution](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution).

* * *

## 

Offline conversion and attribution

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * This feature needs to be activated by Appier Support.
>   * To see the channels that support offline conversion attribution, see [Attribution models by channels](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution#/attribution-models-by-channel).
>   * Offline conversion events need to be uploaded via [Offline Event API v2](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/getting-starting-with-the-offline-event-api-v2).
>   * AIQUA calculates the offline conversion count daily using offline events with a timestamp within 90 days.
> 


If you've enabled offline event attribution, you can select the attribution model and attribution window for offline events.

  * **Conversion events** : You can select up to five offline conversion events. Note that changes to offline conversion events aren't applied retroactively to previously uploaded event data.

  * **Offline attribution models** : For a conversion event to be attributed to a campaign, the user needs to complete the event within a certain time period after viewing or clicking the campaign.

    * **Conversion attribution** : The different models determine whether the attribution is based on campaign clicks or views, and whether the attribution is only counted for the last campaign. For more details, see [Understanding Attribution Models](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution#understanding-attribution-models).
    * **Attribution window** : You can set an attribution window between 1 to 30 days. For an offline conversion event to be attributed to a campaign, the timestamp of the uploaded event must be within this window after the user clicks or views the campaign. Changes to the attribution window aren’t applied retroactively to previously uploaded data. For more details, see [Setting Attribution Window](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution-setting-attribution#/setting-the-attribution-window).



* * *

## 

Notification frequency cap

AIQUA provides two types of frequency caps to help you limit the number of notifications sent to users.

  * Daily limit
  * Minimum interval



Please note that:

  * For regular message campaigns, both frequency caps can be overridden by enabling the **Bypass frequency cap** in the campaign settings.
  * The frequency cap doesn't apply to users in the test segment when you click the [**Test Your Creative**](doc:creatives#test-creative) button. Notifications sent via the **Test Your Creative** button do not count toward the frequency cap.
  * Notifications that are blocked, for example, due to a blackout window, may sometimes still count toward the frequency cap. As a result, users may receive fewer notifications than the limit set by frequency cap settings.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Push notifications: Device types
> 
> For push notifications, the frequency cap is counted separately for Android, iOS, and web devices. The definition of each device is as follows:
> 
>   * Web push: Each web browser is counted as one device. For example, if a person is subscribed to your web push from the Chrome browser on their laptop, the Firefox browser on their laptop, and their Android device's Chrome browser, this is counted as three separate devices. If the browser cookie is cleared, this web browser is treated as a new device.
>   * Android push: An Android device that has your Android app installed.
>   * iOS push: An iOS device that has your iOS app installed.
> 


### 

Daily limit

Set the maximum number of push notifications that can be sent to a device per day, regardless of the campaign type.

  * Push notifications sent from message campaigns and API calls are all limited by this frequency cap.
  * The notification count of each device is reset to 0 at midnight (00:00) based on your account's time zone.



To set the daily limit:

  1. Check **Enable notification limits**.
  2. Enter the maximum number of push notifications that can be sent to each device each day.
  3. Click **Save**.



After updating the daily limit, campaigns that are already running will still use the previous setting. The new limit will be applied to campaigns which start running after saving the new setting.

### 

Minimum interval

Set a minimum time interval in seconds between two notifications for each channel for your message campaigns. For example, if the minimum interval for **Email** message campaigns is set to `100`, then users who receive an email campaign won't receive another one for at least 100 seconds.

Note that changes to the minimum interval only apply after the previous interval expires. For example, if a user receives an SMS campaign when the minimum interval was 600 seconds, and then the minimum interval is updated, the new settings won't apply until the original 600-second interval elapses.

#### 

Minimum-interval Message campaigns

For regular message campaigns, the interval is counted separately for each channel.

For trigger message campaigns, the interval is counted separately for each type of trigger rule, meaning a user can receive up to three notifications from that channel during the interval, one from each trigger rule type: user action, relative date, and feed change.

In summary, the minimum interval is counted separately for each campaign type listed below.

Campaign type| Interval is counted separately for each listed campaign type  
---|---  
Message campaign: Regular| 

  * Web push
  * Android push
  * iOS push
  * SMS
  * MMS
  * Email
  * LINE
  * Kakao

  
Message campaign: Trigger| 

  * Web push (Trigger: User action)
  * Web push (Trigger: Relative date)
  * Web push (Trigger: Feed change)
  * Android push (Trigger: User action)
  * Android push (Trigger: Relative date)
  * Android push (Trigger: Feed change)
  * iOS push (Trigger: User action)

### 

Bypassing the frequency cap

You can override the account setting's frequency cap settings (both the minimum interval and daily limit) for regular message campaigns by selecting **Bypass frequency cap** in the campaign settings. In addition, notifications sent from this campaign still increase the device's notification count for both types of frequency caps.

## 

Email list-unsubscribe header

  * **Use Appier 's default unsubscribe URL**: By default, email campaigns use Appier's default unsubscribe URL. Select this option if you don't need to maintain your own list of unsubscribed users.
  * **Use a custom URL**: Specify a custom URL, which can include dynamic content variables (user attributes or events). A POST request is made to your custom URL whenever a user clicks the one-click unsubscribe link at the top of the email (list-unsubscribe header). Note that using a custom URL requires additional implementation steps.

![Unsubscription link at the top of the email \(list-unsubscribe header\)](https://files.readme.io/d15f7fb-one-click-unsubscribe.png)

Unsubscription link at the top of the email (list-unsubscribe header)

### 

Use Appier's default unsubscribe URL

When a user clicks unsubscribe from an email campaign:

  * That user's `email_unsubscribe` attribute is set to `true`, and their email address is excluded from the **Email subscribers** count shown in the [segment list](doc:segments-segment-list#user-and-subscriber-count).
  * That user's email address is added to AIQUA's unsubscribed user email list. Email campaigns will no longer be sent to users on this list.



### 

Use a custom URL

When a user unsubscribes from email campaigns by clicking the one-click unsubscribe button at the top of the email, a POST request is made to your custom unsubscribe URL. Custom unsubscribe URLs can contain dynamic content such as user identifiers.

#### 

Required steps for custom unsubscribe URLs

If you choose to use a custom URL to unsubscribe from email campaigns, you'll need to complete additional steps to ensure the unsubscription is processed correctly:

  1. Implement a handler in your system to receive the unsubscribe POST request and process the user's unsubscription. The POST request will be sent to the custom URL configured in your account settings. The request looks like this:



Email unsubscribe request
    
    
    "POST /unsubscribe/custom/url HTTP/1.1
    Host: example.com
    Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
    Content-Length: 26
    List-Unsubscribe=One-Click"

  2. Use the [email subscription API](ref:add-emails-to-unsubscribed-email-list) to add the email to the unsubscribed email list. Until this step is completed, AIQUA email campaigns will continue to be sent to the user.



#### 

Dynamic content in custom unsubscribe URLs

Dynamically insert user attributes or events into your custom URL by clicking **{...}** and selecting the attribute or event you'd like to use.

![](https://files.readme.io/c28b5f9cee5945c06f036f9c4136b58765827e9da5715ce3c078f2742a6d4492-email-list-unsubscriber-header-dynamic-content.png)

## 

Default UTM parameters

Set account-level UTM parameters to pre-fill UTM parameter fields for new email campaigns when [UTM tracking is enabled](doc:creatives-email#enable-utm-tracking), ensuring consistent performance measurement in tools like Google Analytics.

To define your account-level default settings, toggle on **Set default UTM parameters**.

![](https://files.readme.io/032ceb99450c43ad7633848ecb5f58233dd9640606f6b91caccf4c4eb9cfdf37-account-settings-default-utm-parameters.png)

Parameter| Required| Description  
---|---|---  
**Campaign source**|  Yes| The `utm_source` parameter, which identifies the referrer that sent the traffic, such as `appier`.  
**Campaign medium**|  Yes| The `utm_medium` parameter, which identifies the marketing medium used, such as `email`.  
**Campaign name**|  No| The `utm_campaign` parameter, which identifies the specific promotion. Click the `{...}` icon to insert dynamic variables like **Campaign name** or **Campaign type**.  
**Campaign term**|  No| The `utm_term` parameter, which identifies paid keywords associated with the campaign. This field remains empty by default.  
**Campaign content**|  No| The `utm_content` parameter, which differentiates links or creatives within an email. This field remains empty by default.  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes
> 
> Campaign-specific UTM parameters can be modified by [enabling campaign UTM tracking](doc:creatives-email#enable-utm-tracking) in individual campaign settings.

### 

UTM tracking behavior

Note the following behaviors when configuring UTM fields:

  * Spaces in UTM parameter fields are automatically converted to underscores (`_`).
  * All parameters are percent-encoded using UTF-8 for compatibility with industry-standard browsers and analytics tools.
  * Each UTM field has a 200-character limit based on the percent-encoded result. If your input exceeds this limit, the parameter value is trimmed.
  * Account-level defaults apply automatically to new campaigns. Existing campaigns aren't affected. To apply UTM tracking to an existing campaign, manually enable the toggle in its [creative settings](doc:creatives-email#enable-utm-tracking).

## 

Managing users

There are four account roles with varying permissions. To see detailed permissions for each role, including accessible pages and functions, see Permissions.

Role| Permissions  
---|---  
**Administrator**|  Access to all features and user data, including personally identifiable information (PII), such as emails collected in lead generation forms.  
**Developer**|  Can create and execute campaigns. They can access **Recent users** and **Recent activity** pages to verify integration.Note that users with the **Developer** role can see PII in the **Recent users** and **Recent activity** pages. To mask PII in these pages, contact [Appier Support](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#294c5a5a765a5c5959465b5d69485959404c5b074a4644) and indicate the fields you want to mask, such as `email`, `phoneNo`, `line_uid`, `IDFA`, `IDFV`, `advertiserId`, and `ip`.  
**Operator**|  Can create and execute campaigns, but cannot access user data or any reports that include user data.  
**Viewer**|  Can only edit campaigns and view the campaign performance pages.  
  
### 

Adding users

  1. Under **Team** , click **\+ Invite user**.
  2. Enter up to 10 email addresses, select a role to assign to these users, and click **Invite**.

![](https://files.readme.io/8e791b1587ce07d853c978cd1264a01044fe441a90418f26ddff1eb8f7d431ab-invite-user.png)

### 

Editing roles and removing users

To edit the role or delete an existing user, click the three vertical dots next to the user's email and select **Edit role** or **Remove**.

![](https://files.readme.io/34317d34cb30e2e40d0a666554d6d02c62e4a3f0293fba2949c9d1d731c6055d-edit-remove-user.png)
